Content:
Wayanad. A severe landslide in Kerala's Wayanad district has once again shaken the area. The death toll in this accident has risen to five, while 7 people are still reported missing. Relief and rescue operations are continuously underway, and teams from various agencies are engaged in searching for people buried under the debris. Ten people injured in the accident are undergoing treatment in different hospitals.

Due to the landslide, a church and a house located nearby were completely swept away. However, the relief was that the residents of the house had gone on a pilgrimage to Mecca, and no one was present inside the church at the time of the incident. A crucial bridge connecting the affected area was also buried under the debris after the accident, posing a serious challenge to rescue operations. Two excavators are continuously working to remove debris and clear a path for rescue teams. Police, National Disaster Response Force, State Disaster Response Force, and Civil Defense volunteers have been deployed at the site. Congress leader and Wayanad MP Priyanka Gandhi expressed deep sorrow over this tragedy and extended heartfelt condolences to the families of the deceased. She said, 'Our prayers and hopes are with those whom rescue teams are still trying to reach; may they remain strong and their loved ones find the courage to bear this painful moment.' She also appealed to UDF workers, party officials, and the general public to cooperate in relief efforts by following the instructions of the district administration. Wada said that every possible effort is being made to rescue the trapped people, and the state administration is working in coordination. Also, NDRF teams are using sniffer dogs (detection dogs) to assist in search and rescue efforts after the Wayanad landslide.

New Delhi/ Jakarta. India and Indonesia signed agreements in 20 sectors including defense, critical minerals, maritime security, healthcare, agriculture, space, digital technology, education, and cultural diplomacy in Jakarta on Tuesday.

The most significant was the BrahMos deal. Discussions between the two countries regarding this had been ongoing for the past four months. This agreement will be worth 200 million dollars. India will provide additional units of BrahMos missiles to Indonesia. With this, Indonesia has become the third country to buy BrahMos after the Philippines and Vietnam. Indonesia has also decided to purchase Indian 'Astra' air-to-air missiles used in Operation Sindoor. Meanwhile, India will also help Indonesia develop Electronic Voting Machines (EVMs). India's UPI will soon be linked to Indonesia's payment system.

This will make doing business and traveling between the two countries easier. These agreements were made during a bilateral meeting between Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Indonesian President Prabowo Subianto. These agreements demonstrate a commitment to strengthening strategic unity and cooperation in security, economic, and technological sectors among the major democracies in the Indo-Pacific region. It is worth noting that Prime Minister Modi will visit Prambanan, Indonesia's largest Hindu temple, on Wednesday during his three-day tour.

Heading: On table: Two BrahMos missile batteries worth $200 million
Summary: India is significantly expanding its defence exports, with a $200 million deal in its final stages to supply Indonesia with two BrahMos supersonic cruise missile batteries, alongside other landmark agreements encompassing Astra air-to-air missile systems, major defence technology transfer, and maritime security cooperation. The BrahMos missile, already operational across all Indian defence services and notably used in striking targets in Pakistan during Operation Sindoor, is also being exported to countries like the Philippines, which procured three batteries in 2022, and Vietnam, with whom a deal has been signed. BrahMos Aerospace is actively developing a next-generation version for export to at least 10 more countries and is working to extend the missile's range for both land and ship attacks, with talks ongoing with several other nations for the export of the system, typically including four launchers and 12 missiles.
Content: INDIA IS set to supply Indonesia with two batteries of BrahMos supersonic cruise missiles valued at $200 million as part of several landmark defence agreements signed between the two countries on Tuesday, including Astra air-to-air missile systems, major defence technology transfer, and maritime security cooperation, officials told The Indian Express. The BrahMos missile has been operationalised in India across all the three defence services and played a key role in striking designated targets inside Pakistan during Operation Sindoor. A BrahMos battery typically comprises four launchers and 12 ready-to-fire missiles, along with other equipment and vehicles, though the composition can vary between land-based regiments and coastal defence batteries. With this deal, India is set to export the system to three countries, also including the Philippines and Vietnam, even as it holds talks with at least half-a-dozen other nations on the missile system. The Philippines had procured three batteries of the weapon system from India in 2022. In May this year, Defence Secretary Rajesh Kumar Singh officially confirmed at the Shangri-La Dialogue in Singapore that India had signed a deal with Vietnam for the sale of BrahMos missiles, and that a similar deal with Indonesia was in “final stages”. New Delhi has been in talks with Jakarta over the sale of the missile system under a joint venture between the Defence Research and Development Organisation (DRDO) and Russia’s NPO Mashinostroyeniya. The Indian Express had earlier reported that the finer details of the deal were discussed during the third India-Indonesia defence ministers’ dialogue, co-chaired by Defence Minister Rajnath Singh and his Indonesian counterpart Sjaffrie Sjamsoddin in New Delhi last November. BrahMos Aerospace Private Ltd is also looking to export a compact next-gen version, BrahMos NG, to at least 10 countries, including South Africa and West Asian nations such as Saudi Arabia, the UAE, and Egypt. Work is also underway to extend the range of existing BrahMos missiles from 290 km to 500 km for land attacks, and to 400 km for ship attacks.

Heading: PM MEETS INDONESIA PRESIDENT, ADDRESSES PARLIAMENT Missiles, minerals and port: Delhi, Jakarta seal key deals
Summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi's visit to Jakarta significantly strengthened the India-Indonesia Comprehensive Strategic Partnership, marked by his meeting with Indonesian President Prabowo Subianto and the signing of several key agreements. These pacts cover enhanced cooperation in defense, critical minerals, maritime security, space, agriculture, blue economy, education, and cultural heritage, including the conservation of the Prambanan Temple. A major highlight was India's commitment to supply Indonesia with two BrahMos missile batteries worth $200 million and other defense technology transfers, underscoring India's active role as a defense exporter, having already supplied the system to the Philippines and finalized a deal with Vietnam, with Indonesia's deal in its final stages. India is also in talks with other nations for the BrahMos system and plans to export a next-generation version (BrahMos NG) to at least 10 countries, alongside efforts to extend the range of existing missiles. During his visit, PM Modi addressed the Indonesian Parliament, emphasizing India's commitment to development and a free, open, and inclusive Indo-Pacific, and later addressed the Indian diaspora, highlighting India's rapid growth, self-reliance, and its role as a global economic driver, moving forward with the mantra of "reform, perform and transform." President Subianto expressed profound admiration for PM Modi and India's democratic values, acknowledging the shared civilizational heritage between the two nations. The visit culminated with PM Modi being awarded Indonesia's highest civilian honor, further cementing the deepening bilateral ties and shared regional and global outlooks.
Content:
Prime Minister Narendra Modi met Indonesian President Prabowo Subianto in Jakarta on Tuesday, where India and Indonesia signed landmark pacts on the supply of BrahMos and Air-to-Air missiles, along with cooperation on critical minerals and rare earths, maritime security, space, and agriculture. Officials told The Indian Express that India is set to supply Indonesia with two batteries of BrahMos supersonic cruise missiles valued at $200 million, as part of these defence agreements which also include Astra air-to-air missile systems and major defence technology transfer. The BrahMos missile is operational across all three Indian defence services and played a key role in striking designated targets inside Pakistan during Operation Sindoor.

A BrahMos battery typically comprises four launchers and 12 ready-to-fire missiles, along with other equipment and vehicles, though the composition can vary between land-based regiments and coastal defence batteries. With this deal, India is set to export the system to three countries, also including the Philippines and Vietnam, even as it holds talks with at least half-a-dozen other nations on the missile system. The Philippines had procured three batteries of the weapon system from India in 2022. In May this year, Defence Secretary Rajesh Kumar Singh officially confirmed at the Shangri-La Dialogue in Singapore that India had signed a deal with Vietnam for the sale of BrahMos missiles, and that a similar deal with Indonesia was in “final stages”. New Delhi has been in talks with Jakarta over the sale of the missile system under a joint venture between the Defence Research and Development Organisation (DRDO) and Russia’s NPO Mashinostroyeniya. The Indian Express had reported that the finer details of the deal were discussed during the third India-Indonesia defence ministers’ dialogue, co-chaired by Defence Minister Rajnath Singh and his Indonesian counterpart Sjaffrie Sjamsoeddin in New Delhi last November. Brahmos Aerospace Private Ltd is also looking to export a compact next-gen version, BrahMos NG, to at least 10 countries, including South Africa and West Asian nations such as Saudi Arabia, the UAE, and Egypt. Work is also under way to extend the range of existing BrahMos missiles from 290 km to 500 km for land attacks, and to 400 km for ship attacks.

Modi also addressed the Indonesian Parliament as part of his two-day visit, making a thinly veiled reference to China's assertive behaviour in the Indo-Pacific. He stated, “India is a strong advocate of a free, open and inclusive Indo-Pacific. India believes in freedom of navigation in the Indo-Pacific... India is a nation that follows the path of development, not expansionism.” Modi said, "In recent years, the relationship between India and Indonesia has acquired renewed energy, greater confidence, and deeper strategic depth. Our Comprehensive Strategic Partnership, established in 2018, is reaching new heights today. We are making significant strides across every domain of cooperation, including development, security, technology, culture, and education. I am confident that today marks the beginning of a golden new chapter in the India-Indonesia partnership." The Indonesian President also awarded PM Modi the Bintang Adipurna of the Republic of Indonesia "Medal of Honour", the country's highest civilian honour for individuals who have rendered exceptional service to its unity, continuity and prosperity. Modi, who is on a three-nation trip from July 6 to 11 during which he will also visit Australia and New Zealand, said, "The growing trust between our two countries is strengthening our cooperation in defence, security, and the maritime domain. Today, we agreed to further enhance collaboration in defence exchanges, disaster management, and industrial cooperation." According to a joint statement issued by both countries, both leaders "agreed to further strengthen cooperation and enhance engagements in both traditional and emerging areas of defence cooperation". It said that "they welcomed the elevation of defence cooperation, including through cooperation on BrahMos Missile System, and the Air-to-Air Missile Cooperation Agreement". The statement quoted Modi as saying that the Coast Guards of the two countries "will now work together to enhance maritime safety and security in the Indian Ocean". "As two close maritime nations, we have also decided to deepen our cooperation in the blue economy, port development, and maritime trade," Modi said. According to the joint statement, President Prabowo "welcomed India's interest in partnering on the integrated development of the Sabang Port". "Both leaders recognised that such a partnership -- spanning cruise and marine-tourism facilities, maritime industries (ship-repair and shipbuilding), and shore-based services supporting offshore energy activities in the Andaman Sea -- would foster institutional, physical, digital and flow of people and commodities between Andaman and Nicobar Islands of India and Provinces in Sumatra Island, that contribute to generating investment, employment, transfer of technology and shared regional prosperity," the statement said. Sabang port is located at the northwestern entrance to the Strait of Malacca, a critical global maritime corridor through which roughly 25 to 40 per cent of global seaborne trade passes. It lies just 160 kilometres, or less than 100 nautical miles, from India's upcoming trans-shipment hub at Great Nicobar. As the two sides signed pacts on rare earth and critical minerals, Modi said, "We have also concluded an important agreement to strengthen supply chain resilience in the areas of critical minerals and steel. In addition, our companies are embarking on a new phase of partnership in stainless steel and rare earth magnets." Indonesia dominates the global critical minerals sector, commanding roughly 21% of the world's nickel reserves and ranking among the top global producers of copper, bauxite, and tin. The other pacts signed between the two sides included the opening of an IIM Bangalore campus in Indonesia, supply of medicines and medical products to Indonesia, telecom technology including wireless and quantum systems, and conservation and restoration of the Prambanan temple complex in Yogyakarta, among others. "Tomorrow, I will have the privilege of joining President Prabowo in Yogyakarta to launch the conservation project for the Prambanan Temple. More than 1,000 years old, the Prambanan Temple stands as a timeless symbol of the shared cultural heritage of India and Indonesia," Modi said. On global issues, Modi said that there "is strong synergy in our respective outlooks on the Indo-Pacific" and that "India has always attached special importance to ASEAN centrality". "In this period of global turbulence, India believes that the role of dialogue and diplomacy has become more important than ever before. On the issue of Palestine, we continue to support a Two-State Solution and the pursuit of lasting peace," he said. On Monday, as Modi landed in Jakarta, he was received at the airport by President Prabowo and four ministers, including the Foreign Minister, Minister of Palace Affairs and Cabinet Secretary. This is the Prime Minister's fourth visit to Indonesia and his first bilateral visit since ties were elevated to a Comprehensive Strategic Partnership in May 2018.

Later, speaking at a diaspora event in Jakarta, also attended by President Prabowo Subianto, Prime Minister Modi summed up India's growth, saying, "1.4 billion aspirations in motion." He underlined that India is moving forward with the mantra of "reform, perform and transform," and that self-reliance is a multiplying force not only for Indonesia but for the entire ASEAN region. "India has carried out one reform after another. We have consistently performed, and that's why the country is transforming today," Modi said, adding that India is not just the world's fastest-growing economy but a nation with a billion-plus dreams in motion, playing a major role in driving global growth. He highlighted India's progress "from energy to connectivity and chip manufacturing," asserting that "India is unstoppable. Today's India is not just fulfilling its own dreams but also fulfilling those of every friendly nation. India walks on the mantra of 'sabka saath, sabka vikas'." Modi further emphasized, "As India is modernising its ports, building new ships and exploring new sea routes to strengthen its maritime sector, Indonesia stands as our favourite friend... Whether in Indonesia or India, our shared goal is development. We cannot afford to wait or stop."

Addressing the gathering ahead of Modi, President Prabowo said Indonesia draws inspiration from Indian democracy. He openly admitted his great admiration for PM Modi, stating, "I don't want to be involved in domestic Indian politics. I'm a friend of all Indians but I want to admit one thing and my close associates and colleagues will testify that I am a great admirer of Narendra Modi ji." Prabowo, who described himself as not a professional politician, shared that he had studied Modi's policies even before becoming President and had "copied many of his policies" with Modi's gracious permission, joking that he "cannot be sued in any court." Prabowo, who was the chief guest at the Republic Day celebrations in 2025, also highlighted his "Indian DNA," sharing how gene testing confirmed it just before he visited India. He added, "Whenever I hear Indian music, I find my body moving... my ministers and generals all like to dance and sing. Maybe most of them have Indian DNA also... It's true. Most of my ministers sing Indian songs really well." Responding to this, Modi said, "Your statement has touched the hearts of Indians. And this DNA is made of mutual trust, shared heritage, shared memories. The relationship between India and Indonesia is rooted in our shared civilisational heritage and the seas that connect us."

Heading: Even Caesar did not send a lie to the Senate
Summary: The article discusses the importance of truth and accountability of ministers in Parliament, especially in light of privilege proceedings against Defence Minister Rajnath Singh for allegedly misleading Parliament over 'Operation Sindoor'. It emphasizes that deliberately misleading Parliament constitutes a breach of privilege and undermines democratic trust, drawing parallels with historical and international parliamentary conventions. The author concludes with confidence that the Ministry of Defence will present full and accurate facts, upholding the integrity of the Defence Minister and parliamentary traditions.
Content: The ensuing Monsoon Session of Parliament is bound to be turbulent, as the Congress seeks privilege proceedings against Defence Minister Rajnath Singh, alleging that he misled Parliament over Operation Sindoor about the six soldiers who laid their lives in the line of duty. The Speaker, Lok Sabha may seek the comments of the Minister or refer it to the Committee on Privileges for enquiry and report. The Speaker has the inherent power to close a matter if satisfied with the explanation tendered. The veracity or otherwise of the allegation will be ascertained after due procedural enquiry. However, the central question is what consequences would visit if a minister deliberately misleads the Parliament. The veracity of statements made in the legislature by the members, including ministers, is a fundamental postulate of a deliberative democracy. Ordinarily, it is presumed that the answers given in Parliament by ministers are sacrosanct, unless proved otherwise. Parliament can function efficiently and effectively as the supreme deliberative body of the nation, if accurate and complete information is furnished to it. The Council of Ministers is accountable to the Parliament and the information that they give to Parliament must be correct and complete, without which the doctrine of accountability would become a myth. Accountability of the executive to the legislature is the linchpin of our parliamentary democracy and therefore, it is incumbent upon the ministers to furnish correct and complete and timely information to Parliament and its Committees. Truth, honesty and integrity are quite integral to the proper and effective function of the Parliament. Not only the ministers and the members, even the witnesses deposing before parliamentary committees are deemed to be under oath to speak truth, and it is invariably made known to the witnesses that the deposition which they shall make, shall be true, that nothing will be concealed and that, no part of their testimony shall be false. Suppression of truth, giving convoluted answers or to mislead Parliament or its committees constitutes breach of privilege. Therefore, greater responsibility is cast on a minister sworn to bear true faith and allegiance to the Constitution and to discharge his duties faithfully and conscientiously as a Minister for the Union. An inaccuracy or chance mistake may inadvertently creep in the statements made or replies given by a Minister in Parliament. The Rules of Procedure and Directions of Parliament provide that in case any inaccuracy or mistake is detected in any answer given or statement made by a Minister, the same shall be pointed out as soon as it is detected and the mistake rectified with the permission of the Speaker. There are many instances of the Ministers making the correcting statements, especially of the answers given to questions. But making a misleading statement deliberately or concealing information from Parliament, constitutes breach of privilege, unless the Minister invokes the plea of national interest. But making a false or deliberately misleading statement is grossly unethical, against sacrosanct parliamentary conventions and unpardonable. Untruthful or misleading statements undermine parliamentary democracy. 'Satyae Meva Jayatae' and 'Yato dharma tato Jaya' are the foremost ideals of India's great civilisational heritage. Many consider India as the Mother of Democracy, and with reference to Vedic texts and post Vedic literature. The Indian civilisational texts of great antiquity lay immense stress on truth and righteousness. There are inscriptions in the old Parliament Building taken from the Mahabharata and the Manusmriti reminding that members of the Assembly must speak with righteousness, and the righteousness must be based on truth, and truth is not truth, if it leads to deceit. Further, one must not enter either an assembly hall, or he must speak with all the righteousness, for one who does not speak or one who speaks falsely, involve equally. Even in the republics of Ancient Greece and Rome, truth was considered as the cornerstone of the rule of law, justice and public trust. Honest speeches were viewed as necessity of informed decision making. In the eponymous play of Shakespeare, when the wife of Julius Caesar beseeches and entreats him not to attend the Senate as she fears for his safety and asks him to send a message to the Senate that 'he is sick', Caesar questions, 'Shall Caesar send a lie?' to the Senate. He declines to say that he 'cannot come today' to the Senate' as that would be false, and prefers to say 'I will not come today'. Eventually, instead of sending a lie, he prefers to go to the Senate. There is no Indian instance of a Minister resigning on the ground of misleading the Parliament, though many ministers have resigned earlier on ground of corruption. In the United Kingdom, there are many instances where ministers resigned once it was so established. In the British parliamentarians use the term 'mislead' instead of 'lied', because the charge as it requires to meet more rigorous test. In the year 2023, Boris Johnson resigned as an MP after learning he faced sanctions. Earlier, he had resigned as PM in 2022 after wide public pressure. The Privilege Committee of the House of Commons had found that he had deliberately misled Parliament over statements related to Party gate. In 2018, the Home Secretary resigned, admitting that she unintentionally misled the House over immigration removal targets. Yet another historical example is of John Profumo, Secretary of State for War who resigned from Govt. and Parliament in 1963 as he had misled first denying that he had scandalous relations with someone but later admitted that his statement was untrue. These instances show that the convention of resignation for misleading the Parliament deliberately is political as well as procedural. The resignations were forced by sensitivity to public pressure, pressure from within the party and the outcry by the media. However, it has become an entrenched and salutary parliamentary convention in UK that if a minister deliberately misleads the Parliament, he will lose his ministry as well as his membership of Parliament. There is no doubt that the Ministry of Defence will place the full and accurate facts before the Parliament to remove all the misgivings as it is inconceivable that the Hon'ble Defence Minister, a veteran Parliamentarian of long standing, of fair image and deeply immersed in parliamentary and constitutional conventions, would think even remotely to mislead the Parliament, undermining the supreme sacrifice of our gallant soldiers. Let the facts speak for themselves once the matter comes on the floor of the House. The author is ex Additional Secretary, Lok Sabha & a member of the Supreme Court Bar Association.

Heading: After Op Sindoor, trust in ‘made-in-India’ defence platforms got enhanced: Rajnath
Summary: Defence Minister Rajnath Singh stated that trust in 'made-in-India' defence platforms has significantly increased following Operation Sindoor, a decisive military action. He highlighted a substantial rise in defence production to over Rs 1.78 lakh crore and record defence exports exceeding Rs 38,000 crore. Singh also emphasized India's progress towards self-reliance and a 'Viksit Bharat' over the past 12 years, speaking at an event in Delhi marking 80 years of Navbharat Times.
Content: NEW DELHI: Defence Minister Rajnath Singh on Saturday said that after Operation Sindoor, the trust in “made-in-India” defence platforms has received a boost. In his address at an event here, he also reiterated that “today, our defence production has reached over Rs 1.78 lakh crore, and about 8-9 years ago, it stood at approximately Rs 46,000 crore”. The Union minister asserted that after Operation Sindoor, “trust in made-in-India defence platforms has got enhanced”. Operation Sindoor was India’s decisive military action conducted in May 2025 in response to the Pahalgam terror attack. Several defence platforms built in India had played a key role in it. Singh said, “Defence exports too have reached a record over Rs 38,000 crore, and in 2013-14, it stood at just Rs 686 crore, and it has grown today 57 times. And, I have not sought the full report, but, currently it should be hovering around Rs 40,000 crore, is my estimate.” In his address, he also spoke of India’s journey in various sectors in the last 12 years, the advancement of artificial intelligence (AI) and the importance of human sensitivity in the age of AI, including in the field of journalism. The event was hosted in Delhi to mark 80 years of the national Hindi daily Navbharat Times. “India’s journey over the last 12 years has been a progression from shortages to self-reliance, from self-confidence and from self-confidence towards building a Viksit Bharat,” Singh said.

Heading: Rebellion in PoK... 48-hour ultimatum to Pakistan government
Summary: Rebellion has intensified in Pakistan-occupied Kashmir (PoK) following police action that resulted in a death and injuries, leading to a 48-hour ultimatum from the Joint Awami Action Committee (JAC) to the Pakistan government. PoK leaders have appealed to India for easier movement across the LoC, citing disrupted daily life due to police blockades and protests. Meanwhile, the ruling Pakistan Peoples Party (PPP) has called for postponing upcoming elections until a 'refugee seat' dispute is resolved, while Pakistani intelligence claims India's 'Sindoor 2.0' operation is behind the unrest.
Content: Rebellion in PoK (Pakistan-occupied Kashmir) has intensified. On Sunday, after the death of a protester and injuries to several people in police action, the movement became more aggressive on Monday. Clashes occurred at several places between police and protesters. In Dadyal, during a lathi-charge, both sides came face-to-face, in which some policemen were also injured along with protesters. Three of them are admitted to ICU. The Jammu and Kashmir Joint Awami Action Committee (JAC) has given a 48-hour ultimatum to the Pakistan government after army firing and arrests. The JAC demands that the ban imposed on it be lifted and its workers be released. It has also warned that if the demands are not met, they will march towards Muzaffarabad on July 9. **PoK leaders appeal to India for help** PoK leader Sardar Aman Kashmiri has appealed to India to ease movement across the LoC. He said that people in Rawalakot should also get an opportunity to live a normal life. He states that the lives of common people are affected by the current situation. **Police blockade, essential goods not reaching** Both sides are at loggerheads over the supply of food items. The JAC alleges that due to the police blockade, essential goods are not reaching the people, while the Pakistan government says that the protesters are obstructing traffic. Local people say that normal life in the valley has been affected for the last nearly 30 days. **Dispute over 'refugee seats', demand to postpone elections** Amidst the general elections to be held in PoK after three weeks, the ruling Pakistan Peoples Party (PPP) has demanded to postpone the elections until the 'refugee seat' dispute is resolved. The party has also advocated for talks with the JAC. On the other hand, the Pakistan government says that talks will only happen when the protest ends, while the JAC is firm on its demands. **Pakistani intelligence agency in fear, deployment of senior officials** An official associated with Islamabad's intelligence network claimed that India's 'Sindoor 2.0' operation is behind the current situation in PoK. The official said, 'Our most experienced officers are handling the situation there. They have dealt with similar situations in Balochistan, and they will deal with it here too.' However, the official did not provide any proof.

Summary: The Tehreek-e-Taliban Pakistan (TTP) has claimed responsibility for the killing of Pakistan Air Force Group Captain Asim Tariq in Islamabad, a claim that contradicts the Islamabad police's statement that the officer was shot while attempting to prevent an abduction or save a woman. Heading: KPCC chief alleges RSS leader met Pakistani officials abroad Ram Madhav sends legal notice to BK Hariprasad
Summary:
A political controversy has erupted in Karnataka after KPCC President B.K. Hariprasad alleged that RSS leader and BJP strategist Ram Madhav held secret meetings with Pakistani officials in Colombo and London. Ram Madhav has issued a legal notice to Hariprasad, denying the allegations as false and defamatory, and demanding an unconditional apology.
The BJP has also condemned Hariprasad's remarks, and the controversy is expected to intensify ahead of upcoming civic elections in Karnataka, with calls for the Union government to clarify the matter.
Content: HANS NEWS SERVICE BENGALURU A fresh political controversy has erupted in Karnataka after senior RSS leader and BJP strategist Ram Madhav issued a legal notice to Karnataka Pradesh Congress Committee (KPCC) President B.K. Hariprasad over his allegations that the former had held secret meetings with Pakistani officials in Colombo and London. The notice accuses Hariprasad of making "false, defamatory and malicious" statements intended to tarnish Ram Madhav's public image and reputation. The legal notice, served under Section 356 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), states that Hariprasad's remarks were made without any factual basis and were aimed solely at causing reputational damage. It further demands that the Congress leader issue an unconditional public apology and withdraw the allegations, failing which appropriate legal proceedings would be initiated against him. The controversy stems from remarks made by Hariprasad during a seminar in Bengaluru earlier this week, where he alleged that Ram Madhav, who has been appointed BJP's in-charge for the upcoming Greater Bengaluru Authority (GBA) elections, had held four "secret meetings" with Pakistani officials in Colombo and London, including one with a retired Major General of Pakistan's Inter-Services Intelligence (ISI). Questioning the legitimacy of the alleged meetings, Hariprasad had asked under whose authority Ram Madhav engaged in discussions with Pakistani representatives. "Ram Madhav is neither the External Affairs Minister nor an MLA or MP. Who authorised an RSS pracharak to hold discussions with Pakistani representatives? The Union government must clarify what transpired during those meetings," Hariprasad had said. He also linked the alleged meetings to "Operation Sindoor" and questioned why an RSS functionary was participating in what he described as sensitive diplomatic engagements. However, Ram Madhav has categorically denied the allegations, maintaining that he never participated in any secret or Track-II dialogue with Pakistani officials. In the legal notice, his counsel has asserted that Hariprasad deliberately made reckless allegations to malign his reputation and mislead the public. The BJP has also condemned the Congress leader's remarks, describing them as baseless and politically motivated. With the legal notice now issued, the controversy is expected to intensify further as both parties continue to trade charges ahead of the upcoming civic elections in Karnataka.

Heading: When trust meets algorithms
Summary: The article explores how the rise of AI-generated synthetic media is eroding foundational trust in information and authorship, making it increasingly difficult to discern truth from falsehood. It highlights instances from deceptive videos to AI-assisted writing, emphasizing the societal implications of widespread misinformation and the challenge of maintaining trust in a post-truth era. The author, an IAS officer, questions how society can navigate this complex landscape where authenticity is constantly in doubt.
Content: The other day, someone in a WhatsApp group of which I am also a member shared a video of a Buddhist monk climbing a cliff with his bare hands. The monk scaled the rocky edges with remarkable agility and death-defying skill. The caption below praised his climbing prowess and chided the viewer for not living the ascetic's way of life. Even I was drawn to it – until another member of the group pointed out, “This video is AI.” Naturally, I felt cheated. I had developed a sense of expertise in detecting and identifying videos made with Artificial Intelligence. AI-made videos are usually too clear and too precise, and there are certain points within each shot where the contours of objects tend to blur or fail to fit with the regularity you expect in real life. The rule of thumb is that if a video looks too good to be true, then it surely is not true. Yet this video of the Buddhist monk was different. It had a particular grainy texture to it, as if it had been shot by an amateur. The monk and the surrounding area had naturally defined contours, making it too difficult to spot any irregularity at first glance. Right when you feel you have mastered the ability to call out AI-made videos, AI goes one step further and bowls you a googly. There are many such “authentic” videos made using Artificial Intelligence now flooding the internet. The one showing CCTV footage of a tiger attacking a sleeping person is one such instance. More importantly, this brings us to the issue of trust. How do we know that what is being thrown at us is real and not generated by an algorithm? The foundations of our societies are built on trust. As humans, trust plays an important role in our day-to-day lives and decision-making. We eat in a restaurant because we trust that the food being served to us is hygienic. We cross the road because we expect the approaching vehicle to slow down on seeing us. We board an aeroplane because we trust that it will not go down. The moment trust breaks down, societal interactions can potentially come to a grinding halt. While the potential downsides of AI in terms of job losses and automation are extensively discussed, the repercussions of a breakdown in trust seem to have been overlooked. AI-generated misinformation is now being produced at a scale perhaps unprecedented in human history. We are flooded with content on social media whose authenticity we cannot be sure of. Some of it is deliberately created. During Operation Sindoor, the adversary attempted psychological warfare through multiple AI-generated videos, which appeared real to the untrained eye at first glance. Yet there are others that are less malicious in nature. The videos I mentioned at the beginning are of this kind. The recent controversy surrounding the Commonwealth Short Story Prize is another curious case that compounds the consternation. We are left questioning whether a particular story was written using AI. But the critical point is this: how does the reader trust the work of an author? Every time we read, the question that arises in our minds is whether these words are flowing from the author or from the machine. The reader gradually tends to lose faith in the craftsmanship of the author. The problem is compounded by the fact that AI is getting better each day at making it even more difficult to separate the genuine from the fake. Teachers today complain of students resorting to AI to prepare answers and project reports. Yet the irony is that hardly any person tasked with preparing a 20-page report refrains from using AI. What this creates is a tragedy of the commons – for trust. As trust erodes, there is hardly any incentive for anyone to expend his or her own effort and energy on doing something original, because no one will believe that it is original work. How does one break out of this vicious cycle? There does not appear to be a clear answer. Perhaps, in this post-truth era of ours, it is simply a lived reality of our times. Or, for starters, how about acknowledging the use of AI in our supposedly original work? Like this piece of writing by yours truly – surely AI must have been used to comb through the content and correct the grammar. Or maybe not? The writer is a serving IAS officer in Assam

Summary: Defence Minister Rajnath Singh highlighted India's transformative journey towards self-reliance and its enhanced global stature, attributing these to government policies like 'Make-in-India' and 'Aatmanirbhar Bharat'. Content: New Delhi: Defence minister Rajnath Singh said Saturday "India's journey over the last 12 years has been a progression from shortages to self-reliance, from self-reliance to self-confidence and from self-confidence towards building Viksit Bharat." Addressing the NBT Utsav programme as the chief guest on the occasion of Navbharat Times completing 79 years, Rajnath said that in its first term, PM Narendra Modi-led govt had addressed shortages, expanded opportunities and transformed the work culture; in the second term, it had turned aspirations into achievements and placed the country firmly on path of Aatmanirbharata; and in its third term, govt is laying foundation for Viksit Bharat through the policy of "reform, perform, transform". Highlighting key aspects of the country's transformation over last 12 years, he said when 'Make-in-India' was launched in 2014, certain quarters labelled it a failure, but scheme set new benchmarks of success. Confidence in 'made-in-India' defence platforms has especially got a boost after Op Sindoor. He said defence production has crossed Rs 1.78 lakh crore, compared with just Rs 46,000 crore about 8-9 years ago. Defence exports, which stood at just Rs 686 crore in 2013-14, have crossed a record Rs 38,000 crore. Indirectly referring to the recent controversy over opposition's allegations that he had lied in Parliament about the death of six soldiers during Op Sindoor, Singh said false narratives are spread at times in society that severely affect the morale of armed forces. He said he would not like to discuss those issues at the event but added that such statements create unnecessary confusion. Terming media's role in the present era of 'communicative abundance' as more crucial than ever, Rajnath said, "Especially when the subject concerns defence, national security or the honour of those who make the severe sacrifice in the service of the nation, every word becomes a matter of national responsibility. Media must always uphold the values of accuracy, objectivity and impartiality." On positive changes in India, minister said, "There has been a transformational change in India's global stature. While the world earlier paid little heed to our voice, today it listens attentively to India's perspective on global issues." Rajnath pointed out that abrogation of Article 370 in J&K and sustained efforts to eliminate Naxalism are shining examples of his govt's resolve to address issues that were once considered beyond resolution. Despite scepticism over India's semiconductor mission when it was launched in 2021, the nation produced its own semiconductor chips last year due to the establishment of semiconductor parks, he added. He also highlighted India's significant growth in manufacturing and technology, citing the expansion of mobile manufacturing, automobile exports, indigenous locomotive production and digital infrastructure under Make-in-India.

"Chanda chori has taken place. It is absolutely beyond any doubt and beyond any controversy," Ramesh said, describing a recent statement by the RSS on the issue as "disgraceful and shameful". "These are people who tried to give certificates to others for integrity, honesty and nationalism, but they have been caught in a most disgraceful and shameful manner. Calling for an independent investigation, Ramesh said: "There should be an inquiry by a sitting Supreme Court judge. The toughest action should be taken against all the accused." He also sought a response from Prime Minister Narendra Modi, noting that the Prime Minister had taken credit for the Ram Temple's construction and inauguration on 22 January, 2024, ahead of the Lok Sabha elections. "We expect the Prime Minister...to make a statement," Ramesh said. On the privilege motion moved by Congress MP K C Venugopal against Rajnath Singh, Ramesh said: "My senior colleague K.C. Venugopal has rightly written a letter to the Speaker stating that the Defence Minister made a statement during his speech in the Operation Sindoor debate that was later contradicted by the facts that emerged."

He highlighted India's journey from dependence to self-reliance and its focus on technological development and modernization as key strengths for the 21st century.
Content: New Delhi, July 5 (Representative): Defense Minister Rajnath Singh said on Monday that after 'Operation Sindoor', trust in 'Made-in-India' defense equipment has increased. In his address at a program here, he said, "Today our defense production has exceeded Rs 1.78 lakh crore, whereas about 8-9 years ago it was around Rs 46,000 crore." 'Operation Sindoor' was an action similar to the demonetization carried out by India in May 2025 in response to the first international attack. Many defense systems made in India played an important role in this. Rajnath said, "Defense exports have exceeded a record Rs 38,000 crore. This was only Rs 686 crore in 2013-14, and it has increased 57 times. I don't want to give the full report, but my estimate is that this figure will currently be around Rs 40,000 crore." In his address, he also spoke about India's journey in various sectors over the last 12 years, the progress of AI, and the importance of human sensitivity in the age of AI (which also includes the field of journalism). Rajnath Singh said, "In the last 12 years, India's journey has been from dependence to self-reliance, from self-reliance to self-confidence, and from self-confidence to the creation of a developed India." He said that India is giving importance to technological development and modernization, and this confluence of 'country and technology' is the greatest strength of the country in the '21st century'.

Heading: Monsoon Parliament
Summary: The article details the upcoming Monsoon Parliament session, where discussions on increasing Lok Sabha seats by 2026 and passing key bills, including constitutional amendments, are anticipated. It highlights significant political controversy, including the suspension of 22 opposition MPs and a proposed bill to remove corrupt ministers, which has sparked intense debate. Opposition parties are poised to challenge the government on various issues, notably accusing the Defense Minister of evading questions regarding Operation Sindoor.
Content: The President has approved the redrawing of Parliament seats by 2026, stating that the number of seats will increase from 20 to 13. This session is expected to discuss actions, discussions, and decisions of national importance. The previous Parliament session was productive, with many states passing important bills. The Speaker's decision to suspend 20 members of the Trinamool Congress (TMC) and 2 members of the Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) for disrupting the Parliament session has led to political uproar. This decision has changed the political landscape. Three TMC MPs were suspended for disrupting the session. This has led to further strengthening of the opposition. Several key bills are expected to be passed in the upcoming Monsoon session. The report of the Joint Parliamentary Committee on 130 constitutional amendment bills is particularly important. The JPC is expected to approve its report in its 17th meeting. The report will be submitted to Parliament for consideration. There is a proposal in the bill that Chief Ministers, Central or State Ministers, or any other minister found guilty of corruption should be removed from their posts for 30 days and sent to judicial custody. This provision is already causing severe political debate. It is known that the government is considering increasing Lok Sabha seats by 50% in all states. The proposal to increase Lok Sabha seats based on population representation has become controversial in many states. Meanwhile, opposition parties are preparing to corner the government on several issues. The Congress has accused Defense Minister Rajnath Singh of avoiding the House on the issue related to the actions of the Indian Army during Operation Sindoor. The demand is that action be taken against him for violating parliamentary privileges, and this issue is expected to be raised in the Monsoon session.

Heading: REVEALED, MASOOD AZHAR'S LETTERS ON OP SINDOOR
Summary: The article analyzes letters from Masood Azhar following an Indian air strike, revealing his attempts to reframe the deaths of his relatives as martyrdom and blame PM Modi. Azhar uses emotional appeals, theological justifications, and calls for Pakistan to retaliate militarily, portraying the damaged mosque as a symbol of resilience. He also claims the subsequent Pakistani response, "Operation Bunyan-un-Marsoos," marked the "beginning of the failure of the RSS in India."
Content: INSIDE A TERROR FACTORY REVEALED, MASOOD AZHAR'S LETTERS ON OP SINDOOR CONTINUED FROM P1 managed household finances carefully and arranged the marriages of all her children. Azhar says he often praised her management skills, telling her she was an expert at running a household despite limited means, while she would quietly bow her head in humility whenever he complimented her. He also reveals that she was especially attached to her youngest son and youngest daughter, both of whom died alongside her in the strike. Another communication focuses on his brother-in-law, Hafiz Muhammad Jamil. Instead of portraying him as a terrorist, Azhar describes him as an accountant employed in Bahawalpur's grain market. According to the letter, Jamil specialised in bookkeeping and also maintained the accounts of JeM's mosques, handling large sums of money entrusted to him. Azhar writes that after Jamil's death the family decided to identify any outstanding debts he might have left behind. When they contacted his employer, they were told that Jamil had borrowed Rs 100,000 for his son's marriage, of which Rs 63,000 remained unpaid. According to Azhar, the employer broke down in tears and refused to recover the remaining amount, citing Jamil's honesty and integrity. The children killed in the strikes emerge as the cen-trepiece of almost every subsequent communication. Azhar repeatedly refers to them as "flowers of Para-dise," "birds of Paradise," and "innocent birds". In one letter he says an entire household lost four children between the ages of three and seven, leaving their parents alone. In another communica-tion, he reveals that two women killed in the strike were pregnant, one due to give birth within a week and the other within four months. Invoking Islamic jurisprudence, he argues that because the unborn chil-dren had already been "en-souled," they too should be counted among the martyrs. Perhaps the most per-sonal passage appears in a letter where Azhar admits that children have always been his greatest emotional weakness. He writes that whenever he saw young children he him-self became like one of them, and they in turn accepted him as their companion. Anticipating the possibility of such a tragedy long before it occurred, he says he had carried for years a copy of Bard al-Akbad "inda Faqd al-Awlad" ("Cooling the Hearts of Those who Have Lost Children") so that if he ever lost one of his own children he would remain patient rather than succumb to grief. Almost immediately af-ter announcing the deaths, Azhar begins reframing them as a theological event. In the very first communi-cation issued after the strike, he personally blames Prime Minister Narendra Modi for the deaths of his relatives. He argues that the strikes crossed all limits and sug-gests that they eliminated any expectation of restraint, portraying the bombing of "major loss" but insists they should not be regarded as a defeat, arguing instead that those killed had fulfilled their duty and attained mar-tyrdom. The letters then connect the deaths directly to JeM's ideological mission even as he kept attacking Prime Minister Modi for authoris-ing Operation Sindoor. Referring to five children killed at Jamia Masjid Sub-han Allah, Azhar writes that the "five innocent birds of Paradise" had, within two days, spread such a power-ful call to faith and jihad that "we could not have achieved the same in forty years." As the immediate mourn-ing subsides, the correspon-dence assumes an increas-ingly political tone. One letter, apparently written about 36 hours af-ter the Indian strikes, calls upon Pakistan to retaliate militarily. Azhar, while acknowledg-ing that modern technology makes it difficult to stop such attacks (referring to the air strike by the Indian Air Force), insists that Pakistan must now launch a counter-strike. Failure to retaliate, he writes, would invite humili-ation and even divine pun-ishment. He goes further, arguing that "forgiveness" in such circumstances would be a sin and that "a ceasefire is a crime", urging Pakistan's leadership to respond mili-tarily to protect the country. Another recurring theme is Jamia Masjid Subhan Al-lah in Bahawalpur, one of the sites damaged during Operation Sindoor. Azhar repeatedly returns to the mosque, portraying it as the principal symbol of re-silience after the strikes. He claims supporters volun-teered to rebuild it, that wor-shippers continued reaching the mosque despite the dam-age and that congregational prayers resumed almost immediately. According to him, only one Fajr prayer was missed after the strike, while Friday prayers and the remaining daily prayers continued without inter-ruption. In another letter he claims the mosque and surrounding buildings were filled with angels on the night of the attack and that miraculous events enabled intended targets to survive. The final stage of the cor-respondence follows Paki-stan's launch of Operation Bunyan-un-Marsoos in response to Operation Sin-door. Azhar immediately issued a letter carrying the same title. Invoking the Quranic phrase Bunyan-un-Mar-soos, he praises those who authorised what he calls the "blessed jihadi attack" and those who carried it out, de-scribing the operation as an extraordinary achievement and claiming it marked "the beginning of the failure of the RSS in India." The letter concludes with one of the most striking pas-sages in the entire series. Returning once again to the children killed in the strikes, Azhar writes that the children were "looking at missiles bearing their names" (ostensibly referring to Pakistani missiles that were used in "Bunyan-un-Marsoos"), though the let-ter does not explain wheth-er this is meant literally or metaphorically. He portrays them as joyfully watching the retaliation, treating the missiles as new toys while declaring that "much more is yet to come." Heading: Parliament Monsoon Session to begin from July 20
Summary:
The Parliament's Monsoon Session is scheduled from July 20 to August 13, 2026, as announced by Union Parliamentary Affairs Minister Kiren Rijiju, with President Droupadi Murmu's approval. Key legislative business includes the women's reservation bill and the controversial 130th Constitution Amendment Bill, which proposes automatic removal of ministers from office if held in judicial custody for 30 days.
This controversial bill has sparked a sharp political debate, with the opposition warning it could be misused for political vendetta and destabilize elected governments. Additionally, the Opposition plans to initiate privilege proceedings against Defence Minister Rajnath Singh for allegedly misleading the House.
Content: UNTIL AUGUST 13 Parliament Monsoon Session to begin from July 20 CORRESPONDENT NEW DELHI The Monsoon Session of Parliament to be held from July 20 to August 13, Union Parliamentary Affairs Minister Kiren Rijiju said on Saturday. In a post on X, Rijiju announced that President Droupadi Murmu has approved Parliament's Monsoon Session 2026 which will be begin from July 20 and continue till August 13, 2026. The upcoming session is expected to witness key legislative business as well as political confrontations between the government and the Opposition. One of the major pieces of legislation expected to return to Parliament is the Constitution Amendment Bill linked to implementing the 33% reservation for women in the Lok Sabha and state legislative assemblies. The proposed amendment seeks a uniform 50% increase in the strength of the Lok Sabha and state assemblies to operationalise the women's reservation law, According to Economic Times. The Joint Parliamentary Committee (JPC) examining the controversial 130th Constitution Amendment Bill is expected to adopt its report on July 17, with indications that it will retain the Bill's most debated provision mandating the automatic removal of the Prime Minister, Chief Ministers and Union or State ministers from office if they are arrested and remain in judicial custody for 30 consecutive days in cases involving serious offences. The JPC is expected to finalise and adopt its report at its meeting on July 17 before submitting it to Parliament for further consideration. The committee is unlikely to recommend dropping the contentious clause despite concerns raised by several stakeholders during deliberations. However, the report is expected to include safeguards aimed at preventing the provision from being misused for political vendetta or motivated prosecutions. "The proposed amendment had triggered a sharp political debate, with supporters arguing that it would strengthen accountability in public office, while the opposition has warned that it could be exploited to destabilise elected governments through politically motivated investigations and arrests. The Opposition is also expected to bring up the issue of privilege proceedings against Defence Minister Rajnath Singh, after the Congress alleged that he spoke a "straightforward, clear-cut lie" to mislead the House over casualties of Indian soldiers during Operation Sindoor.

Heading: REVEALED, MASOOD AZHAR'S LETTERS ON OP SINDOOR
Summary: The article reveals internal communications from Jaish-e-Mohammed chief Masood Azhar following India's Operation Sindoor, detailing his personal grief over the loss of fourteen family members and associates. Azhar's letters chronicle JeM's shift in narrative, transforming the strikes from a setback into a call for religious justification and military retaliation. The communications offer an intimate look into the lives of those killed and Azhar's personal connections, particularly with his elder sister.
Content: INSIDE A TERROR FACTORY The first communication issued after the strikes opens with an unusually personal disclosure by Azhar. He writes that fourteen people connected to him had been killed, including ten members of his family and four close associates. ABHINANDAN MISHRA NEW DELHI A series of internal communications issued by Jaish-e-Mohammed (JeM) chief Masood Azhar in the days following India's Operation Sindoor offers the most detailed account yet of how the Pakistan-based terror outfit internally processed the Indian strikes, documenting Azhar's deeply personal account of losing close family members, his attempts to transform those losses into an ideological narrative, his appeal for Pakistan to retaliate militarily and his subsequent endorsement of Islamabad's military response. The communications chronicle the evolution of JeM's messaging from 7 May 2025 onwards when Operation Sindoor became operational. Rather than portraying the strikes as an organisational setback, the letters systematically reinterpret the episode through a religious lens, beginning with personal grief, moving to theological justification, then to demands for military retaliation and finally to the celebration of Pakistan's retaliatory operation. The first communication issued after the strikes opens with an unusually personal disclosure by Azhar. He writes that fourteen people connected to him had been killed, including ten members of his family and four close associates. He identifies those killed as his elder sister, her husband, his scholar nephew, his nephew's wife, his scholar niece, five children from the family, his longtime associate Huzaifa, Huzaifa's mother and two other associates. While JeM had earlier acknowledged casualties following Operation Sindoor—a development first revealed by this newspaper on social media—the subsequent letters provide a far more intimate account of those killed, dwelling extensively on their lives and Azhar's relationship with them. One entire letter is devoted to his elder sister, whom he calls “Baji Jan”. Rather than describing her in organisational terms, Azhar remembers her as a deeply religious woman who regularly read Azhar's writings. He recalls that she frequently sent messages saying that a particular letter had resolved a problem in her household, even remarking that it often seemed as though he somehow knew what was happening inside her home. According to Azhar, she constantly prayed for martyrdom and dedicated all six of her children to Islamic education. He writes that all six became Islamic scholars and that five memorised the Quran. He highlighted that defense production has surged to over Rs 1.78 lakh crore and exports have grown 57-fold since 2013-14, emphasizing India's journey towards self-reliance and a developed nation. Content: New Delhi/Bhasha. Defense Minister Rajnath Singh said on Saturday that after 'Operation Sindoor', trust in 'Made-in-India' defense equipment has increased. Addressing a program here, he said that today our defense production has exceeded Rs 1.78 lakh crore, whereas about 8-9 years ago it was around Rs 46,000 crore. The Union Minister said that after Operation Sindoor, trust in Made-in-India defense equipment has increased. Operation Sindoor was a decisive military action taken by India in May 2025 in response to the Pahalgam terrorist attack. Many defense systems made in India played a crucial role in this. Singh said, defense exports have also exceeded a record Rs 38,000 crore. This was only Rs 686 crore in 2013-14, and today it has increased 57 times. I have not asked for the full report, but my estimate is that this figure will be around Rs 40,000 crore. In his address, he also spoke about India's journey in various sectors over the last 12 years, the progress of Artificial Intelligence (AI), and the importance of human sensitivity in the era of AI (which also includes the field of journalism). This program was organized in Delhi to mark the completion of 80 years of the national Hindi daily 'Navbharat Times'. Singh said that India's journey over the last 12 years has been from scarcity to self-reliance, from self-reliance to self-confidence, and from self-confidence towards building a developed India. He warned that AI can read data and analyze it, but it cannot understand the pulse of the people. He said that this is where human sensitivity and human understanding play a crucial role. Singh stated that 'journalism' has also been affected by technological advancements like Artificial Intelligence (AI), but these will not be able to surpass human creativity and intellect. He said that the future success of journalism will depend on how well it can strike a balance and coordination between AI's capabilities and human empathy. While AI will make journalism faster and more accurate, emotional intelligence will ensure that it remains human and trustworthy.

Summary: Defence Minister Rajnath Singh stated that trust in "made-in-India" defence platforms has significantly increased following Operation Sindoor, a decisive military action. He highlighted a substantial boost in defence production and exports, emphasizing India's journey towards self-reliance and a "Viksit Bharat." Singh also discussed the role of AI in various sectors, including journalism, stressing the importance of human sensitivity and credible reporting, especially concerning national security.
Content: NEW DELHI, July 4: Defence Minister Rajnath Singh on Saturday said that after Operation Sindoor, the trust in “made-in-India” defence platforms has received a boost. In his address at an event here, he also reiterated that “today, our defence production has reached over ₹ 1.78 lakh crore, and about 8-9 years ago, it stood at approximately ₹ 46,000 crore”. The Union minister asserted that after Operation Sindoor, “trust in made-in-India defence platforms has got enhanced”. Operation Sindoor was India’s decisive military action conducted in May 2025 in response to the Pahalgam terror attack. Several defence platforms built in India had played a key role in it. Singh said, “Defence exports too have reached a record over ₹ 38,000 crore, and in 2013-14, it stood at just ₹ 686 crore, and it has grown today 57 times. And, I have not sought the full report, but, currently it should be hovering around ₹ 40,000 crore, is my estimate.” In his address, he also spoke of India’s journey in various sectors in the last 12 years, the advancement of artificial intelligence (AI) and the importance of human sensitivity in the age of AI, including in the field of journalism. The event was hosted in Delhi to mark 80 years of the national Hindi daily Navbharat Times. “India’s journey over the last 12 years has been a progression from shortages to self-reliance, from self-reliance to self-confidence towards building a Viksit Bharat,” Singh said. He said India lays emphasis on both technological development and celebrating its traditions, and this confluence of “tradition and technology” is the “biggest strength of the country in the 21st century”. Underlining that AI has touched nearly all aspects of human existence today, he cautioned that while AI can read and analyse data, it “cannot feel the pulse” of the people, which is where the human sensitivity comes into picture. Singh pointed out that journalism too has been impacted by technological advancements such as AI, but they won’t be able to surpass human creativity and intellect. “The future success of journalism will depend on how well it establishes the balance and synergy between the capabilities of AI and human empathy. While AI will make journalism faster and more precise, emotional intelligence will ensure that it remains humane and credible,” he said. The Union minister also emphasised maintaining credibility in journalism in the era of fake news and misinformation. Terming the media’s role in the present era of, what he described as “communicative abundance”, as more crucial than ever, the defence minister said the challenge today is not lack of information, but its accuracy and reliability. Misinformation severely impacts society and the morale of defence forces, he said, adding that while being the first to report may be important in journalism, disseminating correct news is even more crucial. “Especially when the subject concerns the defence forces, national security, or the honour of those who make the supreme sacrifice in the service of the nation, every word becomes a matter of national responsibility. The media must always uphold the values of accuracy, objectivity, and impartiality,” Singh said. (PTI)

Heading: Monsoon Session to begin from July 20
Summary: The Monsoon Session of Parliament is scheduled to commence on July 20 and conclude on August 13, 2026, with President Droupadi Murmu having approved the session based on the Central Government's recommendation, as stated by Parliamentary Affairs Minister Kiren Rijiju. During this session, the government plans to introduce new bills, notably one to remove Prime Ministers, Chief Ministers, or ministers jailed for 30 days, while the opposition is preparing to raise concerns such as paper leaks and inflation. Content:
New Delhi. The Monsoon Session of Parliament will be held from July 20 to August 13, 2026. Parliamentary Affairs Minister Kiren Rijiju informed that President Droupadi Murmu has approved the calling of a meeting of both Houses on the recommendation of the Central Government. This announcement regarding the Monsoon Session dates has been made by the central government.

During this session, the government is expected to introduce several new bills, including a significant Constitution Amendment Bill. This bill proposes the removal of Prime Ministers, Chief Ministers, and ministers from their posts if they remain in jail for 30 days. Meanwhile, the opposition is preparing to challenge and corner the government on various issues such as Defense Minister Rajnath Singh's statement on the martyrdom of soldiers in Operation Sindoor, recent paper leaks, rising inflation, and the alleged theft of offerings from the Ram Mandir.

Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla has indicated that the inquiry committee report on the Justice Yashwant Verma case will be tabled in the Lok Sabha on the first or second day of the session. Speaker Birla stated that the inquiry report related to the cash recovery case involving Justice Yashwant Verma will be presented to the House, and further parliamentary procedure may be decided based on its findings.

In a related development, the Joint Parliamentary Committee (JPC) investigating the 130th Constitution Amendment Bill, 2025, is scheduled to meet on July 17 to approve its report, which will then guide the subsequent legislative process. Additionally, two other important matters—the recognition of opposition parties and seating arrangements in the Lok Sabha—are also expected to be decided soon. The Lok Sabha Speaker is anticipated to make decisions on pending issues concerning the Trinamool Congress (TMC) and Shiv Sena (Uddhav Balasaheb Thackeray), which could significantly impact their parliamentary status and roles. New Delhi, Date 4 (Special Correspondent) - The Monsoon Session of Parliament, scheduled to begin on July 20 and continue till August 13, is expected to witness a major uproar. Parliamentary Affairs Minister Kiren Rijiju announced today via an 'X' post that President Droupadi Murmu has informed the government about convening this session, which will last for about four weeks. The session is anticipated to be tumultuous, with the opposition planning to raise issues such as the alleged embezzlement of donations from the holy Shri Ram Temple in Ayodhya, a symbol of faith not only in the country but for Hindus worldwide, by individuals associated with the BJP. The alleged 'theft' of MPs from Shiv Sena and Trinamool Congress for a 'demonic majority' is also expected to be a contentious point. Due to the alleged donation theft in the Ram Temple, the Narendra Modi government at the Centre is on the back foot. As the role of Champat Rai, the trustee of the Ram Temple appointed by Prime Minister Modi himself, is suspicious, PM Modi himself is in trouble. It is likely that the opposition will target the Prime Minister over the issue of Champat Rai.

Furthermore, the government will face scrutiny over 'Operation Sindoor'. While the government had stated that no Indian soldier was martyred in 'Operation Sindoor', information has come to light that six soldiers had to make the supreme sacrifice, exposing the government's falsehood. Due to this, Defense Minister Rajnath Singh and the government will have to face a barrage of questions. At the same time, the government will try to pass important bills. There is a strong possibility that the Lok Sabha Constituency Delimitation Bill, which was rejected in the previous session, will be reintroduced by the government. In recent months, BJP and its allies have split MPs from opposition parties, increasing the NDA's numbers on paper. Based on this, there is a possibility that the government will try to push this bill through. The government is also trying to get the 'One Nation One Election' bill passed. Page 4.

Content:
NEW DELHI THE BJP-led Central government's controversial proposal to automatically remove the Prime Minister, Chief Ministers and Ministers from office if they remain in judicial custody for 30 consecutive days, along with a brewing row over Defence Minister Rajnath Singh's remarks on Operation Sindoor, are set to dominate the monsoon session of Parliament beginning July 20. The government on Saturday announced that the session will run until August 13. Parliamentary Affairs Minister Kiren Rijiju said President Droupadi Murmu had approved summoning both Houses from July 20 "for meaningful debate, discussion and decisions on issues of national importance". The spotlight is expected to fall on the Constitution (130th Amendment) Bill, 2025, after a Joint Parliamentary Committee (JPC) examining the legislation is scheduled to meet on July 17 to adopt its report.

The JPC is unlikely to recommend dropping the bill's contentious provision, which mandates the automatic removal of the PM, CMs and Union or State Ministers if they are arrested and remain in judicial custody for 30 consecutive days in cases involving serious offenses. The report, however, is expected to recommend safeguards to prevent misuse through politically motivated prosecutions or vendetta, reports said, citing unnamed sources but did not report further details. The proposed constitutional amendment has emerged as one of the government's most debated legislative initiatives since it was introduced last year.

Heading: After Op Sindoor, trust in ‘made-in-India’ defence platforms got enhanced: Rajnath Singh
Summary: Defence Minister Rajnath Singh stated that trust in 'made-in-India' defence platforms has significantly increased following Operation Sindoor, a decisive military action in May 2025. He highlighted a boost in defence production to over Rs 1.78 lakh crore and a 57-fold increase in defence exports since 2013-14. Singh also discussed India's journey towards self-reliance and the importance of human sensitivity and credibility in journalism amidst advancements in AI.
Content: Press Trust of India New Delhi, Jul 4 Defence Minister Rajnath Singh on Saturday said that after Operation Sindoor, the trust in "made-in-India" defence platforms has received a boost. In his address at an event here, he also reiterated that "today, our defence production has reached over Rs 1.78 lakh crore, and about 8-9 years ago, it stood at approximately Rs 46,000 crore". The Union minister asserted that after Operation Sindoor, "trust in made-in-India defence platforms has got enhanced". Operation Sindoor was India's decisive military action conducted in May 2025 in response to the Pahalgam terror attack. Several defence platforms built in India had played a key role in it. Singh said, "Defence exports too have reached a record over Rs 38,000 crore, and in 2013-14, it stood at just Rs 686 crore, and it has grown today 57 times. And, I have not sought the full report, but, currently it should be hovering around Rs 40,000 crore, is my estimate." In his address, he also spoke of India's journey in various sectors in the last 12 years, the advancement of artificial intelligence (AI) and the importance of human sensitivity in the age of AI, including in the field of journalism. The event was hosted in Delhi to mark 80 years of the national Hindi daily Navbharat Times. "India's journey over the last 12 years has been a progression from shortages to self-reliance, from self-confidence, and from self-confidence towards building a Viksit Bharat," Singh said. He said India lays emphasis on both technological development and celebrating its traditions, and this confluence of "tradition and technology" is the "biggest strength of the country in the 21st century". Underlining that AI has touched nearly all aspects of human existence today, he cautioned that while AI can read and analyse data, it "cannot feel the pulse" of the people, which is where the human sensitivity comes into picture. Singh pointed out that journalism too has been impacted by technological advancements such as AI, but they won't be able to surpass human creativity and intellect. "The future success of journalism will depend on how well it establishes the balance and synergy between the capabilities of AI and human empathy. While AI will make journalism faster and more precise, emotional intelligence will ensure that it remains humane and credible," he said. The Union minister also emphasised maintaining credibility in journalism in the era of fake news and misinformation. Terming the media's role in the present era of what he described as "communicative abundance" as more crucial than ever, the defence minister said the challenge today is not lack of information, but its accuracy and reliability. Misinformation severely impacts society and the morale of defence forces, he said, adding that while being the first to report may be important in journalism, disseminating correct news is even more crucial. "Especially when the subject concerns the defence forces, national security, or the honour of those who make the supreme sacrifice in the service of the nation, every word becomes a matter of national responsibility. The media must always uphold the values of accuracy, objectivity, and impartiality," Singh said.

Summary: The article discusses the political controversy surrounding 'Operation Sindoor' and the martyrdom of six Indian soldiers. The opposition accuses the Modi government and the Defense Minister of misleading Parliament about casualties and failing to adequately honor the martyrs. The government, however, maintains that no Indian soldiers were harmed in the operation and that the martyrs were honored much earlier, criticizing the opposition for politicizing the issue.

Anyway, when the Defense Minister had said that no soldier was harmed, it was believed that India caused considerable damage to Pakistan in Operation Sindoor, but the country suffered no loss. Although Pakistan claimed to have shot down several fighter jets, sometimes killing more than 10 soldiers. But these were not taken seriously. Certainly, no country publicizes its losses during war or conflict; all opposing countries exaggerate the losses of the enemy. Now that the names of six soldiers have come forward, the opposition has started criticizing. Rifleman Sunil Kumar (Vir Chakra) Sergeant Surendra Kumar (Vayu Medal) Subedar Major Pawan Kumar Lance Naik Dinesh Kumar Aviation Technician Nand Murli Nayak Havildar Sunil Kumar Singh Even the world's most powerful country cannot claim that damage was one-sided in any attack or war. Despite a military force being highly trained and equipped with state-of-the-art facilities and resources, some loss of life and property is natural. This does not question the strength of the army, nor should war be brought under suspicion, nor is it appropriate to accuse the government. Six soldiers were martyred in 'Operation Sindoor', whose names have now been made public by the Modi government a year later. The names of the six martyrs are engraved in the National War Memorial. The spirit of sacrificing one's life and making the ultimate sacrifice for the defense and self-respect of the country cannot be praised enough in words, nor can sufficient gratitude be expressed. Martyrdom is martyrdom; it is not just a matter of a soldier's life; behind this lies the entire nation's... Honor is attached to any martyrdom; there should be no political debate or controversy over it. But the issue is that the weak opposition wants to find an excuse to corner the Modi government, and perhaps that is why controversial statements are being made about martyrdom, disregarding national honor and national interest. A video of the Defense Minister's statement is circulating on social media, in which it can be heard that he emphasized the word 'no' with full force, and then Home Minister Amit Shah and all BJP MPs present in the house welcomed this statement by thumping their desks and smiling. Rajnath Singh had further said in the same statement, 'To the opposition... People kept asking how many of our planes were shot down; I think their question does not correctly represent national sentiment. They never once asked how many enemy planes our forces shot down. If they want to ask a question, their question should be: did India destroy terrorist hideouts? The answer is yes. If you want to ask a question, ask if Operation Sindoor was successful, and the answer is yes.' He wrote, 'The government that wraps itself in the tricolor and never tires of talking about nationalism did not give these brave heroes the respect and remembrance they deserved.' Pawan Khera said, 'The names of these heroes should be etched forever in the collective memory of the nation.' The Ministry of Defense stated that it is clarified that the country had paid tribute to these martyred heroes much before the news of their sacrifice came out.
