Content: New Delhi // Milap News Network // Defense Minister Rajnath Singh said on Thursday that India stopped Operation Sindoor on its own terms, not because of any reduction in its capabilities. Addressing the INA National Security Summit in New Delhi, the Defense Minister said, 'We stopped it on our own terms. If the need arises, we are fully prepared for a long war. Our enhanced capability, meaning the ability to increase capability at short notice, is not only present but also better than before, and still is.' He said, 'Operation Sindoor was an example of 'joint cooperation' between the Indian Armed Forces.' This is extremely dangerous and, in a way, provides terrorists with a platform to gradually advance towards their goals. 'Terrorism is not just an enemy of one country. It has multiple dimensions - operational, ideological, and if we can solve all these politically.' In his address at an event here, he also reiterated that "today, our defence production has reached over Rs 1.78 lakh crore, and about 8-9 years ago, it stood at approximately Rs 46,000 crore". The Union minister asserted that after Operation Sindoor, "trust in made-in-India defence platforms has got enhanced". Operation Sindoor was India's decisive military action conducted in May 2025 in response to the Pahalgam terror attack. Several defence platforms built in India had played a key role in it. In his address, he also spoke of India's journey in various sectors in the last 12 years, the advancement of artificial intelligence (AI) and the importance of human sensitivity in the age of AI, including in the field of journalism. The event was hosted in Delhi to mark 80 years of the national Hindi daily Navbharat Times. "India's journey over the last 12 years has been a progression from shortages to self-reliance, from self-reliance to self-confidence, and from self-confidence towards building a Viksit Bharat,' Singh said. He said India lays emphasis on both technological development and celebrating its traditions, and this confluence of 'tradition and technology' is the 'biggest strength of the country in the 21st century'." Underlining that AI has touched nearly all aspects of human existence today, he cautioned that while AI can read and analyse data, it 'cannot feel the pulse' of the people, which is where the human sensitivity comes into picture. Singh pointed out that journalism too has been impacted by technological advancements such as AI, but they won't be able to surpass human creativity and intellect. "The future success of journalism will depend on how well it establishes the balance and synergy between the capabilities of AI and human empathy. While AI will make journalism faster and more precise, emotional intelligence will ensure that it remains humane and credible,' he said. The Union minister also emphasised maintaining credibility in journalism in the era of fake news and misinformation. Terming the media's role in the present era of, what he described as 'communicative abundance', as more crucial than ever, the defence minister said the challenge today is not lack of information, but its accuracy and reliability. Misinformation severely impacts society and the morale of defence forces, he said, adding that while being the first to report may be important in journalism, disseminating correct news is even more crucial. "Especially when the subject concerns the defence forces, national security, or the honour of those who make the supreme sacrifice in the service of the nation, every word becomes a matter of national responsibility. The media must always uphold the values ??of accuracy, objectivity, and impartiality,' Singh said.

Heading: More Strength to the Armed Forces
Summary: The Indian government has approved defense deals worth approximately 52,000 crore rupees to significantly boost the armed forces' capabilities. These acquisitions, sanctioned by the Defence Acquisition Council chaired by Defence Minister Rajnath Singh, include advanced drones, anti-tank missiles, air defense systems, and naval mines for all three services. The move aims to enhance intelligence, surveillance, and striking power, reflecting a forward-thinking approach to modern warfare and a substantial increase in the defense budget.
Content: The government's approval for the purchase of state-of-the-art drones and anti-tank missiles to enhance the striking capability of the Indian armed forces is a big step. In the meeting of the Defence Acquisition Council (DAC) held on Friday under the chairmanship of Defence Minister Rajnath Singh, defense deals worth about 52 thousand crore rupees were given in-principle approval. The significant thing is that various acquisition proposals for all three services were approved in this meeting. This includes the approval for the UAV Electronic Warfare System 'Akash Tarang' for the Army, man-portable anti-tank missile system, medium-range surface-to-air missile weapon system, very short-range air defense system (V-SHORADS), active protection system for tanks, and jet-based kamikaze drone system. Akash Tarang will not only disrupt the communication and navigation systems of enemy drones but also reduce their effectiveness. This will help in thwarting enemy drone attacks. Similarly, shoulder-fired missile systems will enhance the infantry's capability to deal with threats from enemy armored vehicles and artillery. While V-SHORADS will strengthen the Army's response capability and effectiveness. Kamikaze suicide drones will increase striking power. The specialty of these low-cost drones is that they hover over the target for some time and then collide and explode. That is why they are called suicide drones, which destroy themselves and also destroy the target. Considering the changing trends of warfare and emerging new technologies in today's era, the decision to purchase the Akash Tarang system will be considered important. During Operation Sindoor, drones and loitering munitions were widely used by both sides in the conflict with Pakistan. Therefore, prioritizing the purchase of the anti-drone Akash Tarang system reflects the far-sighted thinking of the Defence Acquisition Council. Along with this, the approval for the purchase of pseudo-satellites for air defense is also important. This will provide the Air Force with continuous intelligence surveillance, telecommunication, and remote sensing capabilities. The approval for modern naval mines to be laid on the sea surface for the Navy is a significant step towards maintaining dominance at sea. Upon their impact, enemy warships or submarines will be destroyed. India has increased its defense budget by more than 15 percent this year, which will become new energy and strength for the Indian armed forces in water, land, and air.

He also emphasized the critical role of human sensitivity and credibility in journalism, particularly concerning national security, in an era of rising AI and misinformation, asserting that while AI can enhance the field, human empathy and accuracy remain paramount for its future success.
Content: PAGE 6 NATION Op Sindoor boosted trust in Indian defence platforms: Rajnath Singh PIONEER NEWS SERVICE n New Delhi Defence Minister Rajnath Singh on Saturday said that after Operation Sindoor, the trust in "made-in-India" defence platforms has received a boost. In his address at an event in New Delhi, he also reiterated that "today, our defence production has reached over `1.78 lakh crore, and about 8-9 years ago, it stood at approximately `46,000 crore". The Union minister asserted that after Operation Sindoor, "trust in made-in-India defence platforms has been enhanced". Operation Sindoor was India's decisive military action conducted in May 2025 in response to the Pahalgam terror attack. Several defence platforms built in India had played a key role in it. Singh said, "Defence exports too have reached a record over `38,000 crore, and in 2013-14, it stood at just `686 crore, and it has grown today 57 times. And, I have not sought the full report, but currently it should be hover-ing around `40,000 crore, which is my estimate." In his address, he also spoke of India's journey in various sectors in the last 12 years, the advancement of artificial intelligence (AI) and the importance of human sensitivity in the age of AI, including in the field of journalism. The event was hosted in Delhi to mark 80 years of the national Hindi daily Navbharat Times. "India's journey over the last 12 years has been a pro-gression from shortages to self-reliance, from self-reliance to self-confidence, and from self-confidence towards building a Viksit Bharat," Singh said. He said India lays empha-sis on both technological development and celebrating its traditions, and this conflu-ence of "tradition and tech-nology" is the "biggest strength of the country in the 21st century". Underlining that AI has touched nearly all aspects of human existence today, he cautioned that while AI can read and analyse data, it "cannot feel the pulse" of the people, which is where the human sensitivity comes into the picture. Singh pointed out that journalism, too, has been impacted by technological advancements such as AI, but they won't be able to surpass human creativity and intellect. "The future success of jour-nalism will depend on how well it establishes the balance and synergy between the capabilities of AI and human empathy. While AI will make journalism faster and more precise, emotional intelligence will ensure that it remains humane and credible," he said. The Union minister also emphasised maintaining credibility in journalism in the era of fake news and misinformation. Terming the media's role in the present era of what he described as "communica-tive abundance" as more crucial than ever, the defence minister said the challenge today is not lack of informa-tion, but its accuracy and reliability. Misinformation severely impacts society and the morale of defence forces, he said, adding that while being the first to report may be important in journalism, dis-seminating correct news is even more crucial. "Especially when the subject concerns the defence forces, national security, or the honour of those who make the supreme sacrifice in the service of the nation, every word becomes a matter of national responsibility. The media must always uphold the values of accuracy, objectivity, and impartiality," Singh said. PTI

Heading: The reality can be different
Summary: The article criticizes the Union government for its lack of transparency regarding casualties in 'Operation Sindoor', specifically the delayed disclosure of six soldiers' names. It highlights contradictory official statements and inconsistent explanations, which have led to scrutiny and a privilege motion against the Defence Minister. The author argues that such selective disclosure undermines public confidence and accountability, risking the government's credibility.
Content: If telling lies ruin one's credibility, disclosed suppressed lie may ruin the very existence of the person. This is a truth that applies everywhere, be it in politics or society in general. It is because one's credibility may be regained in time by consistent endeavour but suppressed lies once disclosed ruin the very prospect of regaining confidence in others. The disclosure of the names of six soldiers who were killed during last year's Operation Sindoor – recently inscribed on the National War Memorial – ironically underlines the Union government's failure to uphold the democratic norms of transparency. While India rightly honours the ultimate sacrifices of Subedar Major Pawan Kumar, Rifleman Sunil Kumar, Lance Naik Dinesh Kumar, Havildar Sunil Kumar Singh, Sergeant Surendra Kumar, and Agniveer Mood Muralinaik, the delay in a ceremonial announcement formally recording their identities has led to scrutiny. These revelations have emerged more than a year after the operation, raising critical questions about accountability. The government's subsequent explanations regarding the delay have not been convincing. Important questions on the credibility of official positions now cloud what should have been a time for remembering the fallen. In May 2025, then Director General of Military Operations (DGMO) Lieutenant General Rajiv Ghai acknowledged that the operation had resulted in casualties but did not reveal the identities or the number of soldiers who had died. Yet, Defence Minister Rajnath Singh told the Lok Sabha that no Indian soldiers were harmed during the operation. The government has since argued that the minister was responding specifically to reports concerning the deaths of fighter pilots. That explanation, however, has failed to blunt the questions. The opposition Congress has sought a privilege motion against the minister, arguing that Parliament was misled. The episode adds to a pattern of contradictory official narratives regarding the losses sustained during Operation Sindoor, undermining public confidence in these accounts. No one expects the government or the armed forces to reveal operational details of the conflict or sensitive information that could compromise national security. However, in a democracy, transparency about casualties, setbacks, and the operational costs of military action is important. Public confidence cannot be ensured through selective disclosure, suppression, or exaggeration of facts. A government's credibility rests not on projecting a face of invincibility but on demonstrating honesty and accountability to the citizens. When official statements are perceived as evasive or inconsistent, they risk creating doubts regarding the government's claims in other domains as well. Heading: First DAC under new military leadership clears Rs 52,000 crore buys
Summary: The Defence Acquisition Council (DAC), chaired by Defence Minister Rajnath Singh, has approved capital acquisition proposals worth approximately Rs 52,000 crore for the armed forces' modernization. These acquisitions prioritize counter-drone systems, layered air defence, anti-tank weapons, and surveillance platforms, influenced by recent hostilities with Pakistan. The approvals also include the indigenous 'Akash-Tarang' anti-UAV electronic warfare system for the Army.
Content:
NEW DELHI: The Defence Acquisition Council (DAC) on Friday cleared capital acquisition proposals worth around Rs 52,000 crore, with counter-drone systems, layered air defence, anti-tank weapons and persistent surveillance platforms emerging as the biggest priorities in the armed forces' latest modernisation push.
Chaired by Defence Minister Rajnath Singh, the DAC granted the "acceptance of necessity" for the projects, which is only the first step in the long-winded procurement process. The proposals will now wind their way through tendering, technical evaluation and cost negotiations, with the high-value ones also needing the Cabinet Committee on Security (CCS) nod, before contracts are eventually inked.
The Friday meeting was also the first of the DAC since a sweeping churn at the top of the military hierarchy, with Gen Raja Subramani having taken over as Chief of Defence Staff, Gen Dhiraj Seth as Army chief and Adm Krishna Swaminathan as Navy chief. The latest approvals also point to the way Operation Sindoor has influenced the military's acquisition priorities. The hostilities with Pakistan, in which swarms of drones and loitering munitions slugged it out with air defence networks on both sides, has forced the shift away from big-ticket conventional platforms towards counter-UAV systems, layered air defence, better tank survivability and round-the-clock intelligence, surveillance and reconnaissance (ISR).
The Army cornered the biggest chunk of approvals. Topping its list is the indigenous 'Akash-Tarang', an anti-UAV electronic warfare (EW) system built to detect, track and jam hostile drones before they get anywhere near forward troops.

Heading: DAC okays purchase of ₹52k-cr arms, systems
Summary: India's Defence Acquisition Council (DAC), led by Defence Minister Rajnath Singh, has approved the purchase of arms and systems worth ₹52,000 crore to significantly boost the armed forces' capabilities. This includes advanced systems like anti-UAV electronic warfare, anti-tank guided missiles, surface-to-air missiles, kamikaze drones, and naval unmanned aerial systems for the Army, Navy, and Air Force. The move aligns with India's new military leadership's focus on modernization and comes amidst increased defence spending.
Content:
Rahul Singh
letters@hindustantimes.com
NEW DELHI: The Defence Acquisition Council (DAC), headed by defence minister Rajnath Singh, on Friday gave its go-ahead for purchasing weapons and systems worth ₹52,000 crore to boost the armed forces' capabilities. The capability boost approved by the council — India's apex defence procurement body — covers procuring a raft of systems, from anti-unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) electronic warfare system 'AKASH TARANG', man-portable anti-tank guided missile (MPATGM) systems to medium range surface-to-air missile (MRSAM) weapon system, the defence ministry said.
The DAC also accorded its Acceptance of Necessity (AoN) for buying the very short range air defence system (V-SHOR-ADS), an active protection system for tanks, and a jet-based kamikaze drone system, the ministry added in a statement.
The military hardware listed above is for the army.
Under India's defence procurement rules, AoN by the council is the first step towards buying military equipment. The DAC convened for the first time under India's new military leadership — chief of defence staff General NS Raja Subramani, navy chief Admiral Krishna Swaminathan and army chief General Dheeraj Seth. The top appointments were made recently.
Seth, who took over as army chief on June 30, said on Wednesday that the force's modernisation would form the bedrock of its transformation into a future-ready force.
The defence ministry outlined the capability boost: AKASH TARANG will provide effective anti-UAV protection to army formations; the MPATGM will enhance the infantry's potential to counter the adversary's mechanised threats; and the MRSAM system provides medium range air defence against various stand-off aerial threats.
"The V-SHORADS with multi-spectral sensing will enhance counter-measure resilience and effectiveness of the Indian Army. The active protection system will improve the defence mechanism of tanks and enhance their survivability. The jet-based kamikaze drones will provide better electronic warfare capability with greater lethality and survivability while also being cost effective," the ministry said.
The military hardware approved for the Navy includes the multi-influence ground mine (MIGM), the naval shipborne unmanned aerial system (NSUAS) and the establishment of a land-based testing facility (LBTF) for electric propulsion systems. "The MIGM will deny freedom of manoeuvre to the adversary. The NSUAS, equipped with advanced sensors, will enhance the Indian Navy's situational awareness. The LBTF will meet the testing requirements for motors and associated propulsion systems of the Indian naval assets," it said.
The Indian Air Force received approval to procure the fixed-wing based high altitude pseudo satellite (FW-HAPS). It will carry out intelligence, surveillance and reconnaissance (ISR), telecommunication and remote sensing for the air force, the ministry added.
In February, India hiked its defence spending by more than 15% against the backdrop of Operation Sindoor, setting aside ₹7.85 lakh crore for the critical sector in the Union Budget for 2026-27.

NEW DELHI: The Defence Acquisition Council (DAC), headed by defence minister Rajnath Singh, on Friday gave its go-ahead for purchasing weapons and systems worth ₹52,000 crore to boost the armed forces' capabilities. The capability boost approved by the council — India's apex defence procurement body — covers procuring a raft of systems, from anti-unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) electronic warfare system 'AKASH TARANG', man-portable anti-tank guided missile (MPATGM) systems to medium range surface-to-air missile (MRSAM) weapon system, the defence ministry said.

The DAC also accorded its Acceptance of Necessity (AoN) for buying the very short range air defence system (V-SHOR-ADS), an active protection system for tanks, and a jet-based kamikaze drone system, the ministry added in a statement.

The military hardware listed above is for the army.

Under India's defence procurement rules, AoN by the council is the first step towards buying military equipment. The DAC convened for the first time under India's new military leadership — chief of defence staff General NS Raja Subramani, navy chief Admiral Krishna Swaminathan and army chief General Dheeraj Seth. The top appointments were made recently.

Seth, who took over as army chief on June 30, said on Wednesday that the force's modernisation would form the bedrock of its transformation into a future-ready force.

The defence ministry outlined the capability boost: AKASH TARANG will provide effective anti-UAV protection to army formations; the MPATGM will enhance the infantry's potential to counter the adversary's mechanised threats; and the MRSAM system provides medium range air defence against various stand-off aerial threats.

"The V-SHORADS with multi-spectral sensing will enhance counter-measure resilience and effectiveness of the Indian Army. The active protection system will improve the defence mechanism of tanks and enhance their survivability. The jet-based kamikaze drones will provide better electronic warfare capability with greater lethality and survivability while also being cost effective," the ministry said.

The military hardware approved for the Navy includes the multi-influence ground mine (MIGM), the naval shipborne unmanned aerial system (NSUAS) and the establishment of a land-based testing facility (LBTF) for electric propulsion systems. "The MIGM will deny freedom of manoeuvre to the adversary. The NSUAS, equipped with advanced sensors, will enhance the Indian Navy's situa-tional awareness. The LBTF will meet the testing requirements for motors and associated pro-pulsion systems of the Indian naval assets," it said.

The Indian Air Force received approval to procure the fixed-wing based high altitude pseudo satellite (FW-HAPS). It will carry out intelligence, surveillance and reconnaissance (ISR), telecom-munication and remote sensing for the air force, the ministry added.

In February, India hiked its defence spending by more than 15% against the backdrop of Operation Sindoor, setting aside ₹7.85 lakh crore for the critical sector in the Union Budget for 2026-27.

Content: LETTERS TO THE EDITOR Freedom and the politics of faith This refers to ‘Time to withdraw the anti-conversion law in Karnataka’ (July 2). The Constitution guarantees every citizen the freedom to profess, practise and propagate religion. Conversion through force, threat or inducement is already punishable under law and must be dealt with firmly. But peaceful persuasion and voluntary conversion cannot be criminalised. Christianity and Islam have existed in India for centuries, yet both remain minority religions. Claims that voluntary conversions threaten the country’s demographic balance are politically motivated and intended to stoke fear. The Constitution’s guarantee of religious freedom has helped preserve communal harmony and must be upheld. M V Sridhara, Mysuru Truth delayed Apropos ‘The costs of deferred truth’ (July 3), it is deplorable that even though six Indian soldiers were killed during last year’s Operation Sindoor, Defence Minister Rajnath Singh told the Lok Sabha that no Indian soldiers had been harmed. The government later argued that he was responding only to reports about the deaths of fighter pilots. The sooner the government sheds its illusion of perfection and upholds democratic accountability, the better it will be for Indian democracy. M Basavaraj, Davanagere No selective action The state government’s safe footpath campaign is commendable for clearing encroachments and restoring pedestrian space while relocating vendors. The government should also address other encroachments. On many roads, places of worship have occupied footpaths and even erected semi-permanent structures, with scant regard for public safety. Heading: Council Clears ₹52,000 cr of Defence Proposals
Summary: The Defence Acquisition Council (DAC) has approved procurement proposals worth ₹52,000 crore, incorporating lessons from Operation Sindoor, to acquire advanced defense systems. These acquisitions, a significant portion of which will be fulfilled by India's domestic industry, include pseudo satellites, jet-based drones, and air defense systems, aiming to enhance intelligence, survivability, and combat capabilities for the Air Force, Army, and Navy. Specific projects involve high-altitude pseudo satellites, upgraded T-90 tanks, indigenous anti-tank missiles, 'Akash Tarang' electronic warfare systems, and naval unmanned aerial systems.
Content:
New Delhi: The defence ministry on Friday cleared a slew of procurements ranging from pseudo satellites to jet-based drones and air defence systems, with the armed forces incorporating lessons learnt from Operation Sindoor into the acquisition roadmap. The Rajnath Singh-led Defence Acquisition Council (DAC) accorded in-principle approval to proposals worth ₹52,000 crore, most of which will be fulfilled by the domestic industry. These projects, worth ₹52,000 crore, include pseudo satellites, air defence systems, and jet-based drones, with most acquisitions to be fulfilled by the domestic industry, incorporating lessons from Operation Sindoor.

Among the proposals cleared is the acquisition of fixed-wing high altitude pseudo satellites for the Indian Air Force. The system consists of a drone that flies at extremely high altitude for durations extended to weeks, powered by solar energy. The system is used to carry out seamless intelligence gathering and surveillance, besides long-range communications. At least two Indian manufacturers have been working on developing pseudo satellites, including state-owned National Aerospace Laboratories and private sector drone manufacturer NewSpace Research and Technologies.

For the army, a major project has been cleared to upgrade T-90 main battle tanks. Under the ₹9,000 crore plan, the fleet of tanks will be equipped with active protection systems. The systems significantly enhance the survivability of tanks in battle, with explosive countermeasures being deployed against threats such as rocket propelled grenades, anti-tank missiles and drones. Also for the army, the DAC cleared a proposal to acquire indigenous man portable anti-tank guided missile systems, valued at ₹2,300 crore. The systems have been developed by the Defence Research and Development Organisation and are likely to be produced by Bharat Dynamics Limited and private sector partners.

On the air defence front, three major systems have been cleared for the army. These include the indigenous anti-unmanned aerial vehicles electronic warfare system 'Akash Tarang'. For protection against missiles and combat aircraft, the army will also get additional medium range surface-to-air missile weapon systems. A large number of Russian origin 'Verba' shoulder fired anti-air missiles are also being procured. A very short range air defence system is likely to be produced by Adani Defence.

Adding to the growing drone arsenal, the DAC also cleared the acquisition of jet-based Kamikaze Drone System. "These drones provide better electronic warfare capability with greater lethality and survivability while also being cost-effective," said an official.

For the navy, projects that have been cleared include a new naval shipborne unmanned aerial system—drones that can be launched at sea to significantly enhance situation awareness. The navy will also get new sea mines under the Multi-Influence Ground Mine project, besides an approval to set up a land-based testing facility for under-development electric propulsion system.

Heading: Attack by Congress leader Jairam Ramesh: The series of government bowing before China continues
Summary: Congress leader Jairam Ramesh has criticized the Modi government, accusing it of continuously bowing to China, leading to a record trade deficit and harm to India's MSME sector. He also raised concerns about China's provocative actions in Arunachal Pradesh, a large hydropower project on the Brahmaputra, and India's alleged abandonment of patrolling rights in Eastern Ladakh. Ramesh further highlighted the "clean chit" given to China after the 2020 Ladakh clash and China's acknowledged role in Pakistan's actions during Operation Sindoor.
Content: DELHI, NAVBHARAT BUREAU. Senior Congress leader Jairam Ramesh has accused the Modi government of "continuously bowing" before China. He said that due to the government's policies, India's trade deficit with China has reached a record level, which is destroying large industries including the country's MSME sector. Congress leader Jairam Ramesh, while mentioning China's provocative actions regarding Arunachal Pradesh, said that these are still ongoing. He also expressed concern over the world's largest hydropower project being built in Medog and said that this puts India's water security regarding the Brahmaputra river at risk. Eastern Ladakh issue raised Raising the issue of Eastern Ladakh, Ramesh alleged that India has abandoned its traditional patrolling and grazing rights in many areas. He also recalled the Prime Minister's statement after the martyrdom of 20 Indian soldiers in Ladakh on June 19, 2020, saying that even then China was publicly given a "clean chit". Jairam Ramesh further said that during Operation Sindoor, the Deputy Chief of Army Staff had admitted China's important role in Pakistan's actions, and this is recorded in documents.

Heading: Defense procurement worth 52 thousand crores, power will increase with drone-missile systems
Summary: India's Defense Acquisition Council has approved weapon procurement worth Rs 52,000 crore, significantly boosting the armed forces' combat capabilities across land, air, and sea. This includes advanced Kamikaze drones, anti-tank guided missile systems, multi-influence ground mines for the Navy, and high-altitude pseudo satellites for enhanced air reconnaissance. The approvals also reflect lessons from "Operation Sindoor," prioritizing anti-drone systems due to their extensive use in conflicts.
Content: New Delhi. The strength of the Indian armed forces will further increase from land to sky and sea. The forces will get advanced drones like Kamikaze and shoulder-fired anti-tank guided missile systems. In a meeting of the Defense Acquisition Council (DAC) chaired by Defense Minister Rajnath Singh on Friday, proposals for the purchase of weapons worth about Rs 52,000 crore were given in-principle approval. Its purpose is to increase the combat capability of the armed forces. According to the Ministry of Defense, for the Army, the Anti-Unmanned Aerial Vehicle Electronic Warfare System Akash Tarang, shoulder-fired Anti-Tank Guided Missile System (MPATGM), Medium Range Surface-to-Air Missile System (MRSAM), Very Short Range Air Defense System (VSHORADS), and Kamikaze drone systems, considered deadly for tanks, have been approved for purchase. Akash Tarang will disrupt the communication of enemy drones and will disrupt navigation systems, reducing their effectiveness. Shoulder-fired missile systems will enhance the infantry's ability to deal with threats from enemy armor and artillery. VSHORADS will strengthen the Army's response capability and impact. Kamikaze drones, also known as suicide drones, will increase lethality. These low-cost drones hover over the target for some time and then crash into it, exploding. Will get landmines The Navy will get Multi-Influence Ground Mines to maintain supremacy in the sea. These are modern landmines laid on the surface of the sea. As soon as they come under their influence, enemy warships or submarines will be destroyed. In addition, high-tech drone shipborne unmanned aerial systems will be purchased for deployment on naval vessels. These will fly from the sea and keep an eye on enemy activities hundreds of kilometers away. Modern testing labs will also be built for checking ships and motors. First meeting after changes at top military level This was the first DAC meeting after the changes. Recently, General Raja Subramaniam took charge as CDS General Dheeraj Seth as Army Chief and Admiral Krishna Swaminathan as Navy Chief. Pseudo Satellite for air security A big decision has been taken to take the reconnaissance and communication capabilities of the Air Force to new heights. Under this, the purchase of fixed-wing based High Altitude Pseudo Satellite has been approved. This is a satellite-like unmanned platform that can stay at very high altitudes for several weeks or months. This will provide the Air Force with continuous intelligence surveillance, telecommunications, and remote sensing capabilities. With its help, effective long-term monitoring of border areas will be possible. Impact of Operation Sindoor The latest approvals make it clear how Operation Sindoor has influenced the Army's acquisition priorities. Drones and loitering munitions were widely used by both sides in the conflict with Pakistan. Keeping this in mind, the purchase of the anti-drone Akash Tarang system has been prioritized for the Army.

The capability boost approved by the council — India's apex defence procurement body — covers procuring a raft of systems, from anti-unmanned aerial vehicle (anti-UAV) electronic warfare system 'AKASH TARANG', man-portable anti-tank guided missile (MPATGM) systems to medium range surface-to-air missile (MRSAM) weapon system, the defence ministry said.

The DAC also accorded its Acceptance of Necessity (AoN) for buying the very short range air defence system (V-SHORADS), an active protection system for tanks, and a jet-based kamikaze drone system, the ministry added in a statement.

The military hardware listed above is for the army.

ACCEPTANCE OF NECESSITY BY THE COUNCIL IS THE FIRST STEP IN BUYING MILITARY EQUIPMENT

Under India's defence procurement rules, AoN by the council is the first step towards buying military equipment. It was for the first time the DAC convened after India's new military leadership took charge under chief of defence staff General NS Raja Subramani, navy chief Admiral Krishna Swaminathan and army chief General Dhiraj Seth. The top appointments were made recently.

Seth, who took over as army chief on June 30, said on Wednesday that the force's modernisation would form the bedrock of its transformation into a future-ready force.

The defence ministry outlined the capability boost: AKASH TARANG will provide effective anti-UAV protection to army formations; the MPATGM will enhance the infantry's potential to counter the adversary's mechanised threats; and the MRSAM system provides medium range air defence against various stand-off aerial threats.

"The V-SHORADS with multi-spectral sensing will enhance counter-measure resilience and effectiveness of the Indian Army. The active protection system will improve the defence mechanism of tanks and enhance their survivability. The jet-based kamikaze drones will provide better electronic warfare capability with greater lethality and survivability while also being cost effective," the ministry said.

The military hardware approved for the Navy includes the multi-influence ground mine (MIGM), the naval shipborne unmanned aerial system (NSUAS) and the establishment of a land-based testing facility (LBTF) for electric propulsion systems. "The MIGM will deny freedom of manoeuvre to the adversary. The NSUAS, equipped with advanced sensors, will enhance the Indian Navy's situational awareness. The LBTF will meet the testing requirements for motors and associated propulsion systems of the Indian naval assets," it said.

The Indian Air Force received approval to procure the fixed-wing based high altitude pseudo satellite (FW-HAPS). It will carry out intelligence, surveillance and reconnaissance (ISR), telecommunication and remote sensing for the air force, the ministry added.

In February, India hiked its defence spending by more than 15% against the backdrop of Operation Sindoor, setting aside ₹7.85 lakh crore for the critical sector in the Union Budget for 2026-27. This included a capital outlay of ₹2.19 lakh crore to boost the capabilities of the armed forces with new weapons and systems including fighter planes, transport aircraft, helicopters, war-ships, submarines, artillery guns, smart weapons, missiles, rockets and a variety of unmanned systems.

The decision has drawn strong political criticism, with the Congress party, through its general secretary Jairam Ramesh, accusing the Modi government of a "calibrated capitulation" to China. Ramesh highlighted a record trade deficit, the alleged allowance of Chinese power equipment manufacturers in critical Indian projects, and China's unabated provocative actions in Arunachal Pradesh, including the Medog hydroelectric project which imperils India's water security. Content:
The Finance Ministry has issued an order allowing four companies with Chinese ownership or links to bid for projects tendered by the Indian government in the power sector, a move seen as a continuing thaw in India's stance on Chinese investments. The order, dated June 24, 2026, was issued by the Procurement Policy Division of the Finance Ministry's Expenditure Department and specifies that this exemption is valid for two years and should not be treated as a precedent.

This decision follows a request from the Power Ministry in January, which had sought an exemption from a previous order mandating that companies located in countries sharing a land border with India must register with the Indian government before bidding for critical public power projects. The approval of this registration was solely at the discretion of the government. Following this, the Committee of Secretaries and the Registration Committee under the Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT) deliberated on the matter before passing the relaxation order.

The four companies granted exemption are TBEA Energy India, Nanjing Electric India, New Northeast Electric India, and Taikai Electric (India). TBEA Energy India is a wholly-owned subsidiary of the Chinese company TBEA Group, while Nanjing Electric India is a wholly-owned subsidiary of the Chinese power equipment manufacturer Nanjing Electric. New Northeast Electric India has technology transfer ties with Chinese power sector companies, and Taikai Electric (India) is a subsidiary of the China-headquartered Taikai Group. The Procurement Policy Division's order, however, made sure to state that “such exemption for firms may not be considered as a precedent.”

This order also builds on other partial relaxations the government has recently offered to companies with investments from China and other countries sharing a land border with India. In May, the Finance Ministry had notified new rules to allow overseas companies with Chinese shareholding of up to 10% to invest in India under the automatic route, rather than first having to obtain government approval. This was a relaxation made to the ‘Press Note 3’ that the Indian government had issued in 2020, ostensibly to prevent opportunistic takeovers and acquisitions of distressed Indian companies due to the COVID-19 pandemic.

However, the Congress on Friday slammed the Union government's decision, alleging that its "calibrated capitulation" to China is continuing even as India's trade deficit with that country reaches record levels, "destroying large sections of industry." Congress general secretary Jairam Ramesh shared a media report on X which highlighted that India had allowed four Chinese power equipment manufacturers with factories in the country to participate in government tenders for critical power projects. In his post, Mr. Ramesh stated, "The Modi Government's calibrated capitulation to China continues even as India's trade deficit with that country reaches record levels destroying large sections of our industry specially MSMEs."

Mr. Ramesh further criticized China's unabated "provocative actions" in relation to Arunachal Pradesh and the ongoing construction of the world's largest hydroelectric project in Medog, which he claimed imperils India's water security in relation to the Brahmaputra. He also alleged that India's traditional patrolling and herding rights in many places in Eastern Ladakh have been given up. The Congress leader recalled that Prime Minister Narendra Modi "infamously gave a public clean chit" to China on June 19, 2020, even after 20 of India's armed forces personnel were martyred in Ladakh. He also pointed out that China's pivotal role in Pakistan's actions during Operation Sindoor was acknowledged by the Deputy Chief of Army Staff and is documented, adding, "And yet, the 'capitulation' to China continues apace."

Content:
NEW DELHI: The External Affairs Ministry on Friday stated that the Indus Waters Treaty (IWT) will remain in “abeyance” until Pakistan “credibly and irrevocably” ceases its support for cross-border terrorism. This statement was made by Randhir Jaiswal, Official Spokesperson of the External Affairs Ministry, in response to a recent international conference in Pakistan. During this conference, the Government of Pakistan had called for the restoration of the IWT, citing the country's severe heatwave.

Mr. Jaiswal, at a media briefing, explicitly stated, “The Indus Waters Treaty of 1960 will be held in abeyance with immediate effect, until Pakistan credibly and irrevocably abjures its support for cross border terrorism.” Earlier in the week, Pakistan had organized a conference on the Indus river and water sharing, where its Foreign Minister and Deputy Prime Minister Ishaq Dar emphasized the IWT's importance for “regional peace, stability and cooperation.”

India’s Cabinet Committee on Security had initially put the IWT in “abeyance” on April 23, 2025, a day after the Pahalagam terror attack on April 22, 2025, which resulted in the deaths of 26 civilians and injured dozens more. This attack subsequently led to India’s strikes on terror targets inside Pakistan under Operation Sindoor.

On May 13, 2025, Mr. Jaiswal elaborated, “The IWT was concluded in the spirit of goodwill and friendship as specified in the preamble of the treaty. However, Pakistan has held these principles in abeyance by its promotion of cross-border terrorism for decades.” He further added, “Please also note that climate change, demographic shifts and technological changes have created new realities on the ground.”

More recently, on May 22, 2025, Mr. Jaiswal had indicated India’s willingness to discuss with Pakistan the modality to gain custody of “noted terrorists whose list was provided to Pakistan some years ago.” Citing Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s remarks, Mr. Jaiswal had previously stated, “Water and blood cannot flow together.” India has intensified its criticism of Pakistan in recent weeks, particularly against the backdrop of protests and police crackdowns in Pakistan-occupied Kashmir.

Heading: Centre opens power bids to four China-linked firms
Summary: The Indian government has eased procurement restrictions, allowing four Chinese-linked companies to bid for power projects for two years, a move signaling a potential thaw in India's stance on Chinese investments and building on earlier relaxations like allowing up to 10% Chinese shareholding under the automatic route. This decision, made by the Finance Ministry after Power Ministry requests and inter-ministerial consultations, is not to be considered a precedent. However, the Congress party has criticized the Modi government for "calibrated capitulation" to China, citing a record trade deficit harming Indian industry, China's provocative actions in Arunachal Pradesh, concerns over a Chinese hydroelectric project on the Brahmaputra, and alleged surrender of India's patrolling rights in Eastern Ladakh.
Content:
The Finance Ministry has issued an order allowing four companies with Chinese ownership or links to bid for projects tendered by the Indian government in the power sector. This decision, dated June 24, 2026, follows a request from the Power Ministry for an exemption from a previous order that mandated re-registration for companies from countries sharing a land border with India before bidding for critical public power projects. The exemption, valid for two years, is not to be treated as a precedent, according to the Procurement Policy Division of the Finance Ministry’s Expenditure Department. The four companies granted this exemption are TBEA Energy India, Nanjing Electric India, New Northeast Electric India, and Taikai Electric (India), all of which have significant Chinese ties. This order builds on earlier partial relaxations, such as the May notification allowing overseas companies with up to 10% Chinese shareholding to invest in India under the automatic route, a change from the 2020 'Press Note 3' aimed at preventing opportunistic takeovers during the COVID-19 pandemic.

However, this move has drawn sharp criticism from the Congress party. On Friday, the Congress alleged that the Union government's "calibrated capitulation" to China is continuing, even as India's trade deficit with China reaches record levels, "destroying large sections of industry," particularly MSMEs. Congress general secretary Jairam Ramesh shared a media report on X highlighting India's decision to allow Chinese power equipment manufacturers to participate in government tenders. Mr. Ramesh further stated that China's provocative actions in relation to Arunachal Pradesh remain unabated, and the world's largest hydroelectric project in Medog continues, imperilling India's water security concerning the Brahmaputra. He also claimed that India's traditional patrolling and herding rights in many places in Eastern Ladakh have been given up. Mr. Ramesh recalled Prime Minister Narendra Modi's "infamous public clean chit" to China on June 19, 2020, following the martyrdom of 20 Indian armed forces personnel in Ladakh, and noted China's acknowledged pivotal role in Pakistan's actions during Operation Sindoor. He concluded by asserting that despite these issues, the "capitulation" to China continues apace.

Summary: The Congress party has criticized the Modi government's China policy, alleging a 'systematic surrender' and highlighting a record trade deficit that negatively impacts Indian industries. Congress General Secretary Jairam Ramesh pointed to Chinese companies' participation in Indian government projects and ongoing Chinese activities in Arunachal Pradesh and Tibet as evidence of a soft stance. He also criticized PM Modi's 'clean chit' to China after the Galwan incident and China's alleged role in Pakistan's activities.
Content: Congress has once again attacked the central government over its China policy. Congress General Secretary (Communications) Jairam Ramesh alleged on Friday that the Modi government's policy of 'systematic surrender' towards China continues, while India's trade deficit with China has reached a record level, and micro, small and medium enterprises are particularly affected by this. Ramesh shared a post on X, stating that according to recent reports, four Chinese companies with manufacturing units in India have been allowed to participate in tenders for some important government power projects. He called this an example of the government's soft policy towards China. The Congress leader alleged that China's activities regarding Arunachal Pradesh are continuously ongoing. He said that the construction of the world's largest hydroelectric project in Tibet's Medog region could pose a threat to India's water security related to the Brahmaputra river. He also claimed that India's traditional patrolling and grazing rights have been affected in several areas of eastern Ladakh. Jairam Ramesh also criticized Prime Minister Narendra Modi's statement of June 19, 2020, referring to the 2020 Galwan Valley incident. He said that after 20 Indian soldiers were martyred, the Prime Minister publicly gave a 'clean chit' to China. He also claimed that China played a significant role in Pakistan's activities during Operation Sindoor, which was mentioned by the Deputy Army Chief. Despite this, the government has adopted a soft stance towards China. The Congress leader said that on one hand, India's trade deficit with China is continuously increasing, and on the other hand, the government's recent decisions raise serious questions about its policy towards China.

Heading: TOP DEFENCE PANEL APPROVES ACQUISITION WORTH ₹52,000 CR
Summary: The Defence Acquisition Council (DAC), chaired by Defence Minister Rajnath Singh, has approved capital acquisition proposals totaling ₹52,000 crore. These acquisitions, influenced by Operation Sindoor and recent hostilities with Pakistan, reflect a strategic shift towards advanced systems for enhanced national security, prioritizing counter-drone systems, layered air defence, anti-tank weapons, and surveillance platforms. Key approvals include the indigenous 'Akash-Tarang' anti-UAV/EW system, 2,300 indigenous man-portable anti-tank guided missiles with 100 launchers and 5 simulators, MR-SAMs, and a Fixed-Wing Based High Altitude Pseudo Satellite for persistent intelligence.
Content:
JAVARIA RANA @New Delhi
The Defence Acquisition Council (DAC) on Friday cleared capital acquisition proposals worth around ₹52,000 crore, with counter-drone systems, layered air defence, anti-tank weapons and persistent surveillance platforms emerging as the biggest priorities in the armed forces' latest modernisation push. Chaired by Defence Minister Rajnath Singh, the DAC granted the "acceptance of necessity" for the projects. The proposals will now go through tendering, technical evaluation and cost negotiations, with the high-value ones also needing the Cabinet Committee on Security (CCS) nod, before contracts are eventually inked. The DAC meeting was also the first after Gen Raja Subramani took over as Chief of Defence Staff, Gen Dhiraj Seth as Army chief and Adm Krishna Swaminathan as Navy chief. The latest approvals also point to the way Operation Sindoor has influenced the military's acquisition priorities. The hostilities with Pakistan, in which drones and loitering munitions slugged it out with air defence networks on both sides, has forced the shift away from big-ticket conventional platforms towards counter-UAV systems, layered air defence, better tank survivability and round-the-clock intelligence, surveillance and reconnaissance (ISR). The Army cornered the biggest chunk of approvals. Topping its list is the indigenous 'Akash-Tarang', an anti-UAV electronic warfare (EW) system built to detect, track and jam hostile drones. The DAC also cleared 2,300 indigenous man-portable anti-tank guided missiles (MPAT-GMs), along with 100 launchers and five simulators, for around ₹2,600 crore, sources said. Developed by DRDO for production by state-run Bharat Dynamics, the third-generation, fire-and-forget missile packs an imaging infrared seeker, tandem warhead and top-attack capability to take out modern tanks and will progressively replace the vintage Milan and Konkurs ATGMs. Additional Medium Range Surface-to-Air Missile (MR-SAM) systems and shoulder-fired Verba VSHORADS, the fourth-generation Russian MANPADS, to be manufactured in India by Adani Defence under transfer of technology from Rosoboronexport, were also cleared. The package also includes Active Protection Systems (APS) and a jet-based kamikaze drone system for longer-range precision strikes. For the Navy, the DAC cleared the Multi-Influence Ground Mine (MIGM), a Naval Ship-borne Unmanned Aerial System (NSUAS) and a land-based testing facility for electric propulsion. For the IAF, the headline approval is the Fixed-Wing Based High Altitude Pseudo Satellite (FW-HAPS), a solar-powered platform built to loiter in the stratosphere for weeks on end to deliver persistent ISR. The DAC cleared other IAF proposals also, without specifying. |P7

Heading: Defense Allocation
Summary: The Indian government, led by PM Modi, is focusing on strengthening defense capabilities against Pakistan and China, emphasizing self-reliance. The Defense Acquisition Council, chaired by Rajnath Singh, has approved the procurement of defense equipment worth ₹42,000 crore for the Army, Navy, and Air Force, including advanced missiles, drones, and surveillance systems.
Content: New Delhi: Emphasis on defense to counter Pakistan and China. Also on crucial self-reliance. Keeping these dual objectives in mind, Prime Minister Narendra Modi's government is set to begin efforts to procure new weapons in the next phase of 'Operation Sindoor'. In this context, the Defense Acquisition Council, chaired by Rajnath Singh on Friday, has approved the purchase of defense equipment worth ₹42,000 crore to strengthen the military capabilities of the Indian Army, Navy, and Air Force through advanced missiles, drones, and surveillance systems.

Heading: TOP DEFENCE PANEL APPROVES ACQUISITION WORTH ₹52,000 CRORE
Summary: The Defence Acquisition Council (DAC), chaired by Defence Minister Rajnath Singh, approved major capital acquisition proposals valued at approximately ₹52,000 crore during a meeting held on Friday. These approvals, made under the new military leadership, prioritize critical systems such as counter-drone technology, layered air defence, and surveillance platforms to modernize India's armed forces. A significant focus is placed on indigenous development and technology transfer for various systems across the Army, Navy, and Air Force, with the acquisitions influenced by recent hostilities with Pakistan and the emphasized need for advanced counter-UAV and ISR capabilities.
Content:
The Defence Acquisition Council (DAC) meeting on Friday cleared major capital acquisition proposals worth around ₹52,000 crore. JAVARIA RANA @ New Delhi. The Defence Acquisition Council (DAC) on Friday cleared capital acquisition proposals worth around ₹52,000 crore, with counter-drone systems, layered air defence, anti-tank weapons and persistent surveillance platforms emerging as the biggest priorities in the armed forces' latest modernisation push. Chaired by defence minister Rajnath Singh, the DAC granted the "acceptance of necessity" for the projects. The proposals will now go through tendering, technical evaluation and cost negotiations, with the high-value ones also needing the Cabinet Committee on Security (CCS) nod, before contracts are eventually inked. The DAC meeting was also the first after Gen Raja Subramani took over as Chief of Defence Staff, Gen Dhiraj Seth as Army chief and Adm Krishna Swaminathan as Navy chief. The latest approvals also point to the way Operation Sindoor has influenced the military's acquisition priorities. The hostilities with Pakistan, in which drones and loitering munitions slugged it out with air defence networks on both sides, has forced the shift away from big-ticket conventional platforms towards counter-UAV systems, layered air defence, better tank survivability and round-the-clock intelligence, surveillance and reconnaissance (ISR).

The Army cornered the biggest chunk of approvals. Topping its list is the indigenous 'Akash-Tarang', an anti-UAV electronic warfare (EW) system built to detect, track and jam hostile drones. The DAC also cleared 2,300 indigenous man-portable antitank guided missiles (MPATGMs), along with 100 launchers and five simulators, for around ₹2,600 crore, sources said. Developed by DRDO for production by state-run Bharat Dynamics, the third-generation, fire-and-forget missile packs an imaging infrared seeker, tandem warhead and top-attack capability to put out modern tanks and will progressively replace the vintage Milan and Konkurs ATGMs in infantry units. Additional Medium Range Surface-to-Air Missile (MRSAM) systems and shoulder-fired Verba VSHORADS, the fourth-generation Russian MANPADS, to be manufactured in India by Adani Defence under transfer of technology from Rosoboronexport, were also cleared. The package also includes Active Protection Systems (APS) and a jet-based kamikaze drone system for longer-range precision strikes.

For the Navy, the DAC cleared the Multi-Influence Ground Mine (MIGM), a Naval Shipborne Unmanned Aerial System (NSUAS) and a land-based testing facility for electric propulsion. For the IAF, the headline approval is the Fixed-Wing Based High Altitude Pseudo Satellite (FW-HAPS), a solar-powered platform built to loiter in the stratosphere for weeks on end to deliver persistent ISR. The DAC cleared other IAF proposals also, without specifying.

Heading: Politics over martyrdom in Operation Sindoor is against national interest
Summary: The article criticizes political opportunism surrounding the martyrdom of six soldiers in 'Operation Sindoor', an anti-terror campaign against Pakistan in May 2025. It defends the Modi government's actions and statements, particularly Defence Minister Rajnath Singh's clarification in Parliament on July 28, 2025, that no Indian soldiers were harmed, which was later clarified by the Defence Ministry to be a response to misleading propaganda. The article emphasizes that politicizing such sacrifices is against national interest and highlights the government's commitment to honoring the fallen soldiers whose names are etched in the National War Memorial.
Content: Manoj Kumar Agarwal Even the world's most powerful nation cannot claim in an attack or war that damage occurred only unilaterally. Regardless of how highly trained and equipped with state-of-the-art facilities and resources a military force may be, some loss of life and property is natural. This should neither question the strength of the army nor is it appropriate to blame the government. In 'Operation Sindoor', six soldiers were martyred, whose names have now been made public by the Modi government a year later. The names of the six martyred soldiers are etched in the National War Memorial. The spirit of putting one's life on the line and making the supreme sacrifice for the defense and self-respect of the country cannot be praised enough in words, nor can adequate gratitude be expressed. Martyrdom is martyrdom; it is not just a matter of a single soldier's life; the honor of the entire nation is attached to it. There should be no political debate or controversy over martyrdom. However, the issue-less opposition wants to find an excuse to corner the Modi government, and perhaps that is why controversial statements are being made about martyrdom, disregarding national honor and national interest. In fact, during the parliamentary session on July 28, 2025, during a debate on Operation Sindoor in the Lok Sabha, Minister Rajnath Singh had told the opposition, "If you want to ask a question, ask if any of our brave soldiers suffered any casualties in this operation, and the answer is no." A video of the Defence Minister's statement is circulating on social media, in which it is heard that he emphasized the word 'no', and then Home Minister Amit Shah and all BJP MPs present in the house welcomed this statement with laughter. It is being said that upon hearing this statement, it is understood that Rajnath Singh is clearly saying that our soldiers suffered no harm. Rajnath Singh further stated in the same speech, "Opposition people kept asking how many planes we shot down; I think this question does not correctly represent national sentiment. They never once asked how many enemy planes our forces shot down. If they have to ask a question, it should be whether India destroyed terrorist hideouts, and the answer is yes. If you have to ask a question, ask if Operation Sindoor was successful, and the answer is yes." In reality, only the army deserves praise for whatever it does, not any political party. Anyway, when the Defence Minister said that no soldier was harmed, it was understood that India caused significant damage to Pakistan in Operation Sindoor, but the country suffered no loss. Although Pakistan sometimes claimed to have shot down fighter jets and killed more than 10 soldiers, these claims were not taken seriously. Certainly, no country publicizes its losses during war or conflict; all opposing countries exaggerate the enemy's losses. Now that the names of six soldiers have come out, the opposition has started criticizing. Congress leader Pawan Khera said that 'Parliament was misled' regarding India's retaliatory action against Pakistan after the Pulwama attack. Mr. Khera wrote on X, 'There are only two possibilities: either the Defence Minister was unaware of the facts related to his own ministry, which raises a 'serious question' about his competence, or he knew the truth and still decided to 'mislead Parliament'.' He wrote, 'The government that wraps itself in the tricolor and does not talk about nationalism did not give these brave men the respect and remembrance they deserved.' Pawan Khera said, 'The names of these brave men should have been etched in the collective memory of the nation forever. Their families should have felt that the entire nation was remembering their sacrifice with honor. But instead, for a whole year, the BJP government decided to hide their martyrdom from the country.' Similar statements were made by other parties, so now the Ministry of Defence has clarified that 'some social media posts are trying to misrepresent the speech given by the Defence Minister in Parliament on July 28, 2025. These posts selectively pick a small part of the misleading statement to falsely claim that the Defence Minister said no Indian soldier died during Operation Sindoor. This claim was deliberately presented in a misleading manner and is completely factually incorrect.' It should be remembered that when the Defence Minister was giving his speech in Parliament, at that time, some sections of the media and social media were constantly spreading false propaganda that Indian Air Force pilots were killed during Operation Sindoor. This claim was completely false, but it was continuously spread with the aim of downplaying the success of the operation and demoralizing the public. The Defence Minister's related statement was given in response to this specific and misleading propaganda. Therefore, his statement should be understood in that context. The Ministry of Defence's statement further said that 'this speech was meant to honor the courage and capability of the Indian armed forces and was a clear message to those trying to harm India.' Let us tell you that Operation Sindoor was a campaign launched against Pakistan in May 2025 in response to the Pulwama terrorist attack, in which 5 Army personnel and 1 Air Force personnel were martyred. Their names are included in the 'Roll of Honor' on the National War Memorial website. The opposition is presenting the government's release of names as 'insult to martyrs' and 'lying in Parliament'. 'The Defence Minister and the Government of India are fully committed to expressing respect, gratitude, and reverence for every member of the Indian armed forces. Especially for those brave soldiers who made the supreme sacrifice while defending the nation.' In honor of this supreme sacrifice, the government has ensured that the names of these brave soldiers are inscribed on the walls of the National War Memorial. The Ministry of Defence said it is clarified that these martyred heroes were honored much before these news reports came out. On May 11, 2025, the then Director General of Military Operations paid heartfelt tributes to these brave soldiers. Their sacrifice during duty in Operation Sindoor was also recognized. These brave soldiers were awarded gallantry awards. This information was published in a press release on August 14, 2025. (Author: Senior Journalist)

Heading: DEFENCE MINISTRY CLEARS ₹52K-CR PROCUREMENT PROPOSALS NATION
Summary: The Defence Ministry has approved defense acquisitions worth ₹52,000 crore, a significant step towards strengthening national defense and bolstering military capabilities. These procurements include counter-UAV systems for the Army, pseudo-satellite based surveillance for the Indian Air Force (drawing lessons from the standoff with China), shipborne unmanned aerial systems for the Navy, jet-powered kamikaze drones, anti-tank guided missiles, and various air defense systems, all aimed at significantly enhancing India's intelligence, surveillance, reconnaissance, and defense capabilities against modern threats.
Content: Approval also granted for pseudo satellite-based surveillance for IAF AJAY BANERJEE TRIBUNE NEWS SERVICE NEW DELHI, JULY 3 Drawing lessons from Operation Sindoor and the military standoff with China, the Defence Ministry on Friday approved a counter-UAV system for the Army and a pseudo satellite-based surveillance platform for the Indian Air Force. A shipborne unmanned aerial system for the Navy and a new category of jet-powered kamikaze drones for the Army were also cleared by the Defence Acquisition Council (DAC), the apex procurement body of the ministry. The DAC, chaired by Defence Minister Rajnath Singh, accorded Acceptance of Necessity (AoN) — the first stage of the acquisition process and an in-principle administrative approval — for proposals worth Rs 52,000 crore. For the Indian Air Force, approval was granted for the procurement of High-Altitude Pseudo-Satellites (HAPS), which will provide persistent intelligence, surveillance and reconnaissance (ISR), telecommunications and remote-sensing capabilities. For the Army, the Defence Acquisition Council approved the procurement of the Akash Tarang anti-UAV system. REPRESENTATIVE PIC The HAPS platforms will feature fixed wings similar to aircraft and will be powered by solar energy and onboard batteries. They are essentially ultra-long-endurance unmanned aerial vehicles that operate in the strato-sphere, typically at an alti-tude of 20 km. A pseudo-satellite flies high enough to perform many functions associated with a geostationary satellite, remaining over a designated geographical area for weeks or even months at a time, but at a fraction of the cost of launching a satellite into space. Unlike conventional satellites, which eventually burn up or become space debris, HAPS can return to base, land on a runway and be redeployed. For the Army, the DAC approved the procurement of the Akash Tarang anti-UAV system, an electronic warfare platform designed to neutralise incoming drones. The Ministry of Defence said the system would provide effective anti-drone pro-tection to Army formations. Rather than relying solely on kinetic interception through guns or missiles, Akash Tarang employs radio-frequency jamming, spoofing and other electronic counter-measures to disrupt the command links and navigation signals of hostile drones. The DAC also approved the procurement of jet-powered kamikaze drones, along with man-portable anti-tank guided missile (MPATGM) systems, medium-range surface-to-air missile (MRSAM) systems and very short-range air defence systems (V-SHORADS). The MPATGM will strengthen infantry units' ability to counter armoured and mechanised threats. The MRSAM system will provide medium-range air defence against a range of aerial threats, while the V-SHORADS will enhance the Army's close-range air defence capability. For the Navy, the DAC approved the procurement of Naval Shipborne Unmanned Aerial Systems (NSUAS). Equipped with advanced sen-sors, these platforms are expected to significantly improve the Navy's situa-tional awareness and surveil-lance capabilities.

Heading: ANTI-DRONE SYSTEMS, MRSAM, KAMIKAZE DRONES - Centre clears Rs 52,000 cr defence procurement push for armed forces
Summary: The Indian Defence Ministry, through its Defence Acquisition Council chaired by Minister Rajnath Singh, has approved capital acquisition proposals totaling Rs 52,000 crore. These significant procurements are aimed at enhancing the operational capabilities and strengthening the multi-layered defense architecture of the Army, Navy, and Air Force. The approvals prioritize indigenous systems, including anti-drone technology, MRSAM, anti-tank missile systems, air defense systems, kamikaze drones, naval mines, and surveillance platforms, to bolster India's preparedness against modern battlefield threats, enhance force protection, and facilitate a transition to technology-driven warfare, thereby boosting domestic manufacturing and reducing reliance on imported military equipment.
Content: NEW DELHI: With modern warfare increasingly shaped by drones, precision-guided weapons and advanced air defence systems, the Defence Ministry on Friday approved capital acquisition proposals worth about Rs 52,000 crore to strengthen the operational capability of the armed forces. The Defence Acquisition Council (DAC), chaired by Defence Minister Rajnath Singh, accorded Acceptance of Necessity (AoN) for a range of indigenous systems for the Army, Navy and Air Force. The approvals are aimed at enhancing India's preparedness against emerging battlefield threats while boosting the induction of domestically developed defence equipment. For the Indian Army, the DAC cleared procurement of the Anti-Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV) Electronic Warfare System 'Akash Tarang', Man Portable Anti-Tank Guided Missile (MPATGM) systems, Medium Range Surface-to-Air Missile (MRSAM) weapon system, Very Short Range Air Defence System (V-SHORADS), Active Protection System (APS) for tanks and a jet-based kamikaze drone system. The Akash Tarang system is designed to detect, track, jam and disrupt hostile drones used for surveillance, reconnaissance and precision strikes. It is expected to provide protection to military bases, strategic assets, critical infrastructure and border areas against the growing threat posed by unmanned aerial systems and drone swarms. The MPATGM system will enhance the Army's capability to engage enemy tanks and armoured vehicles at short and medium ranges. The missile system is intended to provide greater mobility to infantry units operating in mountainous, desert and urban terrain while reducing dependence on imported anti-tank weapons. The MRSAM weapon system provides air defence against fighter aircraft, helicopters, drones, cruise missiles and precision-guided munitions. Jointly developed by the Defence Research and Development Organisation (DRDO) and Israel Aerospace Industries (IAI), the Barak-8-based system formed a key part of India's air defence network during Operation Sindoor, intercepting aerial threats as part of a layered defence architecture. The Army will also induct the V-SHORADS, which provides por-table air defence against low-fly-ing aircraft, helicopters and drones, particularly in frontline, high-alti-tude and border areas. The coun-cil further approved procurement of the Active Protection System for tanks, which detects and intercepts incoming anti-tank guided mis-siles, rocket-propelled grenades and loitering munitions before they strike, improving the survivability of armoured formations against mod-ern anti-armour threats. The approved jet-based kamikaze drone system will provide the Army with a high-speed precision strike capability against high-value targets, including air defence systems, radar stations, command centres, ammu-nition depots and logistics hubs. Owing to its higher speed, the sys-tem is expected to be more difficult to intercept than conventional pro-peller-driven loitering munitions. For the Indian Navy, the DAC approved procurement of the Multi Influence Ground Mine (MIGM), Naval Shipborne Unmanned Aerial System (NSUAS) and the establish-ment of a Land Based Testing Facil-ity (LBTF) for electric propulsion systems. The MIGM is an advanced sea-bed mine that detects enemy war-ships and submarines through a combination of magnetic, acous-tic and pressure signatures before engaging them. The system is intended to strengthen sea denial capabilities while protecting ports, naval bases and key maritime routes in the Indian Ocean Region. The NSUAS is designed to oper-ate from naval warships, extending surveillance beyond a ship's radar horizon and providing real-time intelligence. It will also support anti-piracy, anti-smuggling and maritime security operations. The proposed Land Based Testing Facility will enable shore-based testing of electric propulsion systems and other criti-cal technologies before they are inte-grated into operational warships. For the Indian Air Force, the council approved procurement of the Fixed-Wing High Altitude Pseudo Satellite (FW-HAPS) and other proposals. The FW-HAPS platform is intended to provide per-sistent intelligence, surveillance and reconnaissance capabilities, besides supporting telecommunications and remote sensing missions over extended durations. According to defence experts, the approved acquisitions address emerging battlefield challenges by strengthening India's multi-lay-ered defence architecture, improv-ing force protection and precision strike capability, and supporting the armed forces' transition towards technology-driven and network-centric warfare. The approvals also align with the government's contin-ued focus on expanding indigenous defence manufacturing and reducing dependence on imported military equipment.

Heading: Cong alleges Centre's 'capitulation' to China amid rising trade deficit and border concerns
Summary: The Congress has accused the Narendra Modi government of "capitulation" to China, citing a rising trade deficit and ongoing border tensions as evidence of a failed approach. Congress leader Jairam Ramesh alleged that the government's policies have weakened India's strategic and economic interests, pointing to China's aggressive posture and its role in supporting Pakistan. The opposition also criticized the Prime Minister's remarks after the 2020 Galwan Valley clash and the continued expansion of bilateral trade despite these concerns.
Content: STATESMAN NEWS SERVICE New Delhi, 3 July The Congress on Friday accused the Narendra Modi government of pursuing a policy of “capitulation” towards China despite mounting strategic and economic challenges, alleging that India’s record trade deficit with its northern neighbour and continuing border tensions reflected a failure of the Centre’s approach. In a statement, Congress general secretary in charge of communications, Jairam Ramesh claimed that the government’s policy towards China had weakened India’s strategic and economic interests. “The Modi govt’s calibrated capitulation to China continues even as India’s trade deficit with that country reaches record levels destroying large sections of our industry, especially MSMEs,” Ramesh said. The Congress leader alleged that China continues to adopt an aggressive posture along the border and undertake activities that affect India’s security and water resources. “China’s provocative actions regarding Arunachal Pradesh are unabated. The world’s largest hydroelectric project in Medog continues, imperilling India’s water security in relation to the Brahmaputra. India’s traditional patrolling and herding rights in many places in Eastern Ladakh have been given up,” he alleged. Referring to the 2020 border clash in eastern Ladakh, Ramesh renewed the Opposition’s criticism of Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s remarks following the Galwan Valley incident. “The Prime Minister infamously gave a public chit to China on 19 June, 2020 even after twenty of our brave armed forces personnel were martyred in Ladakh,” he said. Ramesh also referred to China’s alleged role in supporting Pakistan during Operation Sindoor, citing recent remarks by the Deputy Chief of Army Staff. “China’s pivotal role in Pakistan’s actions during Operation Sindoor was acknowledged by the Deputy Chief of Army Staff and is documented,” he added. “And yet the capitulation to China continues apace,” Ramesh added. The Congress has repeatedly criticised the Centre’s handling of relations with China since the military standoff that began in eastern Ladakh in 2020, alleging that the government has failed to adequately address border and economic concerns while allowing bilateral trade with China to expand. The Centre has consistently maintained that it is firmly safeguarding India’s territorial integrity, strengthening border infrastructure and pursuing diplomatic and military engagement to maintain peace and tranquillity along the Line of Actual Control, while taking measures to reduce strategic dependence on imports and promote domestic manufacturing.

Heading: Opposition's Statements on Martyrdom in Operation Sindoor
Summary: The article criticizes the opposition for politicizing the martyrdom of soldiers and misrepresenting the Defense Minister's statements regarding "Operation Sindoor." The piece emphasizes the need for national unity and respect for martyrs, urging the opposition to refrain from divisive rhetoric.
Content: No country, however powerful, can claim that there was only one-sided damage in any attack or war. Despite a military force being highly trained and equipped with state-of-the-art facilities and resources, loss of life is natural. This should neither question the strength of the army nor cast doubt on its combat skills, nor should the government be accused. Yet, some people see politics in everything, which the Modi government has now made public after clearing the names. The names of six martyred soldiers are etched in the National War Memorial. The spirit of putting one's life on the line and making the ultimate sacrifice for the defense and self-respect of the country cannot be praised enough. This does not represent the true national sentiment. They never once asked how many enemy planes our forces shot down. If they have to ask questions, their question should be whether India destroyed terrorist hideouts, and the answer is 'yes'. If you have to ask a question, ask if Operation Sindoor was successful, and the answer is 'yes'. In reality, whatever the army does deserves praise, not any political party. However, when the Defense Ministry had stated that no soldier was harmed, it was believed that India had inflicted damage on Pakistan in Operation Sindoor, but the country suffered no loss. Although Pakistan claimed to have shot down all fighter jets, sometimes killing more than 10 soldiers. But these claims were not taken seriously. Certainly, no country publicizes its losses during war or conflict; all opposing countries exaggerate the enemy's losses. Now that the names of six soldiers have come out, the opposition has started to criticize. Heading: The one who trapped the youth in a love affair was a 'transgender': Youth killed him by stoning him in Shapar to get rid of him
Summary: Police in Shapar, Rajkot, have solved the murder of an unknown male found near railway tracks, arresting 20-year-old Piyushkumar Bharatwar from Uttar Pradesh.
