Content: Staff Reporter | Rajkot A decomposed body of an unknown male, dressed in women's clothes, was found near the railway tracks in Shapar, causing a stir in the entire area. Police solved the mystery of the murder within five days and arrested the 20-year-old accused, Piyushkumar Bablu Bharatwar, from Uttar Pradesh. Behind this murder, a shocking story of homosexual relationships and three years of mental harassment has come to light. According to police sources, the accused Piyush, originally from UP and currently working in a pyramid factory in Padvala, was in Hyderabad three years ago when he befriended a profile with the ID 'NISHA KUMAR' on Facebook and 'POONAM383203' on Instagram. Later, this youth named Chandankumar arrived in Hyderabad and introduced himself as Poonam. Piyush was so blinded by love that he even filled sindoor in Chandan's hairline and married him. After marriage, whenever Piyush insisted on physical relations, Chandan would make excuses saying, 'It's a vow to Vaishnodevi, we will have relations after it's fulfilled.' When Piyush became suspicious and investigated, it was revealed that Chandan was a transgender person. One night, while Chandan was sleeping, Piyush removed his clothes and made a video. Chandan, who woke up, angrily broke Piyush's mobile and assaulted him. To get rid of him, Piyush went from Hyderabad to his native UP, but Chandan followed him there too and threatened to stop Piyush's sister's wedding, causing a commotion. Frustrated, Piyush went to Bhilwara in Rajasthan to settle, but Chandan followed him there too and attacked his private parts. Finally, without telling anyone, Piyush came to his brother's place in Shapar (Padvala) in Rajkot district, Gujarat. Chandan somehow found his address and on June 21, at the room of the Padvala factory, had arrived. As soon as Chandan arrived at the room, he started fighting with Piyush. In a fit of rage, Piyush retaliated, rendered Chandan semi-conscious, and dragged him by the hand to a deserted pit near the railway tracks. There, he brutally murdered him by repeatedly hitting his face and head with heavy stones and then placed stones on the body. After the murder, Piyush returned to the factory as if nothing had happened and resumed his work as usual. PM report revealed the mystery of the murder, mobile location and CCTV identified the culprit. Shapar police initially registered a case of accidental death under Section 194 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS). Later, the forensic PM report from Rajkot Government Hospital clearly stated that the deceased died due to severe head injuries, after which the course of investigation changed. Police, using technical surveillance, saw the movement of the suspicious laborer Piyush from the pyramid factory and interrogated him in their unique way, in which he broke down. On the instructions of Rajkot Range IG Nirlipt Rai and Rural SP Vijaysinh Gurjar, Shapar Police, based on technical sources and CCTV footage, apprehended the killer Piyush within a few days.

Heading: Air Marshal Dixit takes over as Deputy Chief of IAF

Content: Agency | New Delhi Air Marshal Ashutosh Dixit, who previously served as 'Chief of Integrated Defence Staff' during 'Operation Sindoor', took over as the new Deputy Chief of the Air Force on Wednesday. He replaced Air Marshal Nagesh Kapoor, who retired on June 30 after four decades of service in the Indian Air Force. Air Marshal Dixit was given a 'Guard of Honour' at Air Force Headquarters 'Vayu Bhawan' upon assuming charge as the new Deputy Chief of the Air Force. Before the ceremony, Dixit visited the National War Memorial and paid floral tributes to the martyrs of the armed forces. Prior to his appointment as Deputy Chief, he was serving as 'Chief of Integrated Defence Staff' at the Integrated Defence Staff Headquarters here.

Heading: Have the citizens' sensibilities themselves become numb?
Summary: The article critically questions the state of citizens' sensibilities in India, highlighting three major concerns: damage to national self-respect, a crisis of trust due to alleged scams, and the perceived insult to martyrs through delayed recognition. It criticizes both the government for its actions and the opposition and media for their perceived inaction or misdirection. The author argues that while the government has finally recognized martyrs after a long delay, their honor should extend beyond mere notifications to include truth and sensitivity.
Content: In the last one and a half decades, three such incidents have been witnessed that have hurt our 'pride', 'faith', and the 'dignity of martyrs'. It is surprising and ironic that while all this is happening, the country's integrity and culture are said to be strong. Three wounds, one question. 1. On Self-Respect: America, especially President Trump, has allegedly behaved in a friendly manner for 17 months, which often undermines our sovereignty and self-respect. 2. On Faith: Crisis of Trust. Scam in offerings at Shri Ram Mandir and land purchase came to light. Has India become a hub of scams since 1948? Disorder in the name of order has eroded trust. What will be said about trust betrayed by distrust? 3. Insult to Martyrs: Operation Sindoor saw 6 jawans (5 Army and 1 Air Force) martyred, but the news was suppressed for 13 months and 7 days. The silence was broken when the Government of India officially published the names of the martyrs on June 26, 2026, and included them in the Roll of Honor of the National War Memorial. According to Hindus, this delay is not a matter of respect but a result of a lack of proper recognition. Earlier, on June 8, 2026, the President posthumously honored martyr Sunil Kumar with Vir Chakra and Surendra Kumar with Vayu Sena Medal. ...do not do it? The limit of shamelessness is that even today no word has been said nor any wrong statement has been refuted. Are these 6 martyrs not precious gems of the country? Or were they not part of Operation Sindoor? India has fought wars with China, Pakistan, Bangladesh, and during that period, the sacrifice of these martyrs was never hidden. Opposition in deep sleep The question is not just for the government, but also for the opposition. On July 28, 2025, an uproar was made in Parliament, while on May 11, 2025, the DGMO paid tribute to the martyrs. Then why did the opposition not accept this martyrdom? Why was the government's notification for the resignation of the Union Education Minister delayed for 2 days? Although on July 30, 2025, Congress presented the families of two martyrs at a press conference in its Patna office, why did the Congress not raise this issue then? On June 8, 2026, the President awarded gallantry medals, but for 8 days, the Union Education Minister was made to sit at Jantar Mantar to demand his resignation for the sake of the youth. The government does not need to answer the insult to the martyrdom of these youth for their selfish motives. Media, which is called the watchdog of democracy, creates sensational news about Sushant Singh Rajput's suicide and creates a ruckus in the country. But what is its role here? The stomach is not turning? In this country, Lal Bihari Mritak fought for 18 years to prove himself alive. He didn't cast a vote. He didn't sell land. He ran a movement by making his own death certificate. Finally, in 1984, he was declared alive. The family of Saroj Devi of Aligarh, whose husband was declared dead, could not get any record till 2022. What a wonder! The dead (martyrs) are declared alive, but the government is trying to make the living martyrs dead. It is good and comforting that the movement has broken the 13-month-long silence, and the government has issued a notification declaring them martyrs. The notification should not be limited to the honor, medals, and memorials of martyrs; it should also be connected with time, truth, and sensitivity. (Author, Tax Consultant and Former President, Betul Sudhar Nyas)

Content: Ahmedabad. Nowadays, relationships are forming and breaking on social media. Heading: Rajnath Singh misled Parliament on soldier deaths, says Venugopal; demands privilege proceedings
Summary: Congress leader K.C. Venugopal has demanded privilege proceedings against Defence Minister Rajnath Singh, accusing him of misleading Parliament. Venugopal alleges that Singh falsely claimed no Indian soldiers were martyred after the Pahalgam terror attack and Operation Sindoor, despite a later statement confirming six deaths. He stated that such an act constitutes a breach of privilege and contempt of Parliament, calling it a "grave insult" to the martyrs' families and the armed forces.
Content: NEW DELHI, JUL 1: Senior Congress leader K C Venugopal on Tuesday wrote to Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla demanding that privilege proceedings be initiated against Defence Minister Rajnath Singh for "misleading" Parliament by claiming that no Indian soldier was martyred post the Pahalgam terror attack last year. Venugopal gave the notice of privilege under Rule 223 of the Rules of Procedure and Conduct of Business in Lok Sabha. In his letter to the Speaker, Venugopal said that on July 28, 2025, during discussions on the terrorist attack in Pahalgam and the Operation Sindoor that followed, Rajnath Singh said that no harm was caused to the Indian soldiers. Venugopal said that later a statement was issued that said six armed forces personnel had died during Operation Sindoor. "The aforesaid position clearly indicates that the minister of defence stating on the floor of the House that there had been no casualties during Operation Sindoor was clearly misleading and incorrect," said the Congress MP in his letter. "It is well established that misleading the House or withholding information by a minister on the floor of the House constitutes a breach of privilege and contempt of Parliament," he added. "In view of the foregoing, I request that privilege proceedings be initiated against the minister of defence in the matter," Venugopal wrote in the letter. Posting a copy of the letter on X, Venugopal claimed that during the debate on Operation Sindoor in Lok Sabha, Singh "lied" to the people of India. "It was a straightforward, clear-cut lie to mislead the House. How could he, in July 2025, say that no Indian soldier was martyred, and then a year later the forces announce that we have lost 6 jawans?" wrote the Congress leader. "It is a grave insult to the families of these six martyrs and the entire armed forces that the people of India were not told of their bravery and ultimate sacrifice," he said. Heading: Have the citizens' sensibilities died, disappeared, become dormant, or dulled?
Summary: The article criticizes the Indian government and opposition for their handling of three major issues: perceived attacks on national self-respect by the US, alleged scams in the Shri Ram Temple, and the delayed acknowledgment and alleged insult to martyrs of "Operation Sindoor." The author questions the public's, political parties', and media's silence and inaction on these critical matters, suggesting a decline in national sensibility.
Content:
Author: Rajeev Khandelwal

In the last one and a half years, the country has witnessed three such incidents that have shattered our "pride and glory." On one hand, a blow to the country's sovereignty, on the other, a crisis of religious faith for millions, and thirdly, an "insult" to martyrs that is "unprecedented" and "unimaginable." It is surprising and ironic that all this is happening under the rule of the party that calls itself the "sole flag-bearer" of the country's integrity and culture.

Three Wounds, One Question!

1. Attack on Self-Respect: America, especially President Trump, has been "shredding" our sovereignty and self-respect for the past 17 months, despite allegedly declared friendly behavior towards India.

2. Blow to Faith: Crisis of Trust! Scams in offerings and land purchases at the Shri Ram Temple have come to light. From the Jeep scandal of 1948 to today's embezzlement of offerings, has India become a "haven for fraudsters"? "Disorder in the name of order" has "bled faith." Where will faith, built on trust, stand when trust is betrayed?

3. Insult to Martyrs: The news of 6 jawans (5 Army and 1 Air Force) martyred in Operation Sindoor was hidden for 13 months in seven posts. The silence was broken only when the Government of India officially released the names of the martyrs on June 26 and included them in the National War Memorial School of Roll of Honor. According to The Hindu, this delay was not a delay but a result of the standard process of adding names. However, before this, His Excellency the President had posthumously honored two martyrs, Sunil Kumar with the Vir Chakra and Surendra Kumar with the "Vayu Sevak Padak" on June 8, 2026. "Heads hang in shame!"

The most "heart-wrenching" thing is that on July 28, 2025, in the Lok Sabha, Defense Minister Rajnath Singh had defiantly stated – "No jawan of ours was martyred." MPs sitting behind were "thumping the tables." At the same time, the anger and pain of martyr Surendra Singh's mother had spilled out, which is viral today. See the irony, on May 11, 2025, the Director General of Military Operations had simply paid tribute to five martyrs at the end of a press briefing. News of the martyrs' last rites was also published. Is Rajnath Singh's statement denying martyrdom on the sacred floor of Parliament not just a matter of "privilege" but also an insult and humiliation to the martyrs and their families? The height of shamelessness is that till today the Defense Minister has neither apologized nor refuted his "wrong statement" or expressed regret. Were these 6 martyrs not precious gems of the country? Or were they not part of "Operation Sindoor"? India never hid martyrdom in wars with China, Pakistan, the Bangladesh Liberation War, and the Kargil War in this manner.

Opposition also in Kumbhakarna's sleep: The question is not just for the government, but also for the opposition. On July 28, an "untruth" was spoken in Parliament, while on May 11, the DGMO had accepted martyrdom by paying tribute. Why didn't the opposition "create a ruckus" then? Was the opposition "waiting for a government notification" to demand resignations? Although two days later, on July 30, Congress had presented two martyr families at a press conference in its Sadakat Ashram in Patna, it is beyond comprehension why Congress did not raise this issue then?

Even when the President awarded gallantry medals on June 8, the opposition's "lips were sealed." The "Jain-Ji" youth, who had been protesting for 8 days at Jantar Mantar demanding the resignation of Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan, responsible for the paper leak, did not feel the "need" to ask the government for an answer regarding the insult to the said martyrdom beyond their limited objective.

The media, which is called the guardian of democracy, creates a sensation by turning Sushant Singh's suicide into sensational news for TRP, creating a stir across the country. But what about its role here? "Than-than Gopal?" (Empty-handed/Useless)

Isn't the Ganges flowing backward? In this country, Lal Bihari +deceased+ had to "wander through offices" for 18 years to prove himself alive. He couldn't vote. He couldn't sell land. He had even prepared for his own funeral. He formed a "Deceased Association" and launched a movement. Finally, he was declared alive in 1984. Saroj Devi of Aligarh, due to an error, was listed as deceased instead of her husband and has not been able to correct the record since 2022.

Heading: Delayed Recognition
Summary: The article discusses the delayed official acknowledgment of six military personnel who died during Operation Sindoor, whose names were inscribed at the National War Memorial a year after their deaths. It questions the government's communication regarding casualties, particularly a statement by the Defence Minister that created an impression of no military losses. The piece emphasizes that democracies should transparently acknowledge soldiers' sacrifices to reinforce public trust, citing examples like the Kargil conflict and practices in other nations.
Content: Every democracy owes two debts to its soldiers. The first is to equip them well enough to fight. The second is to acknowledge them with honesty if they fall. The first secures the nation's borders. The second safeguards its conscience. The recent inscription of the names of six military personnel who died during Operation Sindoor at the National War Memorial has reopened questions that extend beyond party politics. The issue is not whether these brave men were honoured. They were. They received gallantry awards, their families were presented with the medals, and they have now found a place on the nation's Roll of Honour. The question is why a clear, official acknowledgement of their sacrifice as casualties of Operation Sindoor came only a year later. The government's defence deserves consideration. It has pointed out that the Director General of Military Operations referred to casualties in May 2025, gallantry awards were announced in August, and the memorial inscription followed established protocol. It has also clarified that Defence Minister Rajnath Singh's statement in Parliament that no Indian soldiers had been harmed was intended to rebut claims that Indian fighter pilots had been killed during the operation. Yet the controversy has persisted because the minister's recorded remarks were broader than that explanation. They conveyed the impression that India had suffered no military casualties. If a clarification becomes necessary a year later, it is reasonable to conclude that official communication left room for misunderstanding. This matters because democracies do not diminish military success by acknowledging combat losses. They reinforce public trust by doing so. No modern army can expect to wage operations without risk. Soldiers know it, their families know it, and the nation knows it. What the public expects in return is candour once operational requirements have been met and next of kin have been informed. India has long understood this principle. During the Kargil conflict, casualty lists were released regularly and the nation watched as fallen soldiers were accorded military honours before being laid to rest. The Pulwama martyrs were identified immediately and mourned across the country. Other established democracies follow similar practices. Whether in the United States, the United Kingdom, Australia or Israel, operational details may remain classified, but the identities of personnel killed in action are normally made public after their families have been notified. National remembrance is never treated as a military secret. The nation should not have had to piece together the human cost of a military campaign through local reports, medal citations and, eventually, inscriptions on a memorial wall. The strength of a democracy lies not in projecting an image of invulnerability but in possessing the confidence to acknowledge sacrifice with clarity and dignity.

Heading: Editorial - Pakistan's Nuclear Threat Amidst Peace Initiative

The language they are using reeks of hatred, not an initiative for peace or harmony. On one hand, Pakistani ministers are threatening India with nuclear war, while on the other hand, some prominent people from India and Pakistan are appealing for peace. This also raises some question marks over this peace initiative. In fact, ever since the Indus Waters Treaty was suspended, Pakistan has been crying 'water-water'. Suddenly, its ministers became aggressive against India and are saying strange things. Pakistan thinks that just as it was allegedly effective in the America-Iran war, it will be the same with India. But that is not the case. India works on its own terms. It knows this. India implemented a ceasefire in Operation Sindoor on its own terms. Meanwhile, Pakistan's Climate Change Minister Musadik Malik has made derogatory, exaggerated, and nefarious statements like 'cutting hands'. In such a situation, can there be a peace initiative? In all these incidents, somewhere or the other, suspicion arises that Pakistan's nefarious intentions are being exposed. Pakistan is raising issues like the Indus Waters Treaty to hide its deteriorating domestic situation. Pakistan is in trouble these days. The Shahbaz government is unable to control the situation in PoK, and people have revolted. On the other hand, Afghans have carried out airstrikes in Pakistan, and India has stopped the water of the Indus, so when Pakistan was surrounded by troubles from three sides, it started squirming. Heading: Every martyr deserves equal recognition Electoral integrity requires public confidence Climate action must move beyond plans
Summary: The clipping features three letters to the editor. One letter criticizes the delay in recognizing soldiers martyred in Operation Sindoor, advocating for equal recognition for all who sacrificed for the nation. Another highlights concerns over electoral roll transparency and deletions, urging the Election Commission to ensure fairness and public confidence. The third emphasizes the urgent need for decisive climate action in India, calling for better funding, implementation of Heat Action Plans, and investments in resilient infrastructure to combat rising temperatures and erratic monsoons.
Content: The delay in officially acknowledging the sacrifice of six soldiers during Operation Sindoor has raised serious concerns. While governments may withhold operational details for strategic reasons, there can be no justification for delaying recognition of those who laid down their lives in the service of the nation. A grateful nation must never allow its martyrs to fade into anonymity. Behind every soldier's sacrifice stands a grieving family that bears an irreparable loss with dignity and pride. No parent, spouse or child can ever forget a loved one who made the ultimate sacrifice. These families, along with the soldiers' regiments and fellow servicemen, deserve the nation's enduring respect and gratitude. It would therefore be a fitting tribute if the names of these six brave soldiers were also inscribed at the Baisaran Martyrs Memorial in Pahalgam alongside the 26 civilians who lost their lives in the tragic terrorist attack. Such a gesture would honour all those who paid the highest price in the same tragic chain of events and reinforce the nation's commitment to remembering every sacrifice equally. National gratitude should never distinguish between civilian victims and soldiers who gave their lives protecting the country. The decision of 23 Opposition parties, along with an Independent MP, to jointly approach the Chief Justice of India over the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls reflects growing concerns about the transparency and fairness of the electoral process. Irrespective of political affiliations, preserving public confidence in elections is fundamental to any democracy. The SIR exercise, now implemented across several states after beginning in Bihar, has reportedly resulted in the deletion of millions of names from electoral rolls. Allegations that many eligible citizens were unable to vote while appeals remained pending have naturally raised questions about due process and voter rights. Equally concerning is the absence of clear official data regarding the identification of alleged illegal immigrants, despite this being cited as one of the objectives of the exercise. It is essential that the Commission clearly explains the criteria for deletions, ensures timely disposal of appeals and protects the voting rights of genuine citizens. Free and fair elections require not only impartial institutions but also the confidence of all stakeholders. Greater openness and procedural fairness will strengthen, rather than weaken, India's democratic foundations. Apropos "India must get ready for climate extremes" (June 30), the alarming rise in temperatures and increasingly erratic monsoons leave little doubt that climate change is no longer a distant threat but a present-day reality. Although several states have adopted Heat Action Plans, many remain poorly funded and weakly implemented. Vulnerable communities, particularly those living in densely populated urban settlements, continue to face severe shortages of drinking water, shade and healthcare during extreme heat. Similarly, inadequate drainage systems turn heavy rainfall into recurring urban disasters, while rain-dependent agriculture suffers repeated setbacks from unpredictable weather patterns. India now needs decisive implementation rather than additional policy documents. Heatwaves should be formally recognised as disasters to facilitate quicker relief and dedicated funding. Investments must prioritise urban drainage, wetland conservation, green cover, cooling shelters, early warning systems and climate-resilient agriculture. As climate extremes become more frequent, delaying action will only multiply future losses. Preparedness, resilience and sustained investment are the need of the hour.

Equally concerning is the absence of clear official data regarding the identification of alleged illegal immigrants, despite this being cited as one of the objectives of the exercise. It is essential that the Commission clearly explains the criteria for deletions, ensures timely disposal of appeals and protects the voting rights of genuine citizens. Free and fair elections require not only impartial institutions but also the confidence of all stakeholders. Greater openness and procedural fairness will strengthen, rather than weaken, India's democratic foundations. Climate action must move beyond plans Apropos "India must get ready for climate extremes" (June 30), the alarming rise in temperatures and increasingly erratic monsoons leave little doubt that climate change is no longer a distant threat but a present-day reality. Although several states have adopted Heat Action Plans, many remain poorly funded and weakly implemented. Vulnerable communities, particularly those living in densely populated urban settlements, continue to face severe shortages of drinking water, shade and healthcare during extreme heat. Similarly, inadequate drainage systems turn heavy rainfall into recurring urban disasters, while rain-dependent agriculture suffers repeated setbacks from unpredictable weather patterns. India now needs decisive implementation rather than additional policy documents. Heatwaves should be formally recognised as disasters to facilitate quicker relief and dedicated funding. Investments must prioritise urban drainage, wetland conservation, green cover, cooling shelters, early warning systems and climate-resilient agriculture. As climate extremes become more frequent, delaying action will only multiply future losses. Preparedness, resilience and sustained investment are the need of the hour.

Heading: INBOX
Summary: This 'INBOX' section features multiple letters to the editor. Topics include concerns over recurring landslides in Vasco requiring immediate government action, questions regarding the delayed official recognition of military martyrs and alleged government misinformation, and an introspection on whether the ideals of Lord Ram are reflected in the administration of the Ayodhya temple. Additionally, one letter criticizes India's poor football performance compared to smaller nations, advocating for grassroots development and increased public support.
Content: INBOX Slope safety A massive boulder came crashing down a rain-soaked hillside onto a house at Vodant in Vasco on Tuesday. Fortunately, the occupants escaped unhurt, but the incident highlighted the dangers faced by residents living near unstable slopes. Just days earlier, a landslide along Harbour Road claimed the life of a labourer. Within days, another landslide occurred along the same stretch, while a recent landslide at New Vaddem has further heightened public concern. These recurring incidents point to a larger issue that requires immediate attention from the authorities. Residents have repeatedly raised concerns about the stability of hills in several parts of the port town. The soil is known to be soft, and continuous heavy rainfall weakens the slopes, increasing the risk of landslides and falling boulders. A comprehensive geological assessment of vulnerable hillsides should be carried out to identify unstable zones. Loose rocks and boulders must be removed before they become hazards. Permanent retaining walls, effective drainage systems and slope stabilisation measures should be taken up in high-risk areas to prevent erosion and land-slides. Authorities should also reg-ularly monitor vulnerable hillsides, particularly during the mon-soon, and issue timely warnings whenever required. The repeated landslides in Vasco are a clear warning that lasting measures can no longer be delayed. Adelmo Fernandes, Vasco Martyrs' recognition Every democracy owes two debts to its soldiers: to equip them well enough to fight and to acknowledge them honestly if they fall. The first se-cures the nation's borders, while the second safeguards its conscience. The recent inscription of the names of six military personnel who died during Operation Sindoor at the National War Memorial has raised questions beyond party politics. The issue is not whether these person-nel were honoured. They received gallantry awards, their families were presented with the medals, and their names have now been inscribed on the nation's Roll of Honour. The question is why official acknowl-edgement of their sacrifice as casual-ties of Operation Sindoor came only a year later. The government has said that the Director General of Military Operations referred to casualties in May 2025, gallantry awards were announced in August, and the me-morial inscription followed estab-lished procedure. At the same time, Opposition leaders have questioned the government's statements in Parliament. The letter cites Congress leader K C Venugopal's contention that misleading or withholding infor-mation from Parliament constitutes a breach of privilege. It also refers to retired Colonel Rohit Chaudhry's de-mand that Defence Minister Rajnath Singh resign over the issue. The gov-ernment should come forward and explain the facts to the nation. Yash Pal Ralhan, Jalandhar Temple introspection The consecration of Ram Lalla in the permanent temple at Ayodhya on January 22, 2024, was a historic occa-sion for millions of devotees. During the ceremony, the Prime Minister described it as the beginning of a new chapter in India's civilisational journey and an occasion for intro-spection. He also highlighted Lord Ram's virtues of truthfulness, duty, justice, com-passion and unwaver-ing commitment to righteousness. A central theme of his address was conveyed through the phrases “dev se desh” and “Ram se rashtra”. He said the temple should inspire ev-ery citizen to contribute to society through honesty, discipline, selfless service and moral character. These words raise an important question. Are these ideals being reflected in the administration and functioning of the Ram Temple today? Those entrusted with managing one of the country's most sacred institutions have a responsibility that extends beyond financial and administra-tive matters. They are also expected to uphold the values that Lord Ram symbolises. Recent developments have prompted many devotees to ask whether the principles of transpar-ency, justice, fairness and ethical conduct are being followed. If the temple is to be a beacon of moral leadership, its trustees and administrators must demonstrate commitment to righteousness. Evaristo Fernandes, Merces Football failure Cape Verde, a nation of just 5.3 lakh people, has reached the FIFA World Cup knockout stage after finishing second in Group H behind Spain and ahead of Uruguay. It is a re-markable achievement for a country considered an outsider. By contrast, India, despite having the world's second-largest population, contin-ues to struggle to field a competitive national football team or qualify for a FIFA World Cup. In my view, those running the game are focusing on issues such as renaming the All India Football Federation instead of investing in grassroots development and giving talented young players opportunities to raise the standard of Indian football. The Indian media also gives football far less attention than cricket. If India is to qualify for a FIFA World Cup, people must show greater interest in football and sup-port the sport at all levels. Jerry Fernandes, Saligao

Venugopal said how could it be stated in July 2025 that no Indian soldier was martyred, when a year later, the security forces themselves provided information about the sacrifice of six soldiers. The document shared by him records Defense Minister Rajnath Singh's statement during the Lok Sabha proceedings. In that part of the proceedings, the Defense Minister, while answering questions raised by the opposition, states that if asked whether Operation Sindoor was successful, the answer is yes. If asked whether our forces eliminated the masters of those terrorists who wiped out the 'sindoor' of our sisters and daughters in Operation Sindoor, the answer is yes.

Summary: The article critically examines the Indian government's handling of national issues, including alleged insults to martyrs, scams related to the Shri Ram Temple, and perceived attacks on India's sovereignty by the US. It questions the government's integrity, the opposition's inaction, and the media's role, urging citizens to be more vigilant and questioning. The author expresses concern over the lack of a strong political alternative amidst these challenges.
Content:
Rajiv Khandelwal
In the last one and a half years, the country has witnessed three such incidents that have tarnished our pride and honor. On one hand, an attack on the country's sovereignty, on the other hand, a crisis of religious faith for millions, and thirdly, an insult to martyrs that has no parallel in history. It is surprising and ironic that all this is happening under the rule of the party that claims to be the sole flag-bearer of the country's integrity and culture.
Three Wounds, One Question.
1. Attack on Self-Respect: America, especially President Trump, has often trampled on our sovereignty and self-respect with allegedly declared friendly behavior towards India for the past 17 months.
2. Attack on Faith: Crisis of Trust. Scams in offerings and land purchases for the Shri Ram Temple have come to light. From the 1948 Jeep scandal to today's embezzlement of offerings, has India become a den of fraudsters? Disorder in the name of order has bled faith. Where will faith, built on trust, stand in the face of betrayal?
3. Insult to Martyrs:
The news of 6 jawans (5 Army and 1 Air Force) martyred in Operation Sindoor was hidden for 13 months under seven veils. The silence, as if having curd in the mouth, was broken only when the Government of India issued a notification on June 26, officially including the names of the martyrs in the National War Memorial School of Roll of Honor. According to The Hindu, this delay was not a delay but a result of the standard process of adding names. However, even before this, His Excellency the President had posthumously honored two martyrs, Sunil Kumar with the Vir Chakra and Surendra Kumar with the Vayu Seva Medal, on June 8, 2026.
Heads hang in shame.
The most heartbreaking thing is that on July 28, 2025, Defense Minister Rajnath Singh, in a challenging tone, stated in the Lok Sabha – 'None of our jawans suffered casualties.' People were patting themselves on the back. At the same time, the anger and pain of the mother of a martyr was viral.
See the irony, on May 11, 2025, the Director General of Military Operations (Chhatarpur) had casually paid tribute to five martyrs at the end of a press briefing. News of the martyrs' last rites was also published. Yet, Defense Minister Rajnath Singh's statement denying martyrdom on the sacred floor of Parliament, besides being a matter of privilege, isn't it an insult and humiliation to the martyrs and their families? The height of shamelessness is that till date, the Defense Minister has neither apologized nor refuted the false statement or expressed regret. Were these 6 martyrs not precious gems of the country? Or were they not part of Operation Sindoor? India never hid such martyrdoms during wars with China, Pakistan, the creation of Bangladesh, and the Kargil War.
Opposition also in Kumbhakarna's sleep
The question is not just for the government, but also for the opposition. A falsehood was spoken in Parliament on July 28, while on May 11, the DGMO had accepted the martyrdom by paying tribute. Why didn't the opposition create a ruckus then? Was the opposition waiting for a government notification to demand resignation? Although two days later, on July 30, the Congress presented two martyr families at a press conference in their Sadakat Ashram in Patna, it is beyond comprehension why the Congress did not raise this issue then?
Even when the President awarded gallantry medals on June 8, the opposition's lips were sealed.
For 8 days, Jain-G youth, who were demanding the resignation of Central Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan responsible for the paper leak at Jantar Mantar, did not feel the need to ask the government for an answer regarding the insult to the said martyrdom, beyond their limited objective.
The media, which is called the watchdog of democracy, creates a sensation by turning Sushant Singh's suicide into sensational news for TRP, causing a stir across the country. But what about its role here? Empty vessel?
Isn't the Ganges flowing in reverse?
In this country, Lal Bihari Mritak had to wander through offices for 18 years to prove himself alive. He couldn't vote. He couldn't sell land. He had even prepared for his own funeral. He formed the 'Mritak Sangh' (Association of the Dead) and led a movement. Finally, in 1984, he was declared alive. Saroj Devi of Aligarh, whose husband was mistakenly recorded as dead, has not been able to correct the record since 2022.
But here, something astonishing happened. A deceased (martyr) was declared alive, and that too in the Lok Sabha, the temple of democracy. We have heard of bringing the dead to life, but here, an attempt was made to declare living martyrdom as dead. Thankfully, consolation is that, without any agitation, after 13 months, the government issued a notification declaring them martyrs, considering them deceased. The notification is not just limited to honor, medals, or memorials; it should also be linked to timely truth and sensitivity.
Learn and understand the importance of a soldier. On April 5, 2026, America, following its 'No One Left Behind' policy, carried out its history's largest and most dangerous successful rescue operation, extracting a wounded airman from Iranian soil within 48 hours with the help of 155 aircraft. This demonstrates that country's strong commitment to its soldiers, and a nation becomes strong not just by power, but also by self-respect.
How do powerful countries like America, who hurt the self-respect of every nation, respond? Learn from some countries in the world. Australia's Turnbull, Canada's Trudeau, Denmark's Mette Frederiksen, Sweden's Stefan Löfven, Germany's Merkel, France's Macron, Mexico's Peña Nieto and Claudia Sheinbaum, Turkey's Erdoğan – all spoke eye-to-eye in the face of Trump's threats. No one sold Greenland, no one paid for the wall, refused to pay for the wall, and the letter was thrown in the dustbin...! Last question?
When offerings are embezzled, faith is plundered, martyrdom is hidden, and sovereignty is being harmed, and yet our blood doesn't boil, what does it mean? Have our sensibilities died? Before history remembers us as a voiceless, conscienceless nation!
Conclusion!
Are we forgetting to react? Or have we become so stone-hearted that we are breaking down martyrdom by wearing political spectacles?
The greatest strength of democracy is not the government, but aware citizens.
History remembers those societies that ask questions – and also those societies that remain silent.
Finally, my point.
Disturbed by the insult to martyrs, the pen is highlighting a sorrowful, distressed mind. May 'Ram Naam Satya' (the truth of Ram's name, often chanted during funerals) not become a reality, may 'Ram Naam Satya' not become a reality. The real concern is that a strong alternative is still not available today.
(The author is a tax consultant and former president, Betul Sudhar Nyas)

He stated that under 'Operation Snow Leopard' on the northern borders, the army fulfilled its responsibilities with full strength, while on the western border, it demonstrated restraint and firmness. He cited 'Operation Sindoor' as an excellent example of the Indian Army's capability, preparedness, and commitment. General Dwivedi said that the army has worked with clear objectives, discipline, and responsibility on every issue related to national security. Highlighting the increasing coordination among the three services as a future necessity, he said that future warfare would be joint, integrated, and theater-based. Therefore, the Army, Navy, and Air Force would have to unite to plan and act. He called this the new normal of India's security strategy.

Heading: Privilege motion notice against Rajnath for misleading Parliament on 'Operation Sindoor' issue
Summary: The Congress party has filed a privilege motion against Defence Minister Rajnath Singh, accusing him of misleading Parliament regarding casualties in 'Operation Sindoor'. Venugopal has written to the Lok Sabha Speaker, demanding action under Rule 223.
Content:
New Delhi, dated 30.
The controversy regarding the death of Indian soldiers during 'Operation Sindoor' has deepened. Defence Minister Rajnath Singh had stated in Parliament that no Indian soldier was harmed during the operation, but later, with official information emerging about the deaths of 6 armed forces personnel, Congress has strongly protested this issue. Congress has demanded the Lok Sabha Speaker initiate privilege motion proceedings against the Defence Minister.

Congress MP and Chairman of the Public Accounts Committee (PAC), K.C. Venugopal, has written a letter to Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla, requesting the initiation of privilege proceedings under Rule 223. According to him, on July 28, 2025, during the discussion in Lok Sabha regarding the Pahalgam terrorist attack and 'Operation Sindoor', the Defence Minister had clearly stated that no Indian soldiers were harmed during the entire operation. Congress alleges that this statement and now the official information released by the government is contrary to that. According to recently released details, 6 armed forces personnel were martyred during Operation Sindoor. The released list includes Subedar Major Pawan Kumar, Rifleman Sunil Kumar (Vir Chakra), Lance Naik Dinesh Kumar, Aviation Technician Mood Muralinayak, Havildar Sunil Kumar Singh and Indian Air Force Sergeant Surendra Kumar (Vayu Sena Medal) are said to be included in the names.

Heading: Gopal Chettri accuses Centre of Failing Students and Misleading the Public
Summary: Gopal Chettri of the Sikkim Pradesh Congress Committee (SPCC) criticized the BJP-led Central government for alleged failures in the education sector, misleading statements on national security, and financial irregularities at the Ram Janmabhoomi temple. He highlighted the NEET exam scam, claiming question papers were sold for Rs 30 lakh, and accused the Defence Minister of misleading Parliament on military casualties. Chettri demanded accountability and the resignation of Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan, stating these issues have eroded public confidence and exposed governance failures.
Content:
TM Report
GANGTOK, 30
JUNE: The Sikkim
Pradesh Congress
Committee (SPCC) on
Tuesday criticised the
Bharatiya Janata Party
(BJP)-led Central
government, alleging
failures in the education
sector, misleading
statements on national
security matters and
irregularities in the
management of the Ram
Janmabhoomi temple.

Addressing a press
conference at the SPCC
headquarters in 6th Mile,
Tadong, SPCC president
Gopal Chettri said the
country was witnessing a
series of incidents that had
shaken public confidence
in the government and
demanded accountability
on several issues.

Speaking on the alleged
irregularities surrounding
the NEET examination,
Chettri described the
examination as “one of the
biggest scams” affecting
students across the
country.

He said lakhs of
students had worked
tirelessly with the dream
of becoming doctors
while their parents had
made enormous financial
sacrifices to support
them.

“Parents sold land,
mortgaged their houses,
exhausted their savings
and even took loans from
banks and private lenders
to help their children
prepare for the
examination. Many
families spent heavily on
travel and accommodation
to reach examination
centres. Their hopes have
been shattered because of
the government’s failure
to conduct the
examination fairly,” he
said.

Chettri alleged that the
paper leak and subsequent
cancellation of the
examination had left
around 2.2 million
students frustrated and
uncertain about their
future.
“The education
system has played with
the emotions of students.
Even while rescheduling
the examination, there
was gross negligence.
One student was
reportedly allotted an
examination centre in Abu
Dhabi. Such incidents
expose the complete
collapse of the system,”
he said. Claiming that
question papers were
allegedly sold for as much
as Rs 30 lakh, Chettri
questioned how such a
large-scale scam could
occur under a government
that frequently speaks of
strong governance.

“Students are the
future of this country. If
the education system itself
becomes corrupt and
unreliable, the nation’s
future is in danger. The
government must explain
under whose protection
such scams are taking
place,” he said.

Quoting figures
released by the Congress
party’s Analysis Wing,
Chettri claimed that
families collectively spend
around Rs 1.32 lakh crore
on a single NEET
examination. He added
that when expenses
related to examinations
such as NEET, UPSC,
JEE, RRB and SSC are
combined, the total
reaches nearly Rs 3.5 lakh
crore.

He demanded the
immediate resignation of
Union Education Minister
Dharmendra Pradhan over
the alleged irregularities
and accused government
ministers of denying the
existence of paper leaks
despite widespread
allegations.

“The government
cannot simply dismiss
everything as rumours.
The students of this
country deserve
transparency, justice and
accountability,” he said.
Referring to Congress
leader Rahul Gandhi’s
recent address during the
‘Chhattron Ki Goonj’
programme in Kota,
Rajasthan, Chettri said the
Congress would continue
raising the concerns of
students and their families
across the country.

The SPCC president
also criticised the Union
government over
Operation Sindoor,
alleging that Defence
Minister Rajnath Singh
had misled Parliament by
stating that there were no
military casualties during
the operation.

“It is deeply
unfortunate if the
country’s Defence
Minister gives incorrect
information in Parliament.
Reports indicate that six
soldiers lost their lives, and
their names were later
inscribed at the National
War Memorial. The
government must explain
why the truth was not
disclosed earlier,” he said.

Chettri further
referred to reported thefts
and financial irregularities
at the Ram Janmabhoomi
temple in Ayodhya,
alleging that despite the
temple’s management and
security being under the
control of the trust,
reports had emerged of
cash, silver bricks and
valuable ornaments going
missing.

“If reports of such
large-scale thefts are true,
the government and those
responsible for the
temple’s administration
must answer how such
incidents occurred despite
high security
arrangements. Turning off
CCTV cameras months
before the alleged theft
raises serious questions
that require an impartial
investigation,” he said.

Concluding the press
conference, Chettri said
the alleged education
scam, the reported
concealment of military
casualties and the alleged
financial irregularities at
one of the country’s most
significant religious sites
had exposed serious
governance failures.

“The scams in the
education sector, the
insult to martyred soldiers
and the financial
irregularities at a centre of
faith have exposed the
true face of the current
government. The
government must provide
clear and truthful answers
to the people on all these
issues,” he said.

Content: New Delhi: General Upendra Dwivedi retired from the post of Army Chief on Tuesday, and in his place, General Dheeraj Seth took over as the 31st Chief of the Indian Army. Before leaving office, General Dwivedi paid tribute to the martyrs at the National War Memorial. This has made a significant contribution to the army's combat effectiveness and long-term transformation. During Operation Sindoor last year, his special division led the high-level operational preparation tasks. He led the challenging five infantry battalions of the armored division in the desert region, the western battlefield. Lieutenant General has also led the army's first independent armored division. In this situation, with increasing security challenges, the new Army Chief General Dheeraj Seth has taken charge. This is seen as significant. General Dwivedi, who took over as the country's 30th Army Chief in June 2024, emotionally described his four decades of service to the Indian Army as the greatest fortune of his life. Our army is strongly deployed on the northern border under 'Operation Snow Leopard', while on the western border, the army has performed its duty with full seriousness under 'Operation Sindoor'. During Operation Sindoor, carried out in response to the Pahalgam terrorist attack in May 2025, the Army, Navy and Air Force, all three wings, worked with a common ideology and excellent coordination, setting new standards. General Dwivedi praised the bravery and discipline of Indian soldiers for upholding the country's flag in humanitarian operations from the jungles of Congo in African countries to earthquake-affected Venezuela.

He also served as Deputy Chief of Integrated Defence Staff (Policy, Planning and Force Development). His contribution in the field of training has also been remarkable. He served as Platoon Commander and Instructor (Class C) at the Indian Military Academy. Additionally, he held the important responsibility of Directing Staff Coordinator in the Indian Military Training Team in Bhutan. Summary: Congress general secretary K.C. Venugopal has moved a privilege notice against Defence Minister Rajnath Singh in the Lok Sabha, accusing him of misleading Parliament regarding casualties in 'Operation Sindoor'. Venugopal claims Singh stated no Indian soldier was killed during a debate in July 2025, but the government later acknowledged six armed forces personnel died in the operation. Content: The Hindu Bureau NEW DELHI Congress general secretary K.C. Venugopal on Tuesday moved a privilege notice against Defence Minister Rajnath Singh in the Lok Sabha, accusing him of misleading Parliament by stating during the Operation Sindoor debate last year that no Indian soldier had been killed. In a letter to Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla, Mr. Venugopal sought initiation of privilege proceedings against the Defence Minister under Rule 223 of the Rules of Procedure and Conduct of Business in the Lok Sabha. The Congress leader said that during the discussion held in July 2025 on the Pahalgam terror attack and Operation Sindoor, Mr. Singh had told the House that no harm had come to Indian soldiers. However, he noted that the government had since acknowledged that six personnel of the armed forces died during the military operation. “The Minister’s statement on the floor of the House that there had been no casualties during Operation Sindoor was clearly misleading and incorrect,” Mr. Venugopal said in the notice, adding that misleading Parliament or withholding information amounted to a breach of privilege and contempt of the House. “How could he, in July 2025, say that no Indian soldier was martyred, and then a year later the forces announce that we have lost six jawans?” he asked in a post on X. ‘Insult to the families’ He said withholding information about the deaths was an insult to the families of the personnel and the armed forces, adding that they had laid down their lives in defence of the nation.

How could he, in July 2025, say that no Indian soldier was martyred, and then a year later the forces announce that we have lost 6 jawans?” the Congress leader asked. Getting the opportunity to serve in the Indian Army for over four decades is the greatest fortune of my life.” The strength of the Indian Army does not depend on just one person, but on its soldiers, commanders, ex-servicemen, their families, and the unwavering trust of the country's citizens, he clarified. General Dwivedi told reporters that in two years, the Army has consistently maintained its readiness on all fronts. Content: ಸುದ್ದಿ ಸಿಂಚನ ಸೈನಿಕರ ಸಾವಿನ ಬಗ್ಗೆ ಸುಳ್ಳು: ರಾಜನಾಥ್ ಸಿಂಗ್ ವಿರುದ್ಧ ಕಾಂಗ್ರೆಸ್‌ನಿಂದ ಹಕ್ಕುಚ್ಯುತಿ ನವದೆಹಲಿ: 'ಆಪರೇಷನ್ ಸಿಂಧೂರ ಸಂದರ್ಭದಲ್ಲಿ ದೇಶದ ಯಾವುದೇ ಯೋಧರು ಸಾವನ್ನಪ್ಪಿಲ್ಲ ಎಂದು ಸದನಕ್ಕೆ ಸುಳ್ಳು ಮಾಹಿತಿ ನೀಡಿ, ದಾರಿ ತಪ್ಪಿಸಿದ್ದರು' ಎಂದು ಆರೋಪಿಸಿ ರಕ್ಷಣಾ ಸಚಿವ ರಾಜನಾಥ್ ಸಿಂಗ್ ವಿರುದ್ಧ ಕೆ.ಸಿ. ವೇಣುಗೋಪಾಲ್ ಅವರು ಲೋಕಸಭೆ ಸ್ಪೀಕರ್ ಓಂ ಬಿರ್ಲಾ ಅವರಿಗೆ ಹಕ್ಕುಚ್ಯುತಿ ಮಂಡನೆ ನೋಟಿಸ್ ನೀಡಿದ್ದಾರೆ. ಕಳೆದ ವರ್ಷ ಜೂ.28ರಂದು ಸದನದಲ್ಲಿ ಮಾತನಾಡುವ ವೇಳೆ, 'ಪಲ್ಲಾಂಗ ದಾಳಿಗೆ ಪ್ರತಿಕಾರವಾಗಿ ಭಾರತ ನಡೆಸಿದ ಆಪರೇಷನ್ ಸಿಂಧೂರದಲ್ಲಿ ಸೈನಿಕರು ಮೃತಪಟ್ಟಿಲ್ಲ' ಎಂದು ಸಿಂಗ್ ಹೇಳಿದ್ದರು. ಆದರೆ ಇತ್ತೀಚೆಗೆ ಸೇನೆ, ಆಪರೇಷನ್ ಸಿಂಧೂರದಲ್ಲಿ 6 ಮಂದಿ ಸೈನಿಕರು ಸಾವನ್ನಪ್ಪಿದ್ದಾರೆ ಎಂದು ಪ್ರಕಟಿಸಿತು. ಇದನ್ನು ಉಲ್ಲೇಖಿಸಿ ಹಕ್ಕುಚ್ಯುತಿ ನೋಟಿಸ್ ನೀಡಲಾಗಿದೆ. ಸೇನಾ ಮುಖ್ಯಸ್ಥರಾಗಿ ಸೇರ್ ಅಧಿಕಾರ ಸ್ವೀಕಾರ ನವದೆಹಲಿ: ಸೇನಾ ಮುಖ್ಯಸ್ಥ ಜನರಲ್ ಉಪೇಂದ್ರ ದ್ವಿವೇದಿ ಮಂಗಳವಾರ ನಿವೃತ್ತಿಯಾದರು. ಇದರ ಬದಲು ಸೇನೆಯ ನೂತನ ಮುಖ್ಯಸ್ಥರಾಗಿ ಲೆಫ್ಟಿನೆಂಟ್ ಜನರಲ್ ರಿತೇಶ್ ಸೇರ್ ಅಧಿಕಾರ ವಹಿಸಿಕೊಂಡರು. ದೇಶದ ಮಹತ್ವದ ಗಡಿಭಾಗವಾಗಿರುವ ಪಶ್ಚಿಮ ಭಾಗದಲ್ಲಿ ನೈಪುಣ್ಯ ಪಡೆದಿರುವ ಹೆಗ್ಗಳಿಕೆ ಸೇರ್ ಅವರಿಗಿದೆ. 40 ವರ್ಷ ಕಾಲ ವಿವಿಧ ಹುದ್ದೆಗಳಲ್ಲಿ ಸುದೀರ್ಘ ಸೇವೆ ಸಲ್ಲಿಸಿದ್ದಾರೆ. ಗ್ರೀಸ್‌ನಲ್ಲೂ ಯುಪಿಐ: ಸೇವೆ ಆರಂಭಿಸಿದ 10ನೇ ದೇಶ ನವದೆಹಲಿ: ಭಾರತದ ಡಿಜಿಟಲ್ ಪಾವತಿ, ಏಕೀಕೃತ ಪಾವತಿ ಇಂಟರ್‌ಫೇಸ್ (ಯುಪಿಐ) ಮತ್ತೊಂದು ಮೈಲಿಗಲ್ಲು ಸ್ಥಾಪಿಸಿದ್ದು, ಗ್ರೀಸ್‌ನಲ್ಲೂ ಈಗ ಯುಪಿಐ ಮೂಲಕ ಡಿಜಿಟಲ್ ವಹಿವಾಟು ಆರಂಭಿಸಿದೆ. ಈ ಬಗ್ಗೆ ವಾಣಿಜ್ಯ ಮತ್ತು ಕೈಗಾರಿಕಾ ಸಚಿವ ಪಿಯೂಷ್ ಗೋಯಲ್ ಅವರು ಈ ಬಗ್ಗೆ ಟ್ವೀಟ್ ಮಾಡಿದ್ದಾರೆ. ಈ ಮೂಲಕ ಯುಪಿಐ ಈಗ ಗ್ರೀಸ್, ಸಿಂಗಾಪುರ, ಯುಎಇ, ಫ್ರಾನ್ಸ್, ಮಾರಿಷಸ್, ನೇಪಾಳ, ಭೂತಾನ್, ಕತಾರ್, ಶ್ರೀಲಂಕಾ ಮತ್ತು ಕಾಂಬೋಡಿಯಾ ಸೇರಿದಂತೆ 10 ದೇಶಗಳಲ್ಲಿ ತನ್ನ ಸೇವೆ ಆರಂಭಿಸಿದಂತಾಗಿದೆ. Content: The Hindu Bureau NEW DELHI Congress general secretary K.C. Venugopal on Tuesday moved a privilege notice against Defence Minister Rajnath Singh in the Lok Sabha, accusing him of misleading Parliament by stating during the Operation Sindoor debate last year that no Indian soldier had been killed. In a letter to Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla, Mr. Venugopal sought initiation of privilege proceedings against the Defence Minister under Rule 223 of the Rules of Procedure and Conduct of Business in the Lok Sabha. The Congress leader said that during the discussion held in July 2025 on the Pahalgam terror attack and Operation Sindoor, Mr. Singh had told the House that no harm had come to Indian soldiers. However, he noted that the government had since acknowledged that six personnel of the armed forces died during the military operation. “The Minister’s statement on the floor of the House that there had been no casualties during Operation Sindoor was clearly misleading and incorrect,” Mr. Venugopal said in the notice, adding that misleading Parliament or withholding information amounted to a breach of privilege and contempt of the House. “How could he, in July 2025, say that no Indian soldier was martyred, and then a year later the forces announce that we have lost six jawans?” he asked in a post on X. ‘Insult to the families’ He said withholding information about the deaths was an insult to the families of the personnel and the armed forces, adding that they had laid down their lives in defence of the nation.

Content:
NEW DELHI: Congress leader KC Venugopal on Tuesday wrote to Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla demanding that privilege proceedings be initiated against defence minister Rajnath Singh for “misleading” Parliament by saying that no Indian soldier was martyred post the Pahalgam terror attack last year.
In his letter to the speaker, Venugopal gave a notice of privilege under Rule 223 of the Rules of Procedure and Conduct of Business in Lok Sabha against the defence minister for having “misled” the House.
Venugopal said that on July 28, 2025, during discussions on the terrorist attack in Pahalgam and the Operation Sindoor that followed, Rajnath Singh said that no harm was caused to the Indian soldiers.
Later, Venugopal said, a statement was issued that said six armed forces personnel had died during Operation Sindoor.
“In view of the foregoing, I request that privilege proceedings be initiated against the minister of defence in the matter,” Venugopal said.

Heading: LETTERS TO THE EDITOR
Summary: This section features multiple letters to the editor addressing diverse issues such as corruption in religious institutions, the need for environmental protection in Ladakh, honoring martyred soldiers, concerns over political defections, and agricultural policy reforms in Punjab. The authors collectively call for greater transparency, accountability, and effective governance to address these challenges. They highlight problems like misuse of funds, environmental damage from tourism, government's perceived ingratitude towards martyrs, weak ideological conviction among leaders, and the groundwater crisis in Punjab due to agricultural practices.
Content: Betrayal of public confidence: Refer to ‘Chanda chori charge’; people donate to religious institutions by virtue of their faith, believing their offerings will serve noble and charitable purposes. Misuse of sacred funds for personal gain, corruption or political ends is a serious betrayal of public trust and an affront to the sanctity of religion. Transparency and accountability strengthen religious institutions. Strong laws and strict penalties are essential to curb embezzlement and ensure that every contribution is used solely for genuine religious, educational and charitable purposes. Ladakh leads the way: With reference to ‘Protecting Ladakh’; the imposition of Rs 50,000 fine each on four tourists for illegal off-roading is a welcome decision. Similar norms should be implemented in states/UTs like Uttarakhand, Himachal Pradesh and Jammu & Kashmir. The greatest environmental damage is caused by tourism under the guise of religious pilgrimage, where visitor numbers become difficult to control. It is up to local authorities and residents to rise above short-term gains and personal benefits and bring in reforms to protect nature. Donations hold public trust: Apropos of ‘Chanda chori charge’; the culprits, irrespective of their position, influence or status must be identified and given exemplary punishment. Temples are among the most sacred places; vulnerability to corruption and political interests raises questions of morality and righteousness. There is an urgent need to create a foolproof system for collection and documentation of donations, whether cash or in kind. Periodical audits, transparency and accountability must become mandatory in big religious institutions. The situation reminds me of a couplet: Yeh dhuan kabhi jhooth nahin bolta yaaro, mere shehar mein koi basti jali to hai. Disservice to Op Sindoor heroes: The delay in informing the nation about the six soldiers who attained martyrdom during Operation Sindoor is disgraceful. A government cannot be ungrateful to the martyrs. Families, soldiers’ units and regiments of the war martyrs deserve utmost respect for their sacrifice. It would be a befitting tribute if the names of the six soldiers are put up on the Baisaran Martyrs Memorial wall, which bears the names of the 26 terror victims in Pahalgam. Leaders lack ideological conviction: Refer to ‘Politics of splits, defections’; MLAs and MPs seem to possess weak ideological moorings these days. A leader chosen by the party for the Rajya Sabha is elected by the MLAs of his/her party, who, in turn, were elected by voters from their constituencies. The anti-defection law should be given a relook so that nobody can dare to escape its strong framework. Farmers not resisting change: Punjab’s worsening groundwater crisis is the result of excessive paddy cultivation, aggravated by distorted agricultural incentives. Expecting diversification of crops without guaranteed procurement is economically unrealistic. The solution lies in extending MSP-backed procurement and developing strong value chains, storage, processing industries and market linkages for alternative produce. Punjab’s farmers are responding rationally to policy incentives, not resisting change. Sustainable farming begins with sustainable market incentives. The government must reform procurement policies.

Heading: Delayed Recognition
Summary: The article criticizes the delayed and unclear official acknowledgement of military casualties, specifically citing Operation Sindoor, and questions the government's transparency. It argues that democracies should openly and promptly honor fallen soldiers to maintain public trust and national conscience, comparing India's practices to other nations. The piece emphasizes that true democratic strength lies in acknowledging sacrifice with clarity and dignity, not in projecting an image of invulnerability.
Content: Every democracy owes two debts to its soldiers. The first is to equip them well enough to fight. The second is to acknowledge them with honesty if they fall. The first secures the nation's borders. The second safeguards its conscience. The recent inscription of the names of six military personnel who died during Operation Sindoor at the National War Memorial has reopened questions that extend beyond party politics. The issue is not whether these brave men were honoured. They were. They received gallantry awards, their families were presented with the medals, and they have now found a place on the nation's Roll of Honour. The question is why a clear, official acknowledgement of their sacrifice as casualties of Operation Sindoor came only a year later. The government's defence deserves consideration. It has pointed out that the Director General of Military Operations referred to casualties in May 2025, gallantry awards were announced in August, and the memorial inscription followed established protocol. It has also clarified that Defence Minister Rajnath Singh's statement in Parliament that no Indian soldiers had been harmed was intended to rebut claims that Indian fighter pilots had been killed during the operation. Yet the controversy has persisted because the minister's recorded remarks were broader than that explanation. They conveyed the impression that India had suffered no military casualties. If a clarification becomes necessary a year later, it is reasonable to conclude that official communication left room for misunderstanding. This matters because democracies do not diminish military success by acknowledging combat losses. They reinforce public trust by doing so. No modern army can expect to wage operations without risk. Soldiers know it, their families know it, and the nation knows it. What the public expects in return is candour once operational requirements have been met and next of kin have been informed. India has long understood this principle. During the Kargil conflict, casualty lists were released regularly and the nation watched as fallen soldiers were accorded military honours before being laid to rest. The Pulwama martyrs were identified immediately and mourned across the country. Other established democracies follow similar practices. Whether in the United States, the United Kingdom, Australia or Israel, operational details may remain classified, but the identities of personnel killed in action are normally made public after their families have been notified. National remembrance is never treated as a military secret. The nation should not have had to piece together the human cost of a military campaign through local reports, medal citations and, eventually, inscriptions on a memorial wall. The strength of a democracy lies not in projecting an image of invulnerability but in possessing the confidence to acknowledge sacrifice with clarity and dignity. Those who lay down their lives for the Republic deserve not only medals and memorials, but also the simple honour of being named, openly and without delay. That is the least a grateful nation owes its fallen.

It highlights the importance of--a--Ac countability in institutions that man age public donations. b--Transparent governance of religious trusts. c-- Strong financial oversight.d--Preserv ing the faith of millions of devotees.e --Ensuring that sacred institutions up hold the highest standards of integrity. Distinction from the Ayodhya land dispute--It is important to distinguish this controversy from the historic Ay odhya title dispute.The land dispute culminated in the 2019 judgement of the Supreme Court of India, which awarded the disputed land for the con struction of the Ram Mandir while di recting that an alternative five-acre plot be allotted for the construction of mosque.The Ram temple was conse crated in January 2024.It was inaugu rated by Prime Minister Narendra Modi.Present Ayodhya row is an ad ministrative and criminal investiga tion into alleged theft and misman agement of temple donations,not a re vival of the Ram Mandir-Babri Masjid legal dispute.The investigation is on going, and legal responsibility will ul timately be determined by the courts based on the evidence.The current Ay odhya row is fundamentally an issue of governance and accountability rather than a religious or legal dispute over the temple itself. Addressing the inaugural session of the Valedictory Gujarat Regional Conference in Vadodara, he said that the country's defense industry has seen significant changes in recent decades. Colonel (Retd.) Rohit Chaudhary, head of the party's Veterans Department, said that a privilege motion should be brought against the Defense Minister in Parliament, and Prime Minister Narendra Modi and the BJP should apologize to the public (Agency). New Delhi, dated 30 The main opposition party, Congress, has intensified its attack on the BJP-led Modi government for failing to name six military personnel martyred during Operation Sindoor more than a year ago and include their names in the National War Memorial. According to The Hindu, Congress on Monday (June 28) demanded the resignation of Union Defense Minister Rajnath Singh, accusing him of saying "buddhu" in Parliament. (It is noteworthy that during a discussion on Operation Sindoor in the Lok Sabha during the Parliament session on July 28, 2021, Defense Minister Rajnath Singh had told the opposition, "If you want to ask a question, then ask if any of our brave soldiers have suffered casualties in this operation. The answer is no.") "It is noteworthy that Operation Sindoor was carried out on April 22 last year to avenge the terrorist attack that occurred earlier, in which 26 civilians (mostly tourists) were killed. In this operation, the Indian armed forces eliminated nine terrorists in Pakistan and Pakistan-occupied Kashmir; these locations were reportedly linked to Jaish-e-Mohammed and Lashkar-e-Taiba. However, no formal announcement was made at the time regarding the terrorists killed during this operation. However, the Indian government has officially released the names of six Indian soldiers who lost their lives during this operation. In a press conference, Colonel (Retd.) Rohit Chaudhary, head of the party's Veterans Department, stated that Defense Minister Rajnath Singh has insulted martyrs by speaking falsely about Operation Sindoor in Parliament, thereby depriving them of due public recognition and honor. He also said that a privilege motion should be brought against the Defense Minister in Parliament, and Prime Minister Narendra Modi and the BJP should apologize to the public. Wing Commander Anoop Acharya claimed that previous governments honored every soldier who made the supreme sacrifice publicly. He accused the current government of "politicizing the armed forces." He further said, "The Modi government, which politicizes the army and soldiers, has repeatedly betrayed the country and its soldiers." Colonel Chaudhary accused the BJP of using soldiers as a "tool" while seeking votes for the armed forces. He said, "When Rajnath Singh was saying 'buddhu' in Parliament that no soldier was killed, BJP MPs were clapping. None of them have the right to sit in Gulmarg." Chaudhary told reporters, "Modi Modi and BJP MPs should publicly apologize. He also reiterated his demands to cancel the Agnipath recruitment scheme. Colonel Chaudhary said that he would request the top leadership of Congress to bring a privilege motion against the Defense Minister. Significantly, the central government has dismissed the opposition's allegations and said that the country has paid tribute to the "martyred soldiers as soon as possible" and their memory has been honored with full glory and respect. In this regard, the Ministry of Defense issued a statement saying, "Some social media posts have attempted to misrepresent the speech given by the Defense Minister in Parliament on July 28, 2021." These posts have made a false claim by selecting a small part of the speech, stating that the Defense Minister is saying that no Indian soldier was killed during Operation Sindoor. This claim is deliberately misleading and completely factually incorrect. Meanwhile, the Ministry of Defense claims that the minister's comments were taken out of context and misrepresented in social media posts.

Summary: The article criticizes the delayed official recognition of six military personnel who died during Operation Sindoor, with their names inscribed on the National War Memorial a year later. It argues that while the government provided explanations, delayed and unclear communication regarding combat losses can erode public trust. The piece emphasizes the importance of prompt and transparent acknowledgment of soldiers' sacrifices for a grateful nation.
Content: Every democracy owes two debts to its soldiers. The first is to equip them well enough to fight. The second is to acknowledge them with honesty if they fall. The first secures the nation's borders. The second safeguards its conscience. The recent inscription of the names of six military personnel who died during Operation Sindoor at the National War Memorial has reopened questions that extend beyond party politics. The issue is not whether these brave men were honoured. They were. They received gallantry awards, their families were presented with the medals, and they have now found a place on the nation's Roll of Honour. The question is why a clear, official acknowledgement of their sacrifice as casualties of Operation Sindoor came only a year later. The government's defence deserves consideration. It has pointed out that the Director General of Military Operations referred to casualties in May 2025, gallantry awards were announced in August, and the memorial inscription followed established protocol. It has also clarified that Defence Minister Rajnath Singh's statement in Parliament that no Indian soldiers had been harmed was intended to rebut claims that Indian fighter pilots had been killed during the operation. Yet the controversy has persisted because the minister's recorded remarks were broader than that explanation. They conveyed the impression that India had suffered no military casualties. If a clarification becomes necessary a year later, it is reasonable to conclude that official communication left room for misunderstanding. This matters because democracies do not diminish military success by acknowledging combat losses. They reinforce public trust by doing so. No modern army can expect to wage operations without risk. Soldiers know it, their families know it, and the nation knows it. What the public expects in return is candour once operational requirements have been met and next of kin have been informed. India has long understood this principle. During the Kargil conflict, casualty lists were released regularly and the nation watched as fallen soldiers were accorded military honours before being laid to rest. The Pulwama martyrs were identified immediately and mourned across the country. Other established democracies follow similar practices. Whether in the United States, the United Kingdom, Australia or Israel, operational details may remain classified, but the identities of personnel killed in action are normally made public after their families have been notified. National remembrance is never treated as a military secret. The nation should not have had to piece together the human cost of a military campaign through local reports, medal citations and, eventually, inscriptions on a memorial wall. The strength of a democracy lies not in projecting an image of invulnerability but in possessing the confidence to acknowledge sacrifice with clarity and dignity. Those who lay down their lives for the Republic deserve not only medals and memorials, but also the simple honour of being named, openly and without delay. That is the least a grateful nation owes its fallen.

Heading: Reports of Chinese infiltration in Arunachal Pradesh baseless, Army rejects claims, says border is under control
Summary: The Indian Army has refuted claims of Chinese infiltration and illegal camps in Arunachal Pradesh, asserting that the Line of Actual Control (LAC) is fully secure and under control, with soldiers vigilantly deployed. This comes after a local organization alleged Chinese encroachment on tribal lands and infrastructure development in areas previously under Indian control. Additionally, the retiring Army Chief, General Upendra Dwivedi, delivered a stern message to hostile nations and terrorists, declaring that India's fear of nuclear threats from Pakistan is over and any misadventure will be met with a precise and destructive response.
Content:
New Delhi, Agency. The Indian Army has completely rejected claims of Chinese army infiltration and setting up camps in Arunachal Pradesh, calling them baseless. Following claims by the local organization Nah Welfare Society, the Army clarified that the Indian territory on the LAC is completely secure and soldiers are vigilantly deployed. The Indian Army has outright rejected claims of new encroachments and military camps being built by the Chinese army in Arunachal Pradesh. Social media and some media reports were claiming that Chinese soldiers had infiltrated within the Indian border. The Army issued a strong official statement calling all these reports completely false, misleading, and without any basis. The situation on the Line of Actual Control is fully under control and Indian soldiers are vigilantly deployed. This entire dispute began when a local organization, Nah Welfare Society, from Taksing, a remote border area in the Upper Subansiri district of Arunachal Pradesh, submitted a memorandum to the district administration. The president of this organization, Keru Chaudar, had claimed that the Chinese army had gradually advanced into Indian territory over the past 10 to 15 years. The memorandum alleged that China had taken control of the traditional hunting, cattle grazing, and agricultural lands of the local Nah tribal community. According to the claims, in areas that were completely under India's control until 2020, the PLA has now built roads, bridges, and permanent military camps. The organization specifically named five sensitive locations: Oying, Paniyar, Marpan, Potrong Lake, and Tindigantang, which hold sacred religious significance for the local people. As soon as this letter from the local organization came to light, political and social unrest intensified in the state. Nacho area MLA Nakap Nalo and former MLA Ponga Bage, calling this issue related to national security, demanded an administrative-level inquiry to alleviate the fear of border residents. On the other hand, the Arunachal Pradesh Congress Committee also demanded that the central government immediately clarify the situation on this sensitive matter and ensure border security. In view of the escalating dispute, the Indian security establishment immediately clarified the situation. According to military sources, Indian soldiers are continuously and very vigilantly conducting Long-Range Patrolling (LRP) on the LAC. Both sides are working within their respective borders on infrastructure development along the China border, but any talk of new encroachment or illegal Chinese camps in Indian territory is completely false and fabricated. The state government led by Chief Minister Pema Khandu and the Union Ministry of Defence have clarified that the borders of Arunachal Pradesh are completely secure. In recent years, the Indian government has strengthened the network of roads, strategic bridges, and forward posts in border areas at a record pace.
