Heading: Operation Sindoor martyr Naik's family should get pension
Summary: The article criticizes the Modi government for its handling of pension and welfare benefits for the family of martyr Murali Naik, who was killed in Operation Sindoor. Despite spending crores on promoting the operation, the government is fighting a court case against providing pension and healthcare to Naik's elderly parents, citing bureaucratic rules. The author argues that changing rules for exceptional cases like martyred soldiers is necessary and that pension is a right, not charity.
Content:
The controversy over revealing the names of brave soldiers martyred in Operation Sindoor years later is raging. In this controversy, we want to talk about another shocking fact related to the martyrs, on which the Modi government is silent.
Among the brave soldiers martyred in Operation Sindoor, one name is Abhinavarya Murali Naik. Abhinavarya Murali Naik was martyred by Pakistani firing on the Poonch border during Operation Sindoor on November 9, 2022.
Murali's elderly parents had to apply to the Bombay High Court to receive pension and healthcare benefits. This government is refusing to provide pension and healthcare benefits to Murali's elderly parents because pension and other benefits are not included in the service rules for officers.
According to current rules, Abhinavarya or his family do not receive any pension or lifelong family welfare benefits in case of death during service or after completing service. While ordinary soldiers receive all benefits including pension and gratuity upon joining the army, Abhinavarya receives a 'Seva Nidhi' fund once at the end of each year.
Even if martyred within a short period, a limited death compensation package is received, but based on that, the martyr's family cannot receive a pension. It is still understandable if Abhinavarya does not receive a pension or other benefits upon retirement, but if his family does not receive benefits even when he is martyred for the country, that is considered extreme ingratitude.
Instead of removing this ingratitude, this government is fighting a case in court to prevent the family of martyr Abhinavarya from receiving benefits. Lawyers are being paid fees to fight this case, but the martyr's family will not be given benefits! What kind of stubbornness is this?
The Modi government feels proud of Operation Sindoor and has spent crores of rupees on its promotion.
Crores of rupees have been spent on various programs to praise Operation Sindoor, but when it comes to giving a pension of twenty-five to fifty thousand rupees a month to a martyr's family, it causes a stomach ache. What kind of low mentality is this?
There is no need to do anything special to provide healthcare and other benefits to the family of martyr Murali Naik. There are numerous Army Medical Hospitals in this country, so what difference would it make if the martyr Naik's family members receive treatment there? Citizens of the country already receive free healthcare facilities under the Ayushman Yojana. The martyr Naik's family should receive those benefits.
The Modi government citing the rules for Abhinavarya's service is proof of sheer bureaucracy. There is nothing wrong with adhering to rules in normal circumstances.
If the system is stuck, it's fine, but for the family of a brave soldier martyred for the country, these are not normal circumstances. Giving one's life for the security of the country is the ultimate sacrifice, and changing rules in these extraordinary circumstances is not wrong.
The government has defended itself by saying that if a pension is given to Murali's family, similar demands will arise in other cases in the future, increasing the burden on the government. This defense is utter nonsense because the incident of Abhinavarya being martyred is not an everyday occurrence, nor do you have to give pension to the family of a martyred Abhinavarya every year. Such incidents rarely happen and are exceptional.
Rules can be changed in exceptional cases, and no one would object to that. There should be no objection to giving pension to the family of a brave soldier martyred for this country.
Unfortunately, the public in this country is so weak that it does not take pride in its martyrs and sits with its tail between its legs against the injustice done to the families of martyrs.
We pay tribute to martyrs, salute them, and praise their bravery, but there is no support for their families to stand on their own feet. Murali's mother has been fighting a case in the High Court since November 2022, but no one is ready to help her.
It is shameful that one has to extend a hand for the families of soldiers martyred for this country to live the rest of their lives with dignity, but it is even more shameful that they are being harassed and have to resort to the High Court. Citing rigid rules and treating the martyr's family like beggars, humiliating them, only happens in this country.
When the Modi government introduced the Abhinavarya scheme, there was strong opposition to it. Accusations were made that the Modi government was recruiting salaried employees instead of passionate soldiers for the country's security. The rules for giving pension to the families of brave soldiers who sacrificed their lives for the country were criticized.
The Modi government claimed this criticism was opposition propaganda, and the secretariat stated that the government would also take care of Abhinavarya's families, but after seeing that Murali Naik's family has to fight for compensation, it seems this criticism is true.
If the Modi government wants to prove this criticism wrong, it should provide pension and other benefits to the family of martyr Naik. Instead of showing that families fighting for the country receive monthly pensions in propaganda, the families of soldiers martyred while fighting for the country should actually receive pensions. This pension is their right, not help or charity.

Heading: Controversy over martyrdom is sad
Summary: The article discusses the controversy surrounding Operation Sindoor, where six Indian soldiers were martyred in May 2025, with their names being revealed a year later. It criticizes the Modi government for allegedly politicizing the army and concealing information about casualties, while the government defends its actions and honors the soldiers at the National War Memorial. The piece concludes by questioning why the government's decisions frequently lead to such controversies and accuses the BJP of politicizing sensitive national security matters.
Content:
Six soldiers were martyred in Operation Sindoor, launched against Pakistan in May 2025, and their names have now been made public by the Modi government a year later. The names of the six martyred soldiers are etched on the National War Memorial. The spirit of putting one's life on the line and making the ultimate sacrifice for the defense and self-respect of the country cannot be praised enough, nor can sufficient gratitude be expressed. Ideally, subjects like martyrdom should not be subjected to political debate or controversy. However, the Modi government has started using the army for political gain. That is why there is controversial rhetoric regarding martyrdom. In fact, during the Lok Sabha debate on Operation Sindoor during the Parliament session on July 28, 2025, Defense Minister Rajnath Singh told the opposition, 'If you want to ask questions, ask if our brave soldiers suffered any damage in this operation, and the answer is no.' The video of the Defense Minister's statement is circulating on social media, in which he emphasized it, and then the Home Minister Amit Shah and all BJP MPs present in the House welcomed this statement by thumping their desks and smiling. Hearing this statement, it is clear that Rajnath Singh is explicitly saying that our soldiers suffered no harm. Rajnath Singh further said in the same statement, 'Opposition members kept asking how many of our planes were shot down, I think their question does not correctly represent national sentiment. They never once asked how many enemy planes our forces shot down. If they have to ask a question, their question should be whether India destroyed terrorist hideouts, and the answer is yes. If you have to ask a question, ask if Operation Sindoor was successful, and the answer is yes.' The way the Defense Minister responded by taking the name of the opposition and questioning the intent of their questions made it clear that the Modi government is politicizing the army. The Modi government wants to take sole credit for the army's actions by raising every question as if it were the Modi government's army. Whereas, whatever the army does, only the army deserves praise, not any political party.

However, when the Defense Minister said that no soldier was harmed, it was assumed that India caused significant damage to Pakistan in Operation Sindoor, but India suffered no loss. Although Pakistan claimed to have shot down fighter jets and killed more than 10 soldiers, these claims were not taken seriously. Now that the names of six soldiers have come out, the opposition has raised questions. Congress leader Pawan Khera said that after the initial attack, the government decided to mislead Parliament regarding India's retaliatory action against Pakistan. He wrote that the government, which wraps itself in the tricolor and never tires of talking about nationalism, did not give these brave soldiers the respect and remembrance they deserved. Pawan Khera said that these heroes' names should be etched in the collective memory of the country forever. Their families should feel that the entire country is remembering their sacrifice with respect. But contrary to this, the BJP government decided to hide their martyrdom from the country for a whole year. Similar statements were made by other parties, so now the Ministry of Defense has clarified that some social media posts are trying to misrepresent the speech given by the Defense Minister in Parliament on July 28, 2025. These posts selectively pick a small part of the speech to falsely claim that the Defense Minister said no Indian soldier died during Operation Sindoor. This claim was deliberately presented in a misleading way and is factually incorrect. It should be kept clear that when the Defense Minister was giving his speech in Parliament, at that time, some parts of the media and social media were continuously spreading false propaganda that Indian Air Force pilots were killed during Operation Sindoor. This claim was completely false, but it was being continuously spread with the aim of undermining the success of the operation and demoralizing the public.

The Defense Minister's related statement was given in response to this specific and misleading propaganda. Therefore, his statement should be understood in that context. The Ministry of Defense's statement further said that the Ministry of Defense was committed to honoring the courage and capability of the Indian armed forces and expressing respect, gratitude, and devotion to every member of the Indian armed forces and the Government of India, especially towards those brave soldiers who made the ultimate sacrifice to protect the nation. In honor of this supreme sacrifice, the government has ensured that the names of these brave soldiers are inscribed on the walls of the National War Memorial. The kind of clarification the Ministry of Defense has provided has never happened in the past. India has been involved in battles before, in which a large number of soldiers have been martyred. These battles occurred during both Congress and BJP governments, but no one ever had to give such a clarification. The Modi government should consider why its decisions get embroiled in such controversies. Even when the first attack happened, terrorists did not ask about religion or caste, but the BJP made a horrific terrorist incident a part of cheap politics by making posters, and now a new controversy has arisen regarding Operation Sindoor, which is not appropriate in any way.

Government said - Attempt was made to misrepresent the speech given in Parliament
Summary: A controversy has erupted over the public release of names of six soldiers martyred in 'Operation Sindoor', with Congress accusing the government of hiding information and disrespecting martyrs. The Ministry of Defence refuted these claims, stating that the Defence Minister's speech was misrepresented and that the government had already honored the martyrs through various means, including inscribing their names on the National War Memorial and awarding gallantry medals. The article details the names of the martyred soldiers and the honors they received.
Content:
New Delhi, June 29 (Agency). A controversy has erupted after the names of 6 soldiers martyred in Operation Sindoor were made public. The Congress has accused the government of hiding information and not honoring the martyrs. Following this, the Ministry of Defence issued a statement saying that an attempt was made to misrepresent the Defence Minister's speech given in Parliament on July 28, 2025. The Ministry stated that the claim that the martyrs were honored for the first time is false.
In fact, on June 26, the government had for the first time made public the names of 6 soldiers martyred during Operation Sindoor. These names were included in the Roll of Honour on the National War Memorial website. The names of these 6 soldiers were also permanently inscribed on special granite plaques at the National War Memorial near India Gate in New Delhi. The controversy arose as soon as the names were released.
After the names were released, Congress leader Pawan Khera said there are only two possibilities. Either the Defence Minister was unaware that 6 soldiers had been martyred when he addressed Parliament. If so, there are serious questions about the minister, who is unaware of the affairs of his own ministry. Or he knew the truth and yet he chose to mislead Parliament. This is even more serious.
Defence Minister Rajnath Singh had said in Parliament on July 28, 2025, "Our opposition people ask how many of our planes crashed. They never asked us how many enemy planes our army shot down. If you want to ask a question, then ask if our brave soldiers suffered any damage in this operation? The answer is - no." It is on this statement that Congress is accusing the Defence Minister of misleading. According to the Ministry, the then Director General of Military Operations paid tribute to the martyrs in a press conference held on May 11, 2025. Information about gallantry awards for the martyrs was made public in a press release on August 14, 2025. The army paid tribute to the martyrs through social media. On October 8, 2025, the Air Chief honored the family members of the martyred sergeant. On January 15, 2026, the Army Chief presented medals to the family members of 3 martyrs.
The martyred soldiers include Sub Major Pawan Kumar of 10 Infantry Brigade Headquarters, Rifleman Sunil Kumar of the 4th Battalion of Jammu and Kashmir Light Infantry Regiment, Lance Naik Dinesh Kumar of 5th Field Regiment, Agniveer Mood Murali Nayak of 851 Light Regiment, Havildar Sunil Kumar Singh of 237 Field Workshop, and Sergeant Surendra Kumar of 39th Wing of the Air Force.
Rifleman Sunil Kumar was posthumously awarded the Vir Chakra, the country's third-highest wartime honor, and Sergeant Surendra Kumar received the Vayu Sena Medal.

Summary: President Droupadi Murmu presented numerous gallantry awards, including Kirti Chakras, Vir Chakras, and Shaurya Chakras, at a Defence Investiture Ceremony in New Delhi. Additionally, police officers Laxman Kewat and Rameshwar Prasad Deshmukh were honored for their courage in anti-Naxal operations, and Sepoy Janjal Praveen Prabhakar was posthumously awarded the Kirti Chakra, received by his emotional mother.
Content:
NEW DELHI (A). President Droupadi Murmu on Monday presented 7 Kirti Chakras, 15 Vir Chakras, and 29 Shaurya Chakras at the Defence Investiture Ceremony at Rashtrapati Bhavan. Among the recipients was Group Captain Manish Arora of the Indian Air Force, who was part of Operation Sindoor and was honored with the Vir Chakra. Also included was Lieutenant Colonel Nitesh Bharti Shukla, who killed 3 terrorists on the LoC. Besides this, Major Aditya Pratap Singh, who showed bravery during a military operation in the border area of Arunachal Pradesh, was also awarded the Shaurya Chakra. Police officers Laxman Kewat and Rameshwar Prasad Deshmukh, who showed courage during anti-Naxal operations in Chhattisgarh, also received this honor.

Mother wept hugging President Droupadi Murmu: Sepoy Janjal Praveen Prabhakar was posthumously awarded Kirti Chakra. He was martyred in July 2024 during an anti-terrorist operation in Kulgam, Jammu and Kashmir, where he killed two terrorists in an encounter. His mother reached the stage to receive this honor.

Group Captain Manish Arora: Group Captain Manish Arora of the Indian Air Force was awarded the Vir Chakra. He participated in an air strike on terrorist hideouts in Pakistan while flying a Sukhoi-30 MKI aircraft during Operation Sindoor. He was given this honor for the bravery shown in this operation. Manish Arora has also previously received the Shaurya Chakra.

NEW DELHI. President Droupadi Murmu on Monday presented distinguished military honors to senior officers of the armed forces at the Defence Investiture Ceremony 2026 (Phase-2) held in New Delhi. Air Marshal Ashutosh Dixit was awarded the Param Vishisht Seva Medal (PVSM), Army Chief-designate Lieutenant General Dheeraj Seth was awarded the Uttam Yudh Seva Medal (UYSM), and Major General Mandeep Singh was awarded the Sena Medal. Major General Mandeep Singh, General Officer Commanding of the White Tiger Armoured Division, was honored with the Sena Medal for his distinguished services. Earlier, on June 8, President Droupadi Murmu had given a total of 51 gallantry awards to personnel and officers of the armed forces, central armed police forces, and police of states and union territories in the first phase of the Defence Investiture Ceremony 2026.

This was the first time since the military operation conducted by the Indian armed forces in May 2025 that the government released the names of these six personnel. Amid the row surrounding the six martyrs of Operation Sindoor, the defence ministry has said the nation paid homage to them at the "earliest opportunity", and their memory shall always be honoured with the dignity and reverence it deserves. The government had earlier said some social media posts sought to "misrepresent" Defence Minister Singh's address in Parliament in July 2025 and "selectively" quoted an isolated portion of it to "falsely imply" that he had claimed that "no Indian soldier lost his life during Operation Sindoor". In his remarks at the presser, Chaudhry claimed that Singh has "insulted" the martyrs of 'Operation Sindoor' and overlooked them. Content:
Bengaluru, June 29 (Agency). Karnataka Congress's senior state leader BK Hariprasad on Monday demanded the resignation of Defense Minister Rajnath Singh. He alleged that the Defense Minister misled Parliament on the issue of Indian soldiers martyred during Operation Sindoor. This controversy emerged after the names of these six soldiers, who made the supreme sacrifice during the operation, were recently inscribed on the National War Memorial.

In his post on social media X, Hariprasad referred to Rajnath Singh's statement made in Parliament in 2025. He claimed that the Defense Minister had clearly stated in the House that no Indian soldier died during Operation Sindoor. However, with the names of six martyred soldiers coming to light later, this claim by the government came under question.

Hariprasad wrote in his post, Defense Minister Rajnath Singh had clearly told Parliament that no Indian soldier lost his life during Operation Sindoor. But later, the BJP government publicly released the names of those soldiers who made the supreme sacrifice for the country. This is a serious contradiction. If Parliament has been misled on such a serious matter of national importance, then accountability must be fixed. Defense Minister Rajnath Singh should resign for providing false information to Parliament. Our martyrs deserve truth, honesty, and respect, not contradictory statements.

The names of six Indian armed forces personnel martyred during Operation Sindoor, which lasted for four days against Pakistan in May 2025, have now been inscribed on the National War Memorial in New Delhi. Following this, the issue took on a political color.

As the controversy escalated, the Ministry of Defense issued a clarification on Saturday, stating that all six soldiers who made the supreme sacrifice in Operation Sindoor were honored by the country at the first available opportunity. The ministry completely rejected claims that their sacrifice was publicly acknowledged for the first time recently.

The Ministry of Defense stated in its statement that misleading news was circulated in some sections of the media and social media, claiming that the sacrifice of these six soldiers was recognized for the first time recently. According to the ministry, in an official press conference held on May 11, 2025, the then Director General of Military Operations had paid tribute to all these martyrs and specifically mentioned their supreme sacrifice during Operation Sindoor.

The ministry also stated that all these martyred soldiers were awarded gallantry medals. Official information regarding this was provided in a press release issued on August 14, 2025. According to the ministry, this honor was a symbol of formally recognizing their bravery and sacrifice at the national level, in line with the highest traditions of the Indian Armed Forces.

Heading: Delayed honour Operational secrecy during wars is a must, but there must be accountability
Summary: The article criticizes the Indian government for its delayed acknowledgment of six soldiers killed in Operation Sindoor in 2025, a cross-border military strike in Pakistan following a terrorist attack in Pahalgam. It argues that the government's lack of transparency, selective disclosure of facts, and initial denial of casualties undermined its credibility and democratic accountability. The piece emphasizes the necessity of public accounting for war's outcomes to ensure wise decision-making.
Content: War is secretive and strategy may require deception. But that is no good explanation for the fact that the Narendra Modi government took over a year before formally acknowledging that six soldiers had lost their lives in Operation Sindoor in 2025. India had launched cross-border military strikes in Pakistan in retaliation for the Pahalgam terrorist attack, in April 2025, that killed 26 innocent people. From the beginning, the government has been reluctant to share any meaningful details of Operation Sindoor even as it continuously kept the hyperbolic self-congratulatory posture. Its decision to not publicly acknowledge and honour the supreme sacrifice of the fallen soldiers contemporaneously was hardly a sign of any wise strategy. Casualties can happen in any military operation and that is a key consideration in any military planning, and more importantly, the political decision to go to war or not. Not being transparent about losses, human and material, may serve the political interests of the ruling party, but not national interest. By trying to be clever and selective about facts, the government undermined its own credibility and did a disservice to those who paid with their lives. Soon after the operation concluded in May 2025, the then Director General of Military Operations (DGMO), Lieutenant General Rajiv Ghai, paid tribute, during a press briefing on May 11, 2025, to Indian military personnel who had made the supreme sacrifice, though their names were not disclosed. The cremations were done with full military honours. In August 2025, Air Chief Marshal A.P. Singh visited the family of Sergeant Surendra Kumar, who was killed during the operation, while the Ministry of Defence also announced gallantry awards for the fallen personnel. Tributes were simultaneously carried on the Indian Army’s official social media platforms. In the Lok Sabha on July 28, 2025, Defence Minister Rajnath Singh said that “no Indian soldiers were harmed” during Operation Sindoor. Following accusations that it has misled Parliament, the government is now explaining that the Minister’s remarks were made in the context of reports that Indian aircraft were shot down and were meant to clarify that no pilot was killed during the mission. The government has also maintained that details relating to aircraft losses during the conflict remain operationally sensitive and refused to disclose them. There is a distinction to be made between operational secrecy and requirements of public accountability. War is a stark demonstration of the fact that it is the public that always pays for all actions of the government. A public accounting of the gains and the losses is the best way to ensure wise decision making. +

Amid the row surrounding the six martyrs of Operation Sindoor, the defence ministry has said the nation paid homage to them at the "earliest opportunity", and their memory shall always be honoured with the dignity and reverence it deserves. The government had earlier said some social media posts sought to "misrepresent" Defence Minister Singh's address in Parliament in July 2025 and "selectively" quoted an isolated portion of it to "falsely imply" that he had claimed that "no Indian soldier lost his life during Operation Sindoor". "Singh lied in the House that no soldier was lost in 'Operation Sindoor'. Inside the BJP, only lies are told and deception is carried out...The foundation of the Modi government is built on lies; they have no right to remain in power," Chaudhry said.

Heading: Is India-Pak dialogue going to happen finally?
Summary: The article discusses the growing buzz around India-Pakistan dialogue, noting internal calls for talks despite a highly explosive situation at the LoC and Pakistan's continued support for terrorism. It highlights India's firm stance on holding Pakistan accountable for atrocities and its commitment to protecting people in PoJK. The author concludes that while dialogue is necessary, the nation's mood remains distrustful of Pakistan's sincerity in curbing terrorism.
Content: Edit Is India-Pak dialogue going to happen finally? Hosabale's words have encouraged the otherwise muted voices to a whisper, which have now become loud appeals Talks Arun Joshi ajoshi57@gmail.com There is a lot of buzz about the possibility of an India-Pakistan dialogue, as it being touted an inescapable reality. The thesis is that sooner or later it will happen, no matter how frozen relations between the two countries are. Is the stage set for dialogue to finally happen? At the moment, certain issues need greater and immediate attention regarding India-Pakistan relations. First, a highly explosive situation is developing across the Line of Control (LoC)- Pakistan-Occupied Jammu and Kashmir (PoJK). Dozens have been killed and scores injured, while thousands are holding a massive sit-in (dharma) to protest against the Pakistani establishment. Second, China and Pakistan are increasingly adopting identical vocabulary regarding Jammu and Kashmir in their joint statements. This cannot be dismissed merely as a display of an Indo-clad friendship, rather, it reflects a growing mutual recognition that both nations are actively working to advance each other's strategic interests. Third, the overall international scenario in which America and Europe are full of praise for Pakistan as a mediator - read messenger - between the US and Iran. Even when the ceasefire is teetering, Pakistan comes in for praise. Trump has reversed his opinion about Pakistan - once described by him as a terror state in his description that played a double game with Washington (January 1, 2018), to the Pakistan army chief, Field Marshall Asim Munir, being his favourite and good friend. Fourth, India's own stature as the loud and powerful voice of the Global South. Its status brings special responsibilities in the ongoing world order. India's pursuit of the Viksit Bharat goal is also dependent upon the external environment, and we are just 21 years from that cherished goal. Fifth, are calls from within urging India to open doors for dialogue with Pakistan. RSS leader Dattatrey Hosabale was the first to make this statement, which was directed at the Prime Minister, though he did not name him. The plea for dialogue itself made it obvious because the leader of the country, Narendra Modi, alone could take this kind of decision. Kashmir's chief cleric Mirwaiz Umar Farooq reminded his followers, and all South Asian countries during his speech at Jamia Masjid, Srinagar, heart of Kashmir, that Modi is the longest-serving Prime Minister of Independent India. He carries with him a mandate that no other leader in the democratic world, particularly in South Asia has. These voices have their merit. It, of course, is for Modi to take a call, as he represents the collective spirit and vote of the people of the country. These calls have their own importance as we all have seen layer after layer of ice accumulating over the glacial nature of Indo-Pak relation now for more than a year. The war of words between the two countries has made it only worse. What the RSS leader did was that he broke the ice at a time when dialogue with Pakistan is deemed as a riskinviting idea. Hosabale's words have encouraged the otherwise muted voices to a whisper, which have now become loud appeals. The TV warriors from both sides of the border keep on telling their domestic audiences that the talks will be a dangerous and devastating affair because neither of the two countries can be trusted for enduring lasting peace in the region. And, take it from me, that they will be the first ones to weigh the merits of sitting across the table when this happens. They work on narratives, the nuances of which are not known to them. They are reckless drivers, unmindful of the geopolitical crashes they cause. We are all witnesses to the crashes they caused during Operation Sindoor. Nothing more needs to be said about such anchors and the screens they occupy to disseminate misinformation and causing strategic problems for the forces in deeply crisis situation. The decision on the dialogue with Pakistan will have to be taken against the backdrop of the Pahalgam massacre of April 22, 2025, and Operation Sindoor (May 7 to 10, 2025). These two developments – the first one being an act of extreme savagery in which 26 civilians were mowed down by gunfire in the beautiful meadow of Baisaran, near Pahalgam, and the other being the retaliation for that massacre – must shape the way forward. “ The nation's mood is not in favour of negotiations and feels profoundly distrustful that Pakistan will deliver a genuine-end to terrorism. Todate, the Indian response has been to condemn the human rights violations and ask the international community to hold Pakistan accountable for what all is happening there. This falls far short of the expectations of the people across the LoC and those living on this side. Pakistan is dubbing the agitators in Pakistan occupied Jammu and Kashmir, as Indian agents. It should be made clear to Pakistan that they are not the Indian agents but Indians. Pakistan has no locus standi regarding the land and the people there. There are two ways of addressing this: intensify the international diplomatic campaign to force the Pakistan government to cease its atrocities, or India directly talk to Pakistan and declare enough is enough. India cannot leave its people abandoned in the occupied territories. During the Iran-US conflict, the Indian leadership took a firm stand that it is concerned about 10 million Indian citizens and workers spread across the Gulf States. The same approach will have to be applied with regard to the people in PoJK, they will have to be saved. One of the ways of doing so is to talk to Pakistan. It is time for India to validate its assertion that it will talk to Pakistan on PoJK only. Let the beginning be made. The people of Pakistan have been fed a misleading narrative that India is an aggressor and it doesn't want the Pakistani state to exist. This misinformation is a lifeline for the institution that controls Pakistan's domestic and foreign policy. Kashmiris themselves were at the forefront in telling terrorists and their sponsors that they have seen through their game and will not fall into their trap again. They were supportive of Indian actions against terrorists within and across the border. But what happened, and its implications, can be ignored only at the risk of courting long-term losses, unless the other side commits by way of words and real-time action to curbing terrorism. With that foreign mindset, they constantly divide and undermine India at the behest of foreign powers," Poonawalla said in a video statement. Heading: Martyr Dinesh Kumar's name registered in the 'Roll of Honor' of the National War Memorial
Summary: Lance Naik Dinesh Kumar Sharma, who sacrificed his life during Operation Sindoor, has been honored by having his name inscribed in the 'Roll of Honor' at the National War Memorial in New Delhi. The family, however, urges the government to fulfill other promises, such as naming the village after the martyr and building a park in his memory.
Content: Team Action India Santosh Garg Palwal. The name of Lance Naik Dinesh Kumar Sharma, a resident of Nagla Mohammadpur village, who made the supreme sacrifice while defending the country during Operation Sindoor, has been registered in the 'Roll of Honor' of the National War Memorial located in New Delhi. With this, his name has also been included among the immortal heroes of the country who sacrificed their lives to protect the motherland. This honor has created an atmosphere of pride for the family and the entire region. The martyr's family said that the financial assistance announced by the Chief Minister has already been received. Meanwhile, the martyr's wife, Seema Sharma, expressed gratitude to the government for getting an appointment as a clerk in the education department. Heading: Operation Sindoor martyr Naik's family should get pension
Summary: The article highlights the plight of martyr Anilveer M. Murali Naik's elderly parents, who are fighting in the Bombay High Court for pension and healthcare benefits, which the government denies based on service rules. The author criticizes this as bureaucratic injustice, arguing that rules should be flexible for soldiers who make the ultimate sacrifice for the nation, and that pension is their right.
Content: The controversy over revealing the names of brave soldiers martyred in Operation Sindoor years later is raging. In this controversy, we need to talk about another shocking fact related to the martyrs, as the Modi government is completely silent on this issue. Among the brave soldiers martyred in Operation Sindoor is Anilveer M. Murali Naik. Anilveer M. Murali Naik was martyred on May 9, 2022, during Operation Sindoor in a firing by Pakistan on the Poonch border. Murali's elderly parents had to apply to the Bombay High Court to receive pension and healthcare benefits. This government is refusing to provide pension, healthcare, and other benefits to Murali's elderly parents because Anilveer's employment rules do not include pension and other benefits. According to current rules, Anilveer or his family do not receive any pension or lifelong family welfare benefits after completing service or in case of death during service. While regular soldiers receive all benefits including pension and gratuity upon joining the army, Anilveers only receive a 'Seva Nidhi' fund once at the end of four years. Even if killed in the line of duty, a limited death compensation package is received, but based on that, the martyr's family can be devastated. It's understandable if Anilveer's fixed-term service doesn't include pension or other benefits, but denying benefits to his family even when he sacrifices his life for the country is sheer ingratitude. Instead of rectifying this injustice, this government is fighting a court case to deny benefits to the family of martyr Anilveer. This country spends crores of rupees and is proud of Operation Sindoor, and has spent crores promoting it. Crores of rupees have been spent on various programs to praise Operation Sindoor, but denying a pension of twenty-five to fifty thousand rupees per month to a martyr's family, what kind of low mentality is that? There is no need to do anything special to provide healthcare and other benefits to martyr Murali Naik's family. There are numerous Army medical hospitals in this country; what difference would it make if two members of martyr Naik's family received treatment there? Citizens of the country already receive free healthcare facilities under the Ayushman Yojana. Martyr Naik's family should receive those benefits. The Modi government's reference to Anilveer's service rules is proof of sheer bureaucracy. There is nothing wrong with adhering to rules in normal circumstances. While running the administration, it's one thing, but sacrificing one's life for the country is not a normal circumstance. Giving one's life for the country's security is the ultimate sacrifice, and there is nothing wrong with changing rules in such extraordinary circumstances. The government argues that providing pension allowance to Murali's family will lead to similar demands in other cases in the future, increasing the burden on the government. This is completely baseless because the incident of an Anilveer being martyred does not happen daily, nor do you have to pay pensions to 355 martyr Anilveer families every year. Such incidents rarely occur and are exceptional. In exceptional cases, rules can be changed, and there should be no objection to that. There should be no objection to providing pension to the families of brave soldiers martyred for this country. Unfortunately, the people of this country are also so weak that they do not honor their martyrs and sit silently with their tails between their legs against injustice to martyrs' families. We pay tribute to martyrs, salute them, praise their bravery, but no one is ready to stand by their families. Murali's mother has been fighting a case in the High Court since May 9, 2022, but no one is ready to help her. It is shameful that one has to extend a hand for the families of soldiers martyred for this country to live the rest of their lives with dignity, but it is even more shameful that they are harassed and have to resort to the High Court. It only happens in this country that the families of martyrs are treated like beggars and humiliated by citing rigid rules. When the Modi government introduced the Anilveer scheme, there was strong opposition to it. Accusations were made that the Modi government was recruiting bureaucrats instead of soldiers who sacrificed their lives for the country's security. The rules denying benefits to the families of brave soldiers who gave their lives for the country were criticized. If the Modi government wants to rectify these criticisms, it should provide pension and other benefits to martyr Naik's family. Even in private-private cases, pensions should be given to the families of soldiers fighting for the country. This pension is their right, not aid or charity.

Content: PTI New Delhi Amid a row surrounding the six martyrs of Operation Sindoor, the defence ministry on Saturday said the nation paid homage to them at the “earliest opportunity”, and their memory shall always be honoured with the dignity and reverence, it deserves. In its statement, the defence ministry said the bravehearts were “conferred with gallantry awards” and that it “constituted a formal and national recognition of their valour and supreme sacrifice”. New Delhi, Agency
The Defense Ministry on Saturday issued a strong clarification regarding the controversy spreading on social media concerning the statement made by Defense Minister Rajnath Singh in Parliament last year about soldiers martyred during Operation Sindoor. The Ministry stated that the claims being spread in this regard are completely misleading and factually incorrect.
Recently, after the names of six soldiers who made the supreme sacrifice during this operation were inscribed on the National War Memorial, questions were being raised on social media by citing an old speech of the Defense Minister, and a misleading narrative was being created that the government had hidden information about the martyrs. The Defense Ministry issued a statement saying that attempts were made to misrepresent the speech given in Parliament on July 28 on social media. These mischievous posts deliberately picked a specific part of the speech and misinterpreted it, as if the Defense Minister had said that no Indian soldier lost their life during 'Operation Sindoor'. The Ministry clarified that those who tried to create controversy over the Defense Minister's parliamentary speech deliberately ignored the broader context of his statement. According to the statement, at the time of the Defense Minister's speech, false rumors were being spread in some sections of the media and on social media in a specific and planned manner, claiming that Indian pilots were killed during 'Operation Sindoor'. This was completely fabricated, yet it was being aggressively spread to demoralize the people of the country. The Defense Minister had given that statement in response to this mischievous narrative, which was an accurate and context-inclusive diplomatic response to a dangerous falsehood spreading at the time. The Ministry stated that the Defense Minister's statement in Parliament was a glorious and accurate description of the splendid success of Operation Sindoor, showcasing the unparalleled precision, resolve, and military professionalism of the Indian defense forces. During this successful military operation, Indian bravehearts eliminated more than 100 terrorists and Pakistani soldiers, and also caused heavy damage to their basic infrastructure deployed along the Line of Control and Pakistani air bases. The Defense Ministry reiterated that the government maintains the highest respect and reverence for every member of the Indian defense forces, especially for those brave sons who sacrificed their lives in defense of the country. Honoring their sacrifice, the government has ensured that their names remain immortal on the National War Memorial. Additionally, all necessary steps have been taken to provide concessions in education, health, and other facilities to the families and dependents of these brave individuals.

This clarification aims to prevent undue distress to the families of the fallen soldiers caused by baseless news.
Content: New Delhi - The Indian Army has issued an official press release clarifying that the news circulated in some media outlets about the names of 6 soldiers martyred in 'Operation Sindoor' being announced for the first time is false. The Army also stated, 'These martyred soldiers were honored at the appropriate time and with utmost respect.' Heading: It is sad that there is a controversy over martyrdom
Summary: The article discusses a controversy surrounding the martyrdom of six soldiers in 'Operation Sindoor' against Pakistan, whose names were revealed a year later. The opposition accuses the Modi government of politicizing the army and misleading Parliament regarding casualties, citing a Defense Minister's statement. The Defense Ministry has issued a clarification, stating that the minister's remarks were taken out of context and aimed at countering false propaganda.
Content: Bhopal, Monday 29 June 2026 Founder-Editor: Late Mayaram Surjan It is sad that there is a controversy over martyrdom In May 2025, six soldiers were martyred in 'Operation Sindoor' launched against Pakistan, whose names the Modi government has now made public a year later. The names of the six martyred soldiers have been engraved in the National War Memorial. The spirit of sacrificing one's life and making the supreme sacrifice for the defense and self-respect of the country cannot be praised enough, nor can sufficient gratitude be expressed. By rights, there should be no political debate or controversy on subjects like martyrdom. But the Modi government has now started using the army for political gain. That is why controversial statements are also being made on martyrdom. Actually, on July 28, 2025, during the Parliament session, during a debate on Operation Sindoor in the Lok Sabha, Defense Minister Rajnath Singh had told the opposition, 'If you want to ask a question, then ask if our brave soldiers suffered any damage in this operation, and the answer to that is no.' A video of the Defense Minister's statement is circulating on social media, in which it is heard that he emphasized the pronunciation of 'no', and then the then Home Minister Amit Shah and all BJP MPs thumped their desks and smiled, welcoming this statement. Hearing this statement, it is clearly understood that Rajnath Singh was saying that our soldiers suffered no harm. Rajnath Singh further said in the same statement, 'People of the opposition keep asking how many of our planes crashed, I think their question does not correctly represent national sentiment. They did not ask even once how many enemy planes our forces shot down. If they have to ask a question, then their question should be whether India destroyed terrorist hideouts, and the answer to that is yes. If you want to ask a question, then ask if Operation Sindoor was successful, and the answer is yes.' The way the Defense Minister answered by naming the opposition and questioning their intentions, it was clear that the Modi government was politicizing in the name of the army. The Modi government wants to take sole credit for the army's actions by portraying it as the Modi government's army. Whereas, by rights, whatever the army does, only it deserves praise, not any political party. However, when the Defense Minister said that no soldier was harmed, it was believed that India caused a lot of damage to Pakistan in Operation Sindoor, but the country suffered no harm. Although claims were made by Pakistan of shooting down fighter jets, sometimes killing more than 10 soldiers, these were not taken seriously. Now that the names of six soldiers have come out, the opposition has raised questions. Congress leader Pawan Khera said that after the Pulwama attack, India's retaliatory action against Pakistan led to 'misleading Parliament'. On X, Mr. Khera wrote that 'there are only two possibilities: either the Defense Minister was unaware of the facts related to his own ministry, which raises a 'serious question' about his competence, or he knew the truth and still decided to 'mislead Parliament'.' He wrote, 'The government that wraps itself in the tricolor and never tires of talking about nationalism, that very government did not give these brave men the respect and remembrance they deserved.' Pawan Khera said, 'The names of these brave men should have been permanently recorded in the collective memory of the country. Their families should have felt that the entire country remembers their sacrifice with respect. But contrary to this, for a whole year, the BJP government decided to hide their martyrdom from the country.' Similarly, statements were also given by other parties, so now the Defense Ministry has clarified that 'some social media posts are trying to misrepresent the speech given by the Defense Minister in Parliament on July 28, 2025. In these posts, a small part of the speech has been selected to make a false claim that no Indian soldier died during Operation Sindoor. This claim has been deliberately presented in a misleading manner and is completely factually incorrect.' 'It should be remembered that when the Defense Minister was giving his speech in Parliament, at that time, some sections of the media and social media were continuously spreading false propaganda that Indian Air Force pilots were killed during Operation Sindoor. This claim was completely false, but it was being continuously spread with the aim of downplaying the success of the operation and lowering the morale of the public. The Defense Minister's related statement was given in response to this specific and misleading propaganda. Therefore, his statement should be understood in that context.' The Defense Ministry's statement further said that 'this speech was meant to honor the courage and capability of the Indian Armed Forces and was also a clear message to those trying to harm India.' 'The Defense Minister and the Government of India are fully committed to expressing respect, gratitude, and reverence for every member of the Indian Armed Forces. Especially for those brave soldiers who made the supreme sacrifice while defending the nation.' 'In honor of this supreme sacrifice, the government has ensured that the names of these brave soldiers are inscribed on the walls of the National War Memorial.' The kind of clarification the Defense Ministry has presented, has never happened in the past. India has been involved in wars before, in which a large number of soldiers have been martyred. These wars happened during both Congress and BJP governments, but never before was there a need to give such a clarification. The Modi government should consider why its decisions get entangled in such controversies. When the Pulwama attack happened, even then terrorists did not ask about religion or caste, but the BJP made a horrific act of terror a part of cheap politics by making posters, and now a new controversy has arisen regarding Operation Sindoor, which is not appropriate in any way.

Sharmistha criticized that after Rahul Gandhi emerged as a prominent leader in 2014, the Congress party has been continuously losing in several elections. Calling the allegations baseless, India urged Pakistan to first take action against the terrorist infrastructure operating on its own soil. Responding to media questions on this matter, Ministry of External Affairs spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said, "We are seeing Pakistan making allegations against India regarding the terrorist attack in Karachi. Jaiswal reiterated that Pakistan should pay attention to abandoning the tendency of using terrorism as an instrument of state policy." The prices of some high-end models have increased by as much as Rs 70,000 to Rs 1 lakh. Apple is introducing AI-powered features like Apple Intelligence in its devices. For these devices to work directly with AI models, powerful processors are required. Market reports indicate that not only smartphone companies but also giant AI data centers are rolling out these features, leading to a shortage of chips in the market, which has significantly increased prices. Apple is investing billions of dollars in the design of its custom silicon chips and AI technology research. Market reports suggest that this premium price is being charged because customers are being provided with technology that can handle future software updates.

Heading: Nation honoured Sindoor Martyrs at earliest opportunity: MoD
Summary: The Defence Ministry clarified that the nation honored the six martyrs of Operation Sindoor at the earliest opportunity, refuting Congress's allegations of delayed recognition. The ministry stated that the bravehearts were conferred with gallantry awards and received formal national recognition for their sacrifice, well before recent media reports suggested otherwise. This clarification was issued following accusations by Congress leader Pawan Khera regarding the government's alleged concealment of their martyrdom.
Content: PTI New Delhi Amid a row surrounding the six martyrs of Operation Sindoor, the defence ministry on Saturday said the nation paid homage to them at the “earliest opportunity”, and their memory shall always be honoured with the dignity and reverence, it deserves. In its statement, the defence ministry said the bravehearts were “conferred with gallantry awards” and that it “constituted a formal and national recognition of their valour and supreme sacrifice”. The statement comes in the backdrop of the Congress’s accusation that the government “concealed” the supreme sacrifice made by the six bravehearts during the military operation in 2025 by “not recognising” their martyrdom for a year. Congress leader Pawan Khera levelled the allegations through social media posts on Friday and Saturday. On Friday, he also shared a link to a report in his post. The defence ministry, without naming anyone, said, “Certain reports circulating in sections of the media and on social media platforms have incorrectly suggested that the supreme sacrifice of six bravehearts during Operation Sindoor have been acknowledged or brought to public notice for the first time only recently”. “It is clarified that the nation paid homage to these fallen heroes at the earliest opportunity, well before the reports in question. During the official press conference held on May 11, 2025, then director general of military operations paid solemn tribute to these brave soldiers and specifically acknowledged their sacrifice in the line of duty during Operation Sindoor,” the statement said. Names of six Operation Sindoor martyrs inscribed at National War Memorial in New Delhi.

Heading: The Unspoken 'Mann Ki Baat' Behind the Reshuffle
Summary: The article critically examines the challenges faced by Prime Minister Modi and the BJP government after 12 years, citing a decline in public image due to ministerial inefficiency and various corruption allegations. It highlights issues like economic mismanagement, foreign policy setbacks, examination paper leaks, and charges against state chief ministers and the Ayodhya Ram Mandir Trust. The author suggests that significant changes and a cabinet reshuffle are essential to restore public trust and the party's influence.
Content: Despite being in a strong position, Prime Minister Modi and the BJP are finding it difficult to maintain their public image after twelve years. The inefficiency of the ministers chosen and fully trusted by the Prime Minister is hitting the BJP's image. Prime Minister Narendra Modi has been telling the countrymen his 'Mann Ki Baat' for 135 consecutive weeks. But most of the time, the real, heartfelt message is not revealed. They avoid commenting on burning issues in the country. Even after coming to power for the third consecutive time, the Prime Minister, despite wishing to speak about the performance of his cabinet colleagues, may not have been able to elaborate on it in 'Mann Ki Baat'. In such a situation, a family member or a person related to the family has rarely dared to advise the Prime Minister on what direction the Modi government should take in the last year. But such an initiative has been taken by journalist-writer Dr. A. Suryaprakash through an article. Dr. A. Suryaprakash, who was the chairman of 'Prasar Bharati' from 2014 to 2020, was honored with 'Padma Bhushan' last year, is an advisor to 'Vivekananda International Foundation' and currently a member of the Prime Minister's Museum and Library institution. He is a senior journalist with a respected position in Delhi's political and Sangh-BJP circles. Therefore, could it be that the Prime Minister tried to subtly admonish his cabinet colleagues through Suryaprakash, without directly revealing his thoughts? "Although Modi's performance as Prime Minister over twelve years has been extraordinary, most central ministers have failed. Arrogance is evident in the performance of many central ministers as well as chief ministers of BJP-ruled states. The BJP, the world's largest political party with fourteen crore members, has not been able to generate enthusiasm among its lesser-known national general secretaries or office-bearers," Suryaprakash has stated. He has presented Modi's inner thoughts in suggestive words, saying that the central government and the BJP attribute all the success of the last twelve years to Prime Minister Modi. The Prime Minister is facing issues with the quality of his central cabinet colleagues, increasing fatigue within the party, and Marathi-speaking problems. The central government and the BJP, whose influence on the countrymen is waning, have realized the need for political surgery by giving opportunities to new blood to maintain the BJP's influence. The discussion about a cabinet reshuffle, which began even before the central government completed twelve years on June 10, has taken a new turn due to this article. It is also being said that apart from Union Home and Cooperation Minister Amit Shah, no one in Modi's 71-member central cabinet is truly effective. Heading: Congress's Misleading Discourse on National Security
Summary: The article criticizes the Congress party for a misleading discourse on national security, specifically regarding 'Operation Sindoor'. It highlights how the opposition distorted the Defence Minister's speech and spread false claims about the government hiding martyrs' names and denying casualties, undermining a successful military operation. The editorial emphasizes the need for political parties to maintain restraint on national security issues, base criticism on facts, and prioritize national security above political gain, especially given external threats.
Content: To be powerful, it is necessary to trust in one's own strength; there is no one weaker than those who do not trust in their own capabilities: Swami Dayanand Saraswati EDITORIAL Healthy political debate and criticism are the hallmarks of a vibrant society in a democracy, but when this criticism centers around the country's sovereignty, military operations, and the brave soldiers who make the ultimate sacrifice, it becomes necessary to reconsider its limits and ethics. The recent sharp debate in political circles regarding 'Operation Sindoor' highlights this very concern. The official clarification issued by the Ministry of Defence has not only exposed the misinformation being spread on this sensitive issue but has also clarified how attempts to distort information for political gain are affecting the country's security discourse. The matter escalated when some leaders of the opposition party Congress shared a selected part of Defence Minister Rajnath Singh's parliamentary speech on social media. Through this post, a misleading claim was made that the government was trying to hide the names of our brave soldiers who made the ultimate sacrifice during this successful military operation and was also making a false claim that no Indian soldier was martyred in the operation. The swift and strong statement from the Ministry of Defence debunked this claim, making it clear that the Defence Minister's speech in Parliament was presented completely out of context, which was not only factually incorrect but also a deliberate attempt to spread discontent in society. 'Operation Sindoor' was not an ordinary event; rather, it was a glorious chapter of the Indian defense forces' unparalleled precision, unwavering resolve, and excellent military professionalism. In this strategic operation, our brave soldiers crossed the Line of Control and not only eliminated more than 100 terrorists and Pakistani soldiers but also caused extensive damage to the enemy's basic infrastructure deployed there. When the details of such a large and sensitive operation are viewed through a political lens and only a selected part is made a subject of controversy, ignoring its entire context, it is like undermining the importance of the entire operation. Any speech or official statement has a specific context. When the Defence Minister mentioned the unprecedented success of the operation, his intention was to refer to the achievement of strategic objectives set by the Indian Army. To portray this as the government denying the sacrifices of martyrs is the height of petty politics. The truth is that the Government of India and every citizen of the country hold the utmost respect and gratitude for their soldiers, and their sacrifices can never be forgotten. It is well-known that the current government has ensured that the names of every brave warrior who sacrificed their lives for the country are inscribed in golden letters on the walls of the 'National War Memorial' forever. Furthermore, concrete policies are being implemented on the ground to provide all possible assistance and concessions in education, health, and other basic facilities to martyr families and their dependents. In such a situation, accusing that the names of the country's brave martyrs are being hidden is not only ridiculous but also hurts the feelings of those families who have sacrificed everything for the country. The most important lesson from this entire episode is that political parties should observe a 'Lakshman Rekha' (a line of restraint) on sensitive issues related to national security. In this era of social media, where misleading news and selected video clips can contaminate any discourse in minutes, the responsibility of the opposition increases even more. Constructive criticism is welcome, but it should be based on facts, not fabricated lies. We must not forget that the enemy sitting across the border is always looking for cracks in our internal strife and discourse. In such a situation, instead of dragging glorious operations like 'Operation Sindoor' into controversies, we should, with one voice, salute the courage of our soldiers and allow the country's security to rise above the level of politics.

Heading: Op Sindoor: BJP accuses Congress of trying to undermine faith in forces

Content: PIONEER NEWS SERVICE New Delhi The BJP on Sunday accused the Congress of "stooping low" by spreading "lies" and undermining public faith in the Indian armed forces, after the Opposition party claimed that the Government concealed and did not acknowledge the martyrdom of military personnel during Operation Sindoor. "How low can the Congress party go? The Congress party hates the BJP and hates Prime Minister Modi. That is well known. "But in its hatred for the BJP, will it start hating our armed forces as well? Will it raise doubts in the minds of people about our armed forces? Does it want our armed forces to have internal problems and revolt so that enemies of the nation like Pakistan and other hostile countries can benefit?" he said in a video statement. Describing Khera as a "serial liar", Poonawalla alleged that the Congress leader has repeatedly made false claims, citing his remarks on Assam Chief Minister Himanta Biswa Sarma and his wife, as well as his claims regarding the India-bound LPG tankers Shivalik and Nanda Devi. He alleged that Khera was now spreading another "sinister lie" about the armed forces.

Heading: The claim of hiding the names of martyrs of Operation Sindoor is completely false
Summary: The article refutes Congress's allegations that the Indian government hid the names of martyrs from "Operation Sindoor" and failed to honor them. It clarifies that the names of six martyrs were announced, their families were honored, and one received the Shaurya Chakra. The Ministry of Defense asserts that there is a fixed process for registering names in the National War Memorial and that all necessary facilities have been provided to the martyrs' families.
Content: Last year, the names of 5 brave martyrs of Operation Sindoor, which took place with Pakistan, were announced by the Central Government within 1 to 3 months. Congress is making false allegations against the government that it is hiding the details of the damage caused to India by Operation Sindoor. This is an act of treason. In response to a question raised by Defense Minister Rajnath Singh in Parliament, Congress had claimed that Operation Sindoor had caused no damage to India. The Central Government has not honored the martyrs of Operation Sindoor for a year, thus depriving them of their honor. This is an insult to the Indian Army. Under Operation Sindoor, the Indian Army had killed 9 terrorists associated with Jaish-e-Mohammed and Lashkar-e-Taiba in Pakistan-occupied Kashmir (PoK) on May 5. On May 10, the Director General of Military Operations (DGMO) of India and Pakistan had a ceasefire. The Ministry of Defense has always maintained that the names of the martyrs of Operation Sindoor, Lance Naik Dinesh Kumar (Fifth Gorkha Regiment), Agniveer Murli Narayan (25th Rajput Regiment), Sergeant Surendra Kumar (Ordnance, 36 Field), Subedar Major Pawan Kumar (Headquarters, 90 Field Brigade), Havaldar Sunil Kumar (8th Madras Regiment) and Havaldar Sunil Kumar Singh (239 Workshop Company) were announced. These 6 martyrs were honored, while Sergeant Surendra Kumar received the Shaurya Chakra for his bravery. Allegations are being made that the details were hidden by announcing them late in May 2023 for Operation Sindoor 2022. The Ministry of Defense has dismissed the Congress's allegations and said that the names of the martyrs were not hidden. The Ministry of Defense has stated that some media reports and social media posts are claiming that the government is hiding the names of the martyrs of Operation Sindoor and their families have not been honored. The Ministry of Defense has clarified that the names of the martyrs were never hidden and their details were provided. According to the Ministry of Defense, on May 11, 2022, a press conference was held by the Director General of Military Operations (DGMO) to pay tribute to the martyrs. After that, on August 15, 2022, the names of the awardees were also announced. The Indian Army also paid tribute on social media platforms. On October 2, 2022, the families of Sergeant Surendra Kumar, who was awarded the Shaurya Chakra, were honored on June 15, 2023, on Army Day. Regarding the delay in registering names in the National War Memorial, the Ministry of Defense has clarified that there is a fixed process for registering names in the National War Memorial. There was a delay in registering the names of the martyrs of Operation Sindoor, and it is believed that their families were not honored. The Ministry of Defense claims that the Central Government has provided education, health, and other facilities to the families of all the martyrs. Regarding Rajnath Singh's statement, the Ministry of Defense has clarified that Rajnath Singh had given a speech in Parliament and presented a photo message, stating that Operation Sindoor had not caused any damage to the Indian Army. In fact, Rajnath Singh had not mentioned any casualties of the Indian Army during Operation Sindoor. The claim that the Indian soldiers were martyred was not hidden by the government, and Rajnath Singh had said that India had not suffered any damage. On May 10, the names of 5 martyrs were announced. The claim of hiding the names of martyrs is actually false. Congress is making false allegations on this issue, but Congress President Pawan Kumar, MP, Murli Narayan, Lance Naik Dinesh Kumar, Subedar Major Om Prakash, Sub-Inspector Mohammed Dimtiyaj, Sergeant Surendra Kumar Mohra, Havaldar Sunil Kumar and officer Raj Kumar paid tribute. Although the terrorists did not mention Operation Sindoor, our soldiers were martyred during the war between the Indian Army and Pakistan. So the government's claim of hiding the names of the martyrs is completely false. And Gandhi did not mention any casualties, so the government's criticism is justified. If Rajnath Singh says in Parliament that the number of Indian soldiers is zero, then it is a lie. Rajnath Singh said in Parliament on October 28, 2022, that the opposition asks how many casualties we suffered, and the Indian Army did not suffer any casualties. So what is 'zero'? Rajnath Singh says that the number of pilots and aircraft lost in his country is not zero. So why are the opposition and Rajnath Singh defending the government? This issue is very important, and the government should accept that Indian soldiers were martyred within two months. Rajnath Singh, while talking about the casualties, says that the opposition should ask in a different way. Now, after 12 months, what is the meaning of asking about the casualties?

Heading: Lashkar-e-Taiba terrorists seen at Shoaib Akhtar's brother's funeral, pictures again expose Pakistan
Summary: A controversy has emerged after viral videos and pictures allegedly showed individuals linked to the banned Lashkar-e-Taiba, including its deputy chief Saifullah Kasuri, at the funeral of Shoaib Akhtar's brother in Islamabad. Kasuri is considered by Indian security agencies as a key conspirator in the 2025 Pahalgam terrorist attack, which prompted India to take strong retaliatory measures like suspending the Indus Waters Treaty. The incident has reignited questions about Pakistan's alleged protection of terrorists, with claims that the Pakistan Markazi Muslim League acts as a political front for Lashkar-e-Taiba.
Content:
Islamabad, Agency.
A new controversy has erupted regarding the funeral of Shahid Akhtar, elder brother of former Pakistan fast bowler Shoaib Akhtar. Videos and pictures going viral on social media claim the presence of some individuals said to be associated with the banned terrorist organization Lashkar-e-Taiba. After these pictures surfaced, questions have once again arisen in Pakistan regarding the public presence of terrorists and the alleged protection they receive. Shahid Akhtar passed away on June 24. He was later laid to rest in Islamabad's H-8 graveyard. Many people from sports, politics, and social sectors attended the funeral. During this, the viral videos claim the presence of Lashkar-e-Taiba's deputy chief Saifullah Kasuri and some leaders associated with Pakistan Markazi Muslim League (PMML). However, these videos and pictures could not be independently verified.

Who is Saifullah Kasuri and why is he in discussion:
India's security agencies consider Saifullah Kasuri to be among the main conspirators of the Pahalgam terrorist attack that occurred on April 22, 2025. 25 tourists died in this attack. India had taken several strong steps after the attack. These included suspending the Indus Waters Treaty and taking action against terrorist hideouts under Operation Sindoor. India has long accused Pakistan of sheltering terrorists.

Who else is claimed to be seen at the funeral:
Viral videos and pictures claim the appearance of several other leaders, including Inam-ur-Rehman Kamboh, Islamabad President of Pakistan Markazi Muslim League (PMML). PMML has long been accused of being a political platform for individuals associated with Lashkar-e-Taiba. It is noteworthy that several organizations associated with Hafiz Saeed, a terrorist designated by the United Nations, are under international sanctions.

Heading: 'Misleading and factually incorrect': Centre hits back as Oppn questions Rajnath Singh's Op Sindoor remarks

Content:
NEW DELHI, June 27 (IANS): The Centre has summarily rejected the Opposition's 'narrative building exercise' over Defence Minister Rajnath Singh's old statement on Operation Sindoor in the Parliament, related to loss of lives in the military exercise, and termed its assertions as "deliberately misleading and factually incorrect."
The Defence Ministry, taking note of certain social media posts, said that this is a deliberate attempt to "misrepresent" Raksha Mantri's address delivered on the floor of Parliament on July 28, 2025, by selectively quoting isolated portions of his speech.
The controversy over Rajnath Singh's statement over 'no soldiers' death in the Parliament, days after Operation Sindoor, started after six fallen jawans were immortalised by inscribing their names on the National War Memorial in the capital yesterday. This marked the first public revelation of the names of the armed forces jawans who laid their lives in Operation Sindoor.
This gave the Congress an opportunity to train guns at the Centre and the Defence Minister, as it claimed that the latter tried to gloss over the sacrifice of soldiers during Operation Sindoor, thus not giving them the respect and honour that they deserved.
Congress leader Pawan Khera dug out the old parliamentary address of Rajnath Singh and said that there could be only two possibilities – either the Defence Minister was unaware of the martyrdom of six soldiers while addressing the House, or the other could be that he knew the truth and yet chose to mislead.
He said that both situations raise questions about his competence and added, "This is an insult to our soldiers, and no true patriot can remain silent or complacent about it."
Another Congress leader, Manish Tewari, targeted the Defence Minister, asking, "Was he oblivious of the facts when he addressed Parliament?"
He said that the Defence Minister, during a debate on Operation Sindoor, said that no harm was caused to any Indian soldier during Operation Sindoor, but then, after 13 months, released the names of six soldiers martyred in the operation. The Centre, replying to these charges, said that these posts selectively quote a truncated portion of the Defence Minister's speech to falsely imply that he claimed that no Indian soldier lost his life during Operation Sindoor.
Dismissing the narrative as 'mischievous', it said that when the Raksha Mantri made the statement in Parliament, there were multiple claims of India losing its pilots in the operation, and therefore, his remarks should be seen in that context and not otherwise.
"The Union Minister's remarks were a targeted and contextually specific response to a falsehood that was gaining dangerous traction at that moment," the Defence Ministry said in a statement.
It also said the narrative was entirely false, yet it was aggressively amplified with the intent to diminish the operation's success and demoralise public sentiment.
It further said that Rajnath Singh's statement in the Parliament was, in its entirety, a proud and accurate account of the remarkable success of Operation Sindoor, an operation that saw Defence Forces demonstrating unmatched precision, resolve, and military professionalism by hitting multiple targets deep inside Pakistan.

Heading: 6 Immortal Martyrs of Operation Sindoor, Misrepresentation in Parliament?

Content:
Operation Sindoor took place approximately 13 months ago. In this operation, 6 Indian soldiers were martyred. Among the martyred soldiers are Subedar Major Pawan Kumar, Rifleman Sunil Kumar, Lance Naik Dinesh Kumar, Agniveer M Murali Naik, Havildar Sunil Kumar, and Sergeant Surendra, who were from the Air Force and were martyred in the clash of Operation Sindoor. He had also warned the opposition, saying that if MPs have questions, they should ask what our success was in Sindoor? Why were our soldiers safe in Operation Sindoor? Now, 13 months later, when the names of these soldiers have been inscribed on the War Memorial's Chakra of Sacrifice, it is openly coming to light that 6 soldiers of the Indian Army were also martyred in Operation Sindoor. Rifleman Sunil Kumar was posthumously awarded the Vir Chakra and Sergeant Surendra Kumar was posthumously awarded the Vayu Seva Medal. It is noteworthy that Operation Sindoor started on May 7, 2025. The Indian armed forces had attacked terrorist hideouts in Pakistan and PoK. More than 100 terrorists were killed. This claim was made by the government. The government had also said that no harm was caused to any of our soldiers. The ceasefire for Operation Sindoor took place on May 10.
Regarding the ceasefire, US President Donald Trump had claimed that he had brokered a ceasefire between India and Pakistan. On the other hand, the Indian government had said that the Pakistani government was begging before us. Seeing this situation, the Indian government accepted the ceasefire. However, 13 months later, as news is emerging, the opposition is raising the biggest objection. The opposition says that the Defense Minister lied in Parliament. The opposition has started creating a ruckus over this. Its effect can be seen in the upcoming monsoon session. The opposition is also alleging that the way the Bharatiya Janata Party and Prime Minister Narendra Modi celebrated Operation Sindoor was an insult to the martyred soldiers. The government hid the real situation. Along with this, it has insulted the soldiers of the army. Along with this, misrepresentation in Parliament has deceived Parliament. The secret of Operation Sindoor has been revealed, and after this, the opposition is talking about adopting a tough stance in the monsoon session. The opposition says that when there was a border dispute with China, China had occupied a large part of the Indian border. Even then, the government had misrepresented in Parliament. Even then, Prime Minister Narendra Modi had said that no one had entered, nor had any Indian land been occupied. Later, these things came out openly when discussions started about the border dispute between China and India. The opposition has many issues this time, but the opposition is unable to raise these issues inside the house. It is said about the BJP that if anyone wants to learn how to make a snake out of a piece of cloth, they can learn it from the BJP.

Heading: Martyrs of Operation Sindoor Immortalized in National War Memorial

These 6 soldiers' names have been added: Subedar Major Pawan Kumar, Rifleman Sunil Kumar, Lance Naik Dinesh Kumar, Agniveer M Murali Naik, Havildar Sunil Kumar, Sergeant Surendra Kumar. On Saturday, Lance Naik DSM Raja was paid tribute at the National War Memorial. Most people who arrived here came to be part of the program. People were reading the names of brave soldiers on the memorials, but many were unaware that the names of soldiers who recently sacrificed their lives in Operation Sindoor had also been included here. Two youths, after reading the news, had arrived here. They also took photos, but the security personnel deleted their pictures. Shivam Dubey, a youth from Bengal, was one of them. He said, "I learned from the news and came to find and see these names. I was familiar with one of the soldiers, Surendra Kumar, and specifically came to see his name." He added, "It felt very good that the martyrs finally received the honor they deserved. No one knows yet how many soldiers were martyred. This is not just a political allegation, but a mockery of the country's self-respect and the valor of the army, which no true patriot can remain silent about.

Every step is taken with full caution, respect, and dignity. Subsequently, in a statement issued on August 14, 2025, information about the gallantry awards given to these six brave jawans was also made public. This was in recognition of their courage and supreme sacrifice on behalf of the nation. It was a formal honor. Content: New Delhi, (Punjab Kesari): A controversy has erupted over the funeral of former Pakistan fast bowler Shoaib Akhtar's elder brother Shahid Akhtar in Islamabad.
