The presence of senior Lashkar officials during Shahid Akhtar's last rites has once again drawn attention to the presence of members of banned terrorist organizations in Pakistan. Analysts say that this incident highlights concerns about the operational space available to banned terrorist groups and their influence in the country's political and social environment. After the attack, India canceled the Indus Water Treaty and launched 'Operation Sindoor' targeting terrorist hideouts in Pakistan and PoK. It is reported that in this operation, several terrorist hideouts, including Lashkar-e-Taiba's headquarters in Muridke, were destroyed. Additionally, military targets from Rawalpindi to Sukkur were also attacked. This operation significantly impacted the activities of Lashkar-e-Taiba and other terrorist groups in Pakistan, although since then Qasuri has continued to issue threats against India, including warnings of other terrorist attacks like Mumbai via sea route. Content: The Union government on Saturday rejected the "misleading social media claims" that Defence Minister Rajnath Singh had stated that no Indian soldier was killed during Operation Sindoor, asserting that his remarks in Parliament had been selectively quoted and stripped of their context. On July 28, 2025, while speaking before the Lok Sabha, Rajnath Singh stated that no Indian soldiers were harmed during Operation Sindoor. While speaking for 55 minutes during the 16-hour-long discussion, he said, "If you want to raise a question, then ask whether any of our brave soldiers were harmed in this operation. The answer is, no, none of our soldiers were harmed." "When the objectives are high then our attention should not be on irrelevant issues. Because by focusing on irrelevant issues at times, our attention gets diverted from important issues related to national security and morale of soldiers," he had said. 'Misrepresented words' The Ministry of Defence (MoD) clarified in a statement that certain social media posts had misrepresented the Defence Minister's address in Parliament, by isolating a portion of his speech to falsely suggest he denied any Indian military casualties during the cross-border operation. According to Saturday's clarification, Mr. Singh's remarks were specifically intended to counter a widely circulated false narrative at the time claiming that Indian Air Force pilots had been killed during the operation. "It was in direct reference to this specific and mischievous narrative that the Defence Minister made the statement in question," the MoD said, adding that his remarks were a targeted response to false claims and not a denial of casualties suffered by the armed forces. The statement emphasised that the Defence Minister's address in Parliament highlighted the success of Operation Sindoor, during which Indian forces carried out precision strikes against terror infrastructure and military targets across the border. It said the operation resulted in the elimination of more than 100 terrorists and Pakistani soldiers, while inflicting significant damage on Pakistani air bases and military infrastructure along the Line of Control.

Content: The Hindu Bureau NEW DELHI A day after the government officially released the names of the soldiers who died during Operation Sindoor, the Congress on Saturday accused Union Defence Minister Rajnath Singh of misleading Parliament by stating that no Indian soldier had died during the military operation. The government’s disclosure had exposed a contradiction between the Defence Minister’s statement in Parliament and the official record, the party said, demanding the Centre place the complete facts relating to the operation before the House during the forthcoming monsoon session. The Congress’s deputy leader in the Lok Sabha Gaurav Gogoi said that during the parliamentary debate on Operation Sindoor, he had urged the Defence Minister to present “the complete truth” before the Parliament and the nation. “Instead, the House was unequivocally told that our soldiers had suffered no loss,” he said in a post on X. A year later, the government itself had officially released the names of six personnel who had made “the supreme sacrifice” during the operation, Mr. Gogoi added. ‘Stark contradiction’ “The government’s own admission exposes a stark contradiction. Heading: Assault after minor dispute in wedding procession, one dead
Summary: A minor dispute during a wedding procession in Jaunpur escalated into a violent clash, resulting in the death of a 24-year-old man named Saurabh Rajbhar. He was hit by a brick and later succumbed to his injuries while being transferred to Varanasi. The incident led to the cancellation of the remaining wedding rituals as the groom's side refused to proceed.
Content: Jaunpur. A minor dispute between the bride's and groom's sides during a wedding procession last night in Rajpat Nagar, Ara, under Gaurabadshahpur police station area, turned into a bloody conflict. In this violent clash, a young man died, turning the joy of the wedding into mourning. According to information received, the wedding procession had come to the house of Jamuna Rajbhar, a resident of Bhadethi village, Saraykhwaja police station. After the Jaimala ceremony, an argument broke out between the bride's and groom's sides over some issue. The dispute escalated to such an extent that bricks and stones started being thrown from both sides. During this, Saurabh Rajbhar (24), son of Rajesh Rajbhar, a resident of Bhadethi, was hit on the head with a brick, causing him to fall seriously injured and become unconscious. Relatives immediately took him to the district hospital, from where he was referred to Varanasi due to his critical condition. Unfortunately, the young man succumbed to his injuries on the way. As soon as the news of the young man's death was received, the wedding atmosphere completely changed. At that time, the 'Sindoor Daan' ritual, part of the wedding ceremony, was about to take place, which the groom's side explicitly refused to proceed with.

Summary: The article refutes social media misrepresentations of the Raksha Mantri's parliamentary address from July 28, 2025, which falsely claimed no Indian soldiers died during Operation Sindoor. It clarifies that the Raksha Mantri's statement was a contextual response to a false narrative, highlighting the successful neutralization of over 100 terrorists and Pakistani soldiers, and significant damage to Pakistani infrastructure during Operation Sindoor. The government reaffirms its commitment to honoring the sacrifices of Indian Defence Forces and supporting their families.
Content: REFUGEE MESSAGE BUREAU DELHI (PIB), JUNE 27 Certain posts circulating on social media platforms have sought to misrepresent the Raksha Mantri's address delivered on the floor of Parliament on July 28, 2025. These posts have selectively quoted an isolated portion of the speech to falsely imply that the Raksha Mantri claimed that no Indian soldier lost his life during Operation Sindoor. These are deliberately misleading and factually incorrect. Those who have sought to construct a controversy out of Raksha Mantri's Parliamentary address have done so by deliberately ignoring the full context of his remarks. It must be recalled that at the time of the Raksha Mantri's address, a particularly persistent and dominant narrative had taken hold, both in certain sections of the media and on social media, which claimed that Indian pilots had been lost during Operation Sindoor. This narrative was entirely false, yet it was being amplified aggressively with the clear intent of diminishing the success of the operation and demoralising public sentiment. It was in direct reference to this specific and mischievous narrative that the Raksha Mantri made the statement in question. His remarks were, therefore, a targeted and contextually specific response to a falsehood that was gaining dangerous traction at that moment. It is also important to place the Raksha Mantri's address in its full and proper context. His statement in Parliament was, in its entirety, a proud and accurate account of the remarkable success of Operation Sindoor, an operation in which the Indian Defence Forces demonstrated unmatched precision, resolve, and military professionalism. During the operation, more than 100 terrorists and Pakistani soldiers were neutralised, as also Pakistani Air Bases and deployment along Line of Control suffered extensive and significant infrastructure damage. The address was a fitting tribute to the courage and capability of the Indian Defence Forces, and a clear message to those who wish India harm. The Raksha Mantri and the Government of India remain steadfast in their respect, gratitude, and reverence for every member of the Indian Defence Forces, and above all, for those who have laid down their lives in the defence of the nation. Their sacrifice is the highest form of service to the Motherland, and it will always be honoured with the dignity, pride, and solemnity it deserves. It is in recognition of their supreme sacrifice that the Government has ensured that their names are inscribed on the walls of the National War Memorial. The Government has taken all necessary steps to provide concessions in education, health and other facilities to the family/ dependents of the bravehearts.

Government called recent claims false

According to the government, in an official press conference held on May 11, 2025, the then Director General of Military Operations (DGMO) paid tribute to these six soldiers who were martyred while performing their duty during Operation Sindoor. Heading: Govt says posts questioning def min’s speech on Op Sindoor ‘deliberately misleading’, ‘incorrect’
Summary: The Indian government's Defence Ministry has refuted social media posts that allegedly misrepresented Defence Minister Rajnath Singh's speech on Operation Sindoor, clarifying that his remarks addressed a false narrative about Indian pilot casualties. The ministry highlighted the operation's success in avenging the Pahalgam terror attack and decimating terror infrastructure in Pakistan and PoK, while also affirming the government's commitment to honoring the sacrifices of bravehearts and supporting their families. The article emphasizes the Indian defence forces' precision and professionalism during the operation.
Content: NEW DELHI, Jun 27: The government on Saturday said some social media posts sought to “misrepresent” Defence Minister Rajnath Singh’s address in Parliament in July 2025 and “selectively” quoted an isolated portion of it to “falsely imply” that he had claimed that “no Indian soldier lost his life during Operation Sindoor”. “These are deliberately misleading and factually incorrect,” the defence ministry said, adding that the minister’s remarks were in reference to the “specific and mischievous narrative” that India had lost its pilots during Operation Sindoor. The statement from the ministry comes after Congress leader PawanKhera accused the government of “concealing” the supreme sacrifice made by six bravehearts during Operation Sindoor. In a post on X, he also shared a video of the defence minister making a statement in Parliament on Operation Sindoor, and claimed that either the minister was “unaware of the martyrdom” of the six soldiers at that time or he “chose to mislead Parliament”. Without naming anyone, the defence ministry in its statement said that “certain posts circulating on social media platforms” have sought to “misrepresent” the defence minister’s address delivered on the floor of Parliament on July 28 last year. These have “selectively quoted an isolated portion of the speech to falsely imply that the rakshamantri claimed that no Indian soldier lost his life during Operation Sindoor”, it added. Those who have sought to “construct a controversy” out of the defence minister’s Parliamentary address have done so by “deliberately ignoring the full context of his remarks,” the statement claimed. It must be recalled that at the time of the defence minister’s address, a “particularly persistent ent and dominant narrative had taken hold, both in certain sections of the media and on social media, which claimed that Indian pilots had been lost during Operation Sindoor, according to the ministry. “This narrative was entirely false, yet it was being amplified aggressively with the clear intent of diminishing the success of the operation and demoralising public sentiment,” it said. It was in direct reference to this “specific and mischievous narrative” that the defence minister had made the statement, the ministry further said. “His remarks were, therefore, a targeted and contextually specific response to a falsehood that was gaining dangerous traction at that moment,” it added. The names of five six military personnel – five from the Indian Army and one from IAF – who died in the line of duty during Operation Sindoor last year, have been inscribed on a wall at the National War Memorial and also added to the Roll of Honours on the National War Memorial website. The Congress on Friday attacked the Centre and alleged that “for an entire year, the BJP government chose to conceal their martyrdom from the nation”. Operation Sindoor was conducted to avenge the deadly Pahalgam terror attack on April 22 last year. In its statement on Saturday, the defence ministry also said, “The Government of India remain steadfast in their respect, gratitude, and reverence for every member of the Indian defence forces, and above all, for those who have laid down their lives in the defence of the nation.” “Their sacrifice is the highest form of service to the motherland, and it will always be honoured with the dignity, pride, and solemnity it deserves,” it said. It is in recognition of their supreme sacrifice that the government has ensured that their names are inscribed on the walls of the National War Memorial, the ministry said. “The government has taken all necessary steps to provide concessions in education, health and other facilities to the family/dependents of the bravehearts,” it added. India launched Operation Sindoor early on May 7 last year and decimated multiple terror infrastructure sites in Pakistan and Pakistan-Occupied-Kashmir (PoK). Pakistan also launched offensives against India, and all subsequent counter-offensives by India were also carried out under Operation Sindoor. The military conflict between the two nuclear-armed neighbours halted after they reached an understanding on the evening of May 10. The ministry in its statement further said that it is also important to place the defence minister’s address in Parliament in its “full and proper context”. “His statement in Parliament was, in its entirety, a proud and accurate account of the remarkable success of Operation Sindoor, an operation in which the Indian defence forces demonstrated unmatched precision, resolve, and military professionalism,” it asserted. “During the operation, more than 100 terrorists and Pakistani soldiers were neutralised, as also Pakistani Air Bases and deployment along the Line of Control suffered extensive and significant infrastructure damage,” it said. The address was a “fitting tribute” to the courage and capability of the Indian defence forces, and a “clear message to those who wish India harm,” the ministry added.

Content: MORE than a year after Operation Sindoor, the government has officially recorded the names of the six military personnel who made the supreme sacrifice during the four-day war by including them in the roll of honour at the National War Memorial. | OUR VIEW |
Tyag Chakra Inscribes the Bravery of Sindoor
The disclosure of the names of six soldiers who laid down their lives during Operation Sindoor is both solemn and historic. For the first time, the nation has been allowed to know the identities of those who bore the ultimate burden in India's cross border strikes of May 2025. These six men, representing both the Army and the Air Force, became the human cost of defending India's sovereignty. Their sacrifice is not merely military; it is moral, reminding us that freedom and security are never free. The symbolism of “Sindoor”—chosen to signify vengeance for widowed women—underscores the emotional depth of the operation. But beyond symbolism lies the stark reality: families shattered, futures altered, and communities left with empty chairs at their hearths. Rifleman Sunil Kumar's Vir Chakra and Sergeant Surendra Kumar's Vayu Medal are fitting recognitions, yet no medal can equal the void their loved ones endure. In remembering them, we must also reflect on the broader duty of the State. Honouring martyrs requires more than ceremonial inscriptions. It demands sustained support for their families, transparent recognition of their service, and a national commitment to ensure their sacrifice strengthens democratic resilience. The six names now revealed are not just entries in military records. They are reminders of courage, of ordinary men who became extraordinary in the face of danger. Their memory must inspire us to uphold justice, resist terror, and preserve the dignity of those who defend the nation. India salutes them—not in passing, but in permanence. Their sacrifice is our inheritance, their courage our responsibility, and their memory our eternal flame.

Union Defense Minister Rajnath Singh said that there has been a significant increase of 14,802 crore rupees in defense exports. This increase indicates that the world is trusting India's indigenous defense capabilities and advanced manufacturing. He stated that both defense public sector undertakings and private industry have played an important role in this achievement. The contribution of Indian public sector undertakings to total exports was 54.84 percent, while the share of the private sector was 45.16 percent. Defense Minister Singh said that under the inspiring leadership of Prime Minister Narendra Modi, India has written a new success story in the field of defense exports. The Ministry of Defense has achieved another milestone in the financial year 2025-26. In fact, the Ministry has fully utilized its capital budget. This budget amount was 1.86 lakh crore rupees. 100 percent of this large capital expenditure was utilized. This is the second consecutive year that the Ministry of Defense has utilized its entire capital budget. Even before this, in the financial year 2024-25, the capital budget was fully utilized for the first time after many years. According to the Ministry of Defense, initially, a provision of 1.80 lakh crore rupees was made for capital expenditure, but after the expenses of the first two quarters and Operation Sindoor, the increased amount for the armed forces was 1.86 lakh crore rupees.

Heading: Names of 6 Martyrs of Operation Sindoor Revealed for the First Time - Found a Place in National War Memorial
Summary: The Indian government has for the first time publicly released the names of six martyrs from Operation Sindoor against Pakistan, whose details are now on the Army War Memorial website. Two of these brave soldiers, Rifleman Sunil Kumar and Sergeant Surendra Kumar, were posthumously awarded the Vir Chakra and Vayu Padak respectively. Their names, along with the others, will be permanently inscribed on granite plaques at the National War Memorial in New Delhi, which features 16 concentric walls honoring post-independence martyrs.
Content:
New Delhi (A). For the first time, the Government of India has made public the names of those martyrs who lost their lives in Operation Sindoor against Pakistan. Details of the martyrs are now available on the official website of the Army War Memorial. Out of these brave soldiers, 2 have been honored with the Vir Chakra and Vayu Padak. The names of these 6 soldiers will be permanently inscribed on special granite plaques at the National War Memorial located near India Gate in New Delhi.

The martyred soldiers include Subedar Major Pawan Kumar from 10 Infantry Brigade Headquarters, Rifleman Sunil Kumar from the 4th Battalion of Jammu and Kashmir Light Infantry Regiment, Lance Naik Dinesh Kumar from 5th Field Regiment, Agniveer Mood Muralinaik from 851 Light Regiment, Havildar Sunil Kumar Singh from 237 Field Workshop, and Sergeant Surendra Kumar from 39th Wing of the Air Force. Rifleman Sunil Kumar was posthumously awarded the Vir Chakra, the country's third-highest wartime honor, and Sergeant Surendra Kumar received the Vayu Padak. According to reporters, most of the 6 martyrs were martyred in Jammu and Kashmir. Sunil Kumar was deployed on the Line of Control adjacent to Pakistan. It is to be noted that the names of all martyrs will be displayed in the National War Memorial. Here, there are 16 concentric circular walls made of granite bricks. Each brick is inscribed with the name, rank, and regiment of a martyr who made the supreme sacrifice since independence.

Heading: Amit Shah Unveils Vision Document for Drug Control; Decisive Target for Next 3 Years; Amendments to Narcotic Tax Laws Under Consideration, Suggestions Sought from States
Summary: Union Home Minister Amit Shah presided over the 10th NCORD meeting in New Delhi, where he unveiled a Vision Document for Drug Control (2026-2029) and the NCB Annual Report-2025. He also inaugurated new NCB zonal offices and launched an online drug disposal campaign, overseeing the destruction of a massive quantity of drugs worth Rs 6,000 crore in a single day. Shah emphasized a national, collective effort to combat drug trafficking, narco-terrorism, and organized crime, aiming for a drug-free India by 2047, while also stressing the importance of technology and a humane approach for rehabilitation. The government has set decisive targets for the next three years in drug control, with amendments to narcotic tax laws under consideration and suggestions sought from states. Separately, Ashura processions were held peacefully in Jammu and Kashmir, and a yellow alert for thunderstorms and heavy rain was issued for the region from June 26 to June 30.
Content:
Union Home Minister Amit Shah presided over the 10th high-level meeting of the Narco Coordination Centre (NCORD) in New Delhi. The Home Minister released the Vision Document on Drug Control (2026-2029) and the NCB Annual Report-2025. He also e-inaugurated NCB zonal offices in Jammu and Gobai. Mr. Amit Shah further oversaw the destruction of drugs weighing 2,09,500 kg and worth Rs 6,000 crore.

Union Home Minister Amit Shah launched an online drug disposal campaign in his address today, saying that our country is currently fighting a major war against drug trafficking, where a decision will be made in the next three years whether we will be able to defeat this menace or not. He said that in the next 100 years, the future of the country will be determined by these efforts. It is not possible for any government or state alone to win this war; instead, a platform should be formed involving all states and related departments. We should include people who are affected by drugs, our youth, and our women in this war to secure the future of the country. Only then can we achieve complete success in this war. Mr. Shah emphasized that the issue of drugs and narcotics is not just a matter of peace and order. This is deeply related to the internal security, economic, social, and moral interests of the country and the future of our youth. To solve this problem, all states of India need a strong collective effort. Amit Shah said that the nature of drug trafficking, organized crime, cross-border terrorism, and narco-terrorism has changed with the passage of time, and it has become a multi-dimensional crime that affects the internal security and economy of our country. We have made our fight against drug trafficking more difficult by adopting traditional methods like drones, sea routes, container routes, dark net, crypto, and parcels. Today, drug trafficking relies on modern technology and the dark net. Now we are facing multi-dimensional crime in a single form. In this war, our collective and coordinated roadmap should be based on technology and the dark net. Only then can we achieve success against this problem. The Union Minister said that we need to maintain a sympathetic and humane attitude towards individuals involved in drug trafficking. He further said that our sympathetic and humane approach is the life of young children who are on the wrong path. We have to bring them back to the right path. Mr. Amit Shah said that a clear message has been given to the four pillars of our fight against drugs, and a clear message has been given to all four pillars. Targets have been set for every pillar, and they will be achieved within one year. After this, the plan will be reviewed, and then in the next two years of this war, new strength will be added. The Union Minister for Drug Disposal and Cooperation said that drugs worth 6000 crore rupees have been destroyed in one day. This is a major success in destroying drug trafficking. The Narcotics Control Bureau (NCB) has issued its annual report. Along with this, a vision document for a drug-free India has also been released. The NCB's zonal offices and joint offices have been inaugurated today. So far, 15,876 NCORD meetings have been held. 266 state-level meetings and 10 am meetings are being held today. All states' chief secretaries and Directors General of Police should make efforts to make NCORD meetings successful. Shah said that Prime Minister Narendra Modi has given a vision of a drug-free India by 2047, and we will achieve this goal with unity and determination. He said that in the next three years, we will make significant progress towards ending the drug network in India. If we all make collective efforts with determination in these three years, then our goal will be achieved.

Content:
NEW DELHI: More than a year after Operation Sindoor, the Union government has officially recorded the names of the six military personnel who lost their lives during the operation by including them in the Roll of Honour at the National War Memorial (NWM), marking the first official listing of the fatalities from the conflict. The names have also been inscribed on the Tyag Chakra (Circle of Sacrifice) at the memorial in New Delhi. The monument comprises 16 concentric granite walls bearing the names, ranks and units of personnel who have laid down their lives in service since Independence. The six are listed on Wall 3D under the 2025 Roll of Honour. Those named are Subedar Major Pawan Kumar of Headquarters 10 Infantry Brigade, Rifleman Sunil Kumar of 4 Jammu and Kashmir Light Infantry, Lance Naik Dinesh Kumar of 5 Field Regiment, Agniveer Mood Muralinaik of 851 Light Regiment, Havildar Sunil Kumar Singh of 237 Field Workshop Company, and Sergeant Surendra Kumar of No. 39 Wing of the Indian Air Force.

Two of the six were decorated for gallantry. Rifleman Sunil Kumar was posthumously awarded the Vir Chakra, India's third-highest wartime gallantry award, while Sergeant Surendra Kumar was awarded the Vayu Sena Medal. Operation Sindoor was launched in the early hours of May 7 last year, in response to the April 22 terror attack in Pahalgam that killed 26 civilians, most of them tourists. Indian armed forces struck nine terror-linked sites in Pakistan and Pakistan-occupied Kashmir associated with Jaish-e-Mohammad and Lashkar-e-Taiba. The cessation of hostilities took place on May 10 after the Directors General of Military Operations (DGMOs) of India and Pakistan agreed to halt military action. Importantly, the list includes Agniveer Mood Muralinaik of 851 Light Regiment, the only Agniveer to lose his life during Operation Sindoor. Naik was killed in Pakistani shelling in Poonch on May 9, 2025. His death has since become the subject of a legal challenge before the Bombay High Court, where his family has sought parity in pensionary and welfare benefits with the families of regular soldiers. The Centre has maintained that Agniveers are entitled to all benefits prescribed under the Agnipath scheme but not to pensionary benefits available to regular service personnel.

Content: Sakshi, Puttaparthi: Andhra Agniveer Murali Nayak, martyred in 'Operation Sindoor', has become a source of pride for the state. Summary: The names of six Indian soldiers, including five from the Army and one from the Air Force, martyred in 'Operation Sindoor' against Pakistan, have been inscribed on the National War Memorial wall in New Delhi. The operation was launched to avenge a terrorist attack in Pulwama, Jammu and Kashmir, which killed 26 people, and resulted in the destruction of terrorist infrastructure and the killing of over 100 terrorists.
Content: New Delhi, June 26: The names of 6 brave soldiers (Army-5, Air Force-1) who were martyred in 'Operation Sindoor' against Pakistan have been inscribed on the wall of the National War Memorial in Delhi. With this, the names of the 6 soldiers martyred in Operation Sindoor have been released for the first time after a year. In Pulwama, Jammu and Kashmir, on April 22 last year, 26 people, including 25 tourists and one pony rider, were killed in a firing by 3 Lashkar-e-Taiba terrorists. To avenge this attack, the Indian Army launched a military operation named 'Operation Sindoor' on the night of May 6-7 last year, targeting terrorist infrastructure in Pakistan and Pakistan-occupied Kashmir. In this operation, terrorist infrastructures were destroyed, and more than 100 terrorists were killed. Following this, military conflict erupted between the infrastructures. This conflict, which lasted for 4 days, caused severe damage to Pakistani military bases, and the fighting was stopped at Pakistan's request. In this operation, Indian Army personnel who were martyred... The names of Subedar Major Pawan Kumar, Rifleman Sunil Kumar, Lance Naik Dinesh Kumar, Agniveer Murali Nayak, Havildar Sunil Kumar Sik, and Indian Air Force personnel Suresh Kumar have been inscribed on the wall of the National War Memorial in Delhi. The names of the brave soldiers have also been released on the National War Memorial website. This is the first time that the names of soldiers martyred after 'Operation Sindoor' have been released. In the central part of the National War Memorial complex within India Gate in Delhi, there is a majestic stupa with the Amar Jawan Jyoti. On the circular walls surrounding it, the names of martyred soldiers are inscribed. On a wall with the number '3D', the phrase 'Operation Sindoor' and below it the year '2025' are inscribed, and the names of 6 brave soldiers are placed there. Content: Names to be Inscribed on National War Memorial New Delhi: Pudhari News Service After the terrorist attack in Pahalgam on April 22, 2025, India launched 'Operation Sindoor' and took action against terrorist bases in Pakistan and Pakistan-occupied Kashmir. During this operation, the names of six brave soldiers who made the supreme sacrifice for the country have been officially announced for the first time. The names of all these martyrs will now be permanently inscribed at the National War Memorial. Martyrs in 'Operation Sindoor' These Soldiers are Martyrs: - Subedar Major Pawan Kumar: Headquarters, 10th Infantry Brigade - Rifleman Sunil Kumar: 4th Battalion Jammu Kashmir Light Infantry Regiment - Lance Naik Dinesh Kumar: 5th Field Regiment - Agniveer Moodh Murli Nayak: 875th Light Regiment - Havaldar Sunil Kumar Singh: 237th Field Workshop - Sergeant Surendra Kumar: 39th Wing, Indian Air Force The six fallen soldiers include 5 personnel from the Indian Army and one Sergeant from the Indian Air Force. Posthumous Awards for Two Brave Soldiers Among these six martyrs, two soldiers have also been posthumously honored for their unparalleled bravery. Rifleman Sunil Kumar was posthumously awarded the 'Vir Chakra', the country's third-highest wartime gallantry award. He was deployed on the Line of Control during the operation. Additionally, Sergeant Surendra Kumar was posthumously awarded the 'Vayu Padak'. This honor was presented by President Droupadi Murmu at a special ceremony held on June 8.

Content: RAKESH K. SINGH NEW DELHI, JUNE 26 Over a year after Operation Sindoor, the names of six military personnel, five from the Indian Army and one from the IAF who died in the line of duty during the military action against Pakistan last year, have been released. Their names have been inscribed on a wall at the National War Memorial as a tribute to their supreme sacrifice. This is the first time since the military operation conducted by the Indian armed forces in May 2025 that the government has released the names of these six personnel. Operation Sindoor was conducted to avenge the deadly Pahalgam terror attack on April 22 last year. The names of the six personnel, inscribed on wall number '3D' of Tyag Chakra at the National War Memorial, are Subedar Major Pawan Kumar, Rifleman Sunil Kumar, Lance Naik Dinesh Kumar, Agniveer Mood Muralinaik, Havildar Sunil Kumar Singh from the Army, and Indian Air Force Sergeant Surendra Kumar. The unit names of these bravehearts have also been inscribed. Sources said these six names were inscribed recently on the wall. The names have also been published on the website of the National War Memorial. The iconic memorial stands as a solemn tribute to the Indian soldiers who have fallen in the line of duty, defending the nation during wars since Independence. The centrepiece of the memorial, located at the India Gate complex, is an obelisk along with the eternal flame—the Amar Jawan Jyoti—surrounded by concentric circles carrying curved walls, named serially, on which the names of the fallen heroes have been inscribed. On the corner of wall number '3D,' a brick on the top row bears the inscription 'OP SINDOOR', the one below it '2025', followed by the names of the six personnel in a column, on different rows of bricks.

Summary: The Congress party criticized the Central government for a one-year delay in recognizing the sacrifice of six soldiers who died during Operation Sindoor, an operation launched in response to the Pahalgam terror attack. Content: Press Trust of India NEW DELHI The Congress on Friday attacked the Centre for its one-year delay in recognising the sacrifice of six soldiers who laid down their lives during Operation Sindoor. Operation Sindoor was launched in response to the Pahalgam terror attack. Congress leader Pawan Khera said it was a shame that the government that wraps itself in nationalism had denied the heroes the recognition they deserved for a year. In a post on X, he named the six personnel and said they are the brave sons of India who laid down their lives defending India's honour. “Their names should have been etched into the national consciousness. Their families should have seen a grateful nation honouring their sacrifice. Instead, for an entire year, the BJP government chose to conceal their martyrdom from the nation,” Mr. Khera said. “The same government that wraps itself in the flag and speaks endlessly of nationalism denied these heroes the recognition and remembrance they deserved. Such a shame!,” he said.

This information has been uploaded on the official website of 'I Am War Memorial'. The names are visible on the OD Wall, which is part of the 2026 section of the website. Names of other martyrs who sacrificed their lives for the country are also visible there. This is the first time the Centre has released the names of martyrs from that operation. Incidentally, India launched 'Operation Sindoor' in May last year to destroy militant bases on Pakistani soil in response to the indiscriminate killing of common people in Pahalgam, Jammu and Kashmir. Six soldiers of the country were martyred there. While releasing the list of army personnel who sacrificed for the country in 2023, the names of these six armed forces members martyred in Operation Sindoor were released. Their sacrifice received formal public recognition for the first time. Various quarters have praised their sacrifice, paying tribute to the families of the martyred soldiers. Subsequently, Pakistan attacked densely populated areas and army bases in India's border states.

Summary: A 19-year-old girl, Karishma Gautam, died under suspicious circumstances in Salone, Raebareli, leading to allegations of murder. Content: Pioneer Correspondent. Salone, Raebareli The life of 19-year-old Karishma Gautam, who dreamt of mehndi on her hands and sindoor in her hair, ended at a point where she hoped to build a new world. The story, which began amidst promises of marriage, love, and trust, is now entangled in suspicious death and murder allegations. The girl's death has shaken the entire region. Karishma Gautam, a resident of Palhipur village in the Kotwali area, had a love affair with Mithun Patel from the same village. Their relationship had progressed so far that they had left home and gone to Tamil Nadu. Later, the girl approached the police station complaining that her lover was backing out of marriage. The police called both parties and arranged a compromise, where it was decided that they would marry soon. After this, it seemed as if both their lives would get back on track. But fate perhaps had something else in store. According to the police, after the compromise, the young man went to Tamil Nadu. Karishma, after staying at her sister's place for a few days, started living at her lover's aunt's house. On June 24, she returned to her village. There, her health suddenly deteriorated. Her family immediately took her to a private hospital in Salone, but she died during treatment. The deceased's father, Deshraj, has alleged that his daughter was two months pregnant. He claims that her lover and his family were pressuring her to abort the pregnancy. When she resisted, she was allegedly poisoned and killed. He has demanded strict action against five people, including her lover Mithun Patel, his father, aunt, and uncle, on charges of murder. The family also refused to cremate the body. After this, the police persuaded them and sent the body for post-mortem. Kotwal Balendu Gautam says that the cause of death could not be clearly ascertained in the post-mortem report. Therefore, the viscera has been preserved and sent for forensic examination.

Content: The ‘Tyag Chakra’ (Circle of Sacrifice) at the National War Memorial is dedicated to the nation’s bravehearts. The military action killed more than 100 terrorists and inflicted heavy damage at six to seven strategic airbases and allied infrastructure in Pakistan. It retaliated triggering aerial engagements, drone attacks and heavy shelling across the border. The military operation, named “Operation Sindoor”, carried deep symbolic messaging. Heading: Operation Sindoor demonstrated that indigenous defense capabilities are crucial for strategic effectiveness: Murmu
Summary: President Droupadi Murmu emphasized that indigenous defense capabilities are crucial for strategic effectiveness and national self-reliance, citing 'Operation Sindoor' as an example. She highlighted that self-reliant nations are better equipped to maintain economic stability amidst global conflicts and geopolitical tensions. Murmu also stressed the importance of sustainable development, urging the adoption of green technologies and environmentally responsible infrastructure for future generations.
Content: New Delhi/Bhasha. President Droupadi Murmu said on Thursday that a self-reliant nation is more capable of maintaining economic stability, and it was clearly seen during 'Operation Sindoor' that indigenous defense capabilities are important in enhancing a country's operational readiness and strategic effectiveness. Addressing a group of trainee officers of the Military Engineer Services (MES) at Rashtrapati Bhavan, Murmu said that in the current era, when the world is facing various conflicts and geopolitical tensions, self-reliance has become a strategic necessity for nations. She stated that a self-reliant nation is more capable of maintaining its economic stability and advancing its development priorities in times of crisis. The President said, "During 'Operation Sindoor', it was clearly seen how important indigenous defense capabilities, advanced technology, and a strong domestic industrial base are in empowering any nation's operational readiness and strategic effectiveness." 'Operation Sindoor' was conducted by the country's defense forces, targeting terrorist hideouts located in Pakistan and Pakistan-occupied Kashmir (PoK) between May 7 and May 10, 2025. This action was taken in response to the terrorist attack that occurred in Pahalgam, Jammu and Kashmir, on April 22, 2025. The Pahalgam terrorist attack resulted in the death of 26 people, most of whom were tourists. Murmu said that today the world is facing many challenges related to climate change and the environment. She said, "In this situation, sustainable development is no longer an option, but a necessity!" The President urged them to adopt green technologies, save energy and water, and increase green cover. She said, "Infrastructure that is strong, efficient, and environmentally responsible will not only meet today's needs but also protect the interests of future generations."

Heading: What happened? How did it happen?
Summary: This article analyzes recent political events involving Donald Trump, Giorgia Meloni, and Rahul Gandhi, highlighting controversies and their implications. It discusses Trump's past praise for PM Modi, his critical comments about Meloni, and the Italian response, while also examining the Indian Youth Congress's portrayal of Rahul Gandhi as Lord Parshuram, which sparked debate about secularism and religious politics. The author criticizes political parties for using religious symbols and calls for focusing on real national issues.
Content:
Column-Inkwell
Kumkum Chaddha

If there is one question that stands before every discerning person, it is 'What happened... how did it happen? And then what is the problem with these people?' Here, 'these people' refers to two individuals: one is the President of a country, America, and the other is a real leader of a political party in India. Their names are Donald Trump and Rahul Gandhi. Let's start with the US President Donald Trump. He openly praised Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi, signaling a softening of relations. These were the same relations that had soured the previous year when Trump imposed heavy tariffs on India. That year, Trump's visit to India was proposed, but due to increasing tensions, the visit was canceled.

Apart from tariffs, many other issues also increased tensions. These included the war between India and Pakistan after Operation Sindoor, the credit for stopping which Trump took for himself. India had no third-party involvement in this war, so Trump was displeased, and US-India relations deteriorated further. In addition, Brazil and China's growing proximity to India also affected the warmth in relations, which sometimes appeared between Trump and Modi.

It is difficult to say this, but Trump's comment cannot be justified in any way. Rather, it should be criticized. Italy responded to this, and Meloni hit back at Trump. She released a video on social media saying, "Donald Trump's statements are completely false. I am truly surprised. I don't understand why the President of America behaves this way with his allies, and this is not the first time. She further said that one thing should be remembered: I never begged, nor did Italy ever ask for anything. The Meloni government went a step further. Italian Foreign Minister Antonio Tajani expressed government anger over Trump's comments and canceled his proposed visit to America. In other words, even if Meloni wanted to take a picture with Trump, how can a head of government use such insulting language? If he likes to consider himself all-powerful, then should he have the right to get others at a price? Is it not below the dignity of a political advantage or a comeback like Trump often does?

Should the President of the world's most powerful country not choose his words carefully? Is it appropriate for a leader like Trump to make personal comments and insult other world leaders? Its answer is just one word, and that too in capital letters: NO. A similar drama is unfolding in India, which, if seen according to the sentiments of devotees, is also an insult to deities.

Congress President Rahul Gandhi's 56th birthday was celebrated. Naturally, preparations were made for the celebration. But Congress workers gave this occasion a different direction and tried to give a religious identity to a leader who calls himself secular. Youth Congress leaders put up a picture of Gandhi and offered milk, and going further, Rahul Gandhi was depicted as Lord Parshuram, holding an axe in one hand and the Constitution in the other.

This means religion and politics were combined. For the record, Parshuram is considered an incarnation of Lord Vishnu and is described as a sage, warrior, and scholar. He received his axe from Lord Shiva and was famous for his knowledge of weapons and scriptures. In the Mahabharata, he taught Bhishma, Drona, and Karna, and it is said that he taught many warriors with his weapons and scriptures. From a political perspective, in the 2024 general elections, Rahul Gandhi made the Indian Constitution a major issue. He alleged that if the BJP comes to power, it will try to change and rewrite the Constitution.

This created a widespread impact as a political message, as Gandhi often talks about the Constitution, which has a small following, keeping it everywhere. Despite BJP's claim of '400 seats', they did not get a clear majority in the Lok Sabha. But despite all this, political swords have been drawn. There has been a huge controversy over presenting Rahul Gandhi as a deity.

BJP leader Shahzad Poonawalla alleged that Congress 'insulted Hindu faith'. He wrote on social media that 'insulting Hindus and getting votes' is their politics. He also demanded that Congress apologize for hurting the sentiments of crores of Hindus. Other BJP leaders also accused Congress of insulting Lord Parshuram. Apart from all this, what was done by an experienced political party like Congress is completely inappropriate.

Today, the situation is that Hindus and Muslims live together in India, but sometimes it happens that both communities are pitted against each other. This is a big issue, which Rahul Gandhi often talks about. Remember his 'shop of love' slogan, which was quite popular. Now the question arises, when his own party is presenting him as a deity and religious rituals are being performed, then should Rahul Gandhi not condemn such acts? Or should his party workers follow the path of BJP's religion-based politics? The demand is that leaders should rise above political symbols and present a constructive agenda before the country. Instead of wasting time and energy, they should focus on the country's real issues and the direction of the future.

Content: NEW DELHI, JUNE 25 India has officially made public the names of six martyrs who laid down their lives during Operation Sindoor against Pakistan in May last year. Two of the bravehearts are gallantry awardees, having received a Vir Chakra and a Vayu Medal. The names of the five Army soldiers and their regimental affiliations along with the lone Indian Air Force warrior and his squadron have been put up on the web-site of the National War Memorial in New Delhi. Each of the six names will be engraved on a special brick. The six martyrs are Sub Maj Pawan Kumar from the Headquarters 10 Infantry Brigade; Rifleman Sunil Kumar from the 4th battalion of the Jammu and Kashmir Light Infantry Regiment; Lance Naik Dinesh Kumar from the 5 Field Regiment; Agniveer Mood Murali Naik from the 851 Light Regiment; Havildar Sunil Kumar Singh from the 237 Filed Workshop; and Sergeant Surendra Kumar from the 39 Wing of the Air Force. Rifleman Sunil Kumar has been awarded the Vir Chakra, the country's third-highest battle honour, and Sergeant Surinder Kumar the Vayu Medal. Most of the six casualties have been in Jammu and Kashmir. Sources said Sunil Kumar was posted along the Line of Control with Pakistan. On June 8, President Droupadi Murmu presented the Vir Chakra (posthumous) to Sunil Kumar at the Defence Investiture Ceremony. The award was received by his mother Sudesh Kumari and father Yash Paul. The names of the Operation Sindoor bravehearts have been made public along with the list of all those soldiers who had lost their lives in 2025 in various operations. Each brick bears the name, rank and regiment of a fallen martyr who made the supreme sacrifice since Independence.
